```ruby
# sms_sender.rb
require 'httparty'
require 'json'
require 'dotenv/load'

class MobizonSMS
  include HTTParty
  base_uri 'https://api.mobizon.com'

  def initialize(api_key:, sender_name: nil)
    @api_key = api_key
    @sender_name = sender_name
    @headers = {
      'Content-Type' => 'application/json',
      'Accept' => 'application/json'
    }
  end

  def send_sms(recipients, message)
    # Validate input
    raise ArgumentError, 'Recipients cannot be empty' if recipients.nil? || recipients.empty?
    raise ArgumentError, 'Message cannot be empty' if message.nil? || message.empty?

    # Prepare recipients
    recipients_array = recipients.is_a?(Array) ? recipients : [recipients]
    
    # Validate phone numbers (basic Ukrainian format validation)
    recipients_array.each do |phone|
      unless phone.match?(/\A380\d{9}\z/) || phone.match?(/\A\d{10}\z/) || phone.match?(/\A\d{12}\z/)
        puts "Warning: Phone number #{phone} might not be in valid Ukrainian format (should be 380XXXXXXXXX)"
      end
    end

    # Prepare request payload
    payload = {
      api_key: @api_key,
      recipient: recipients_array.join(','),
      text: message,
      sender: @sender_name
    }.reject { |_, v| v.nil? || v.empty? }

    # Make API request
    response = self.class.post('/service/message/sendsms', 
                              headers: @headers,
                              body: payload.to_json)

    handle_response(response)
  end

  def send_sms_batch(recipients_messages)
    # Validate input
    raise ArgumentError, 'Recipients-messages cannot be empty' if recipients_messages.nil? || recipients_messages.empty?
    
    # Prepare batch payload
    batch_items = recipients_messages.map do |item|
      {
        recipient: item[:recipient],
        text: item[:message],
        sender: item[:sender] || @sender_name
      }
    end

    payload = {
      api_key: @api_key,
      batch: batch_items
    }

    # Make API request
    response = self.class.post('/service/message/sendbatch', 
                              headers: @headers,
                              body: payload.to_json)

    handle_response(response)
  end

  def get_balance
    response = self.class.get('/service/user/getbalance', 
                             headers: @headers,
                             query: { api_key: @api_key })

    handle_response(response)
  end

  private

  def handle_response(response)
    case response.code
    when 200
      begin
        result = JSON.parse(response.body)
        if result['success']
          result
        else
          raise "API Error: #{result['message']}"
        end
      rescue JSON::ParserError
        raise "Invalid API response: #{response.body}"
      end
    when 401
      raise "Authentication failed: Invalid API key"
    when 403
      raise "Access denied: Insufficient permissions"
    when 429
      raise "Rate limit exceeded"
    else
      raise "HTTP Error #{response.code}: #{response.body}"
    end
  end
end

require 'pdf/reader'
require 'csv'
require 'nokogiri'

class PDFExtractor
  def initialize(pdf_path)
    @pdf_path = pdf_path
  end

  def extract_text
    text = ""
    PDF::Reader.open(@pdf_path) do |reader|
      reader.pages.each do |page|
        text += page.text
      end
    end
    text
  end

  def extract_tables
    tables = []
    PDF::Reader.open(@pdf_path) do |reader|
      reader.pages.each_with_index do |page, index|
        # Простий підхід: шукаємо таблиці через розділення пробілами
        lines = page.text.split("\n")
        table = []
        lines.each do |line|
          # Якщо рядок містить багато пробілів або розділювачів (приклад)
          if line.strip.length > 0
            row = line.split(/\s{2,}/) # Розділяємо за двома або більше пробілами
            table << row if row.length > 1
          end
        end
        tables << { page: index + 1, data: table } unless table.empty?
      end
    end
    tables
  end

  def save_tables_to_csv(output_dir = "./tables")
    Dir.mkdir(output_dir) unless Dir.exist?(output_dir)

    tables = extract_tables
    tables.each do |table_data|
      filename = File.join(output_dir, "table_page_#{table_data[:page]}.csv")
      CSV.open(filename, "w") do |csv|
        table_data[:data].each { |row| csv << row }
      end
    end
  end
end

# Приклад використання
pdf_path = "example.pdf"
extractor = PDFExtractor.new(pdf_path)

# Витягти текст
puts "=== Текст із PDF ==="
puts extractor.extract_text

# Витягти таблиці і зберегти у CSV
puts "\n=== Таблиці ==="
extractor.save_tables_to_csv("./output_tables")
```

---

### 🔍 Пояснення:

- `PDF::Reader` — дозволяє читати PDF, витягуючи текст.
- `extract_tables` — спроба розпізнати таблиці за розділенням пробілами, що працює не завжди, але для простих таблиць достатньо.
- `save_tables_to_csv` — зберігає кожну таблицю у окремий CSV-файл.

# spell_checker.rb
require 'hunspell'
require 'active_support/core_ext/string/inflections'
require 'down'
require 'json'

class SpellChecker
  def initialize(dictionary_path = nil)
    @dictionary_path = dictionary_path || find_dictionary
    @hunspell = Hunspell.new(@dictionary_path)
  end

  def check_text(text)
    words = extract_words(text)
    results = []

    words.each do |word|
      is_correct = @hunspell.spell?(word)
      suggestions = is_correct ? [] : @hunspell.suggest(word)
      
      results << {
        word: word,
        correct: is_correct,
        suggestions: suggestions
      }
    end

    results
  end

  def check_and_correct(text)
    results = check_text(text)
    corrected_text = text.dup
    
    # Replace misspelled words with first suggestion or keep original
    results.each do |result|
      if !result[:correct] && !result[:suggestions].empty?
        # Replace first occurrence of the misspelled word
        corrected_text.gsub!(result[:word], result[:suggestions].first)
      end
    end
    
    {
      original: text,
      corrected: corrected_text,
      issues: results
    }
  end

  private

  def extract_words(text)
    # Extract words (alphanumeric characters and apostrophes)
    text.scan(/[a-zA-Z]+(?:'[a-zA-Z]+)*/).map(&:downcase)
  end

  def find_dictionary
    # Try to find dictionary file in common locations
    dict_paths = [
      '/usr/share/hunspell/en_US.dic',
      '/usr/share/myspell/dicts/en_US.dic',
      '/usr/share/dict/words',
      './en_US.dic'
    ]

    dict_paths.find { |path| File.exist?(path) } || raise("No dictionary file found")
  end
end

# Alternative implementation using a more accessible approach
class SimpleSpellChecker
  def initialize
    # Create a basic word list for demonstration
    @common_words = load_common_words
  end

  def check_text(text)
    words = extract_words(text)
    results = []

    words.each do |word|
      is_correct = @common_words.include?(word.downcase)
      suggestions = is_correct ? [] : suggest_corrections(word)
      
      results << {
        word: word,
        correct: is_correct,
        suggestions: suggestions
      }
    end

    results
  end

  def check_and_correct(text)
    results = check_text(text)
    corrected_text = text.dup
    
    results.each do |result|
      if !result[:correct] && !result[:suggestions].empty?
        corrected_text.gsub!(result[:word], result[:suggestions].first)
      end
    end
    
    {
      original: text,
      corrected: corrected_text,
      issues: results
    }
  end

  private

  def extract_words(text)
    text.scan(/[a-zA-Z]+(?:'[a-zA-Z]+)*/).map(&:downcase)
  end

  def load_common_words
    # This would load a comprehensive word list
    # For demo purposes, using a small sample
    %w[
      the be to of and a in that have i it for not on with he as you do at
      this but his by from they we say her she or an will my one all would
      there their what so up out if about who get which go me when make can
      like time no just him know take people into year your good some could
      them see other than then now look only come its over think also back
      after use two how our work first well way even new want because any
      these give day most us
    ]
  end

  def suggest_corrections(word)
    # Simple edit distance algorithm for demonstration
    # In a real implementation, you'd use a more sophisticated approach
    suggestions = []
    
    @common_words.each do |dict_word|
      if edit_distance(word.downcase, dict_word) <= 2
        suggestions << dict_word
      end
    end
    
    suggestions.uniq.sort.first(5)
  end

  def edit_distance(str1, str2)
    # Calculate Levenshtein distance
    m = str1.length
    n = str2.length
    
    return n if m == 0
    return m if n == 0
    
    dp = Array.new(m + 1) { Array.new(n + 1, 0) }
    
    (0..m).each { |i| dp[i][0] = i }
    (0..n).each { |j| dp[0][j] = j }
    
    (1..m).each do |i|
      (1..n).each do |j|
        cost = str1[i-1] == str2[j-1] ? 0 : 1
        dp[i][j] = [
          dp[i-1][j] + 1,      # deletion
          dp[i][j-1] + 1,      # insertion
          dp[i-1][j-1] + cost  # substitution
        ].min
      end
    end
    
    dp[m][n]
  end
end

require 'active_support'
require 'active_support/core_ext/string/inflections'
require 'nokogiri'

class SlugGenerator
  def self.generate(title)
    return '' if title.nil? || title.strip.empty?
    
    # Convert accented characters to ASCII equivalents
    slug = title.to_ascii
    
    # Remove HTML tags if present
    slug = Nokogiri::HTML::DocumentFragment.parse(slug).text
    
    # Replace non-alphanumeric characters with hyphens
    slug = slug.gsub(/[^a-zA-Z0-9\s]/, '-')
    
    # Convert spaces to hyphens
    slug = slug.gsub(/\s+/, '-')
    
    # Remove leading/trailing hyphens
    slug = slug.strip('-')
    
    # Convert to lowercase
    slug = slug.downcase
    
    # Remove multiple consecutive hyphens
    slug = slug.gsub(/-+/, '-')
    
    # Limit length to 50 characters
    slug = slug[0..49]
    
    # Remove trailing hyphen if present
    slug = slug.chomp('-')
    
    slug
  end
  
  # Alternative method with more control over accent handling
  def self.generate_advanced(title)
    return '' if title.nil? || title.strip.empty?

```ruby
require 'httparty'
require 'json'
require 'logger'
require 'securerandom'

class DiiaPushNotifier
  include HTTParty

  # Configure HTTParty
  default_timeout 30
  headers 'Content-Type' => 'application/json'
  headers 'Accept' => 'application/json'

  def initialize(api_key:, base_url:, logger: nil)
    @api_key = api_key
    @base_url = base_url
    @logger = logger || Logger.new(STDOUT)
    @logger.level = Logger::INFO
  end

  # Send push notification to a single user
  def send_notification(recipient_id, title, body, data = {}, options = {})
    payload = build_notification_payload(
      recipient_id: recipient_id,
      title: title,
      body: body,
      data: data,
      options: options
    )

    response = perform_request('/notifications', payload)
    
    if response.success?
      @logger.info("Notification sent successfully to user #{recipient_id}")
      {
        success: true,
        notification_id: response['notification_id'],
        response: response
      }
    else
      @logger.error("Failed to send notification to user #{recipient_id}: #{response['error']}")
      {
        success: false,
        error: response['error'],
        response: response
      }
    end
  end

  # Send push notification to multiple users
  def send_bulk_notifications(recipient_ids, title, body, data = {}, options = {})
    results = []
    
    recipient_ids.each do |recipient_id|
      result = send_notification(recipient_id, title, body, data, options)
      results << {
        recipient_id: recipient_id,
        result: result
      }
    end
    
    results
  end

  # Send notification with device tokens directly
  def send_notification_by_tokens(tokens, title, body, data = {}, options = {})
    payload = build_notification_payload(
      tokens: tokens,
      title: title,
      body: body,
      data: data,
      options: options
    )

    response = perform_request('/notifications/bulk', payload)
    
    if response.success?
      @logger.info("Bulk notification sent successfully to #{tokens.length} devices")
      {
        success: true,
        notification_id: response['notification_id'],
        response: response
      }
    else
      @logger.error("Failed to send bulk notification: #{response['error']}")
      {
        success: false,
        error: response['error'],
        response: response
      }
    end
  end

  # Get notification status
  def get_notification_status(notification_id)
    response = perform_request("/notifications/#{notification_id}", nil, :get)
    
    if response.success?
      {
        success: true,
        status: response
      }
    else
      {
        success: false,
        error: response['error']
      }
    end
  end

  private

  def build_notification_payload(recipient_id: nil, tokens: nil, title:, body:, data: {}, options: {})
    payload = {
      title: title,
      body: body,
      data: data
    }

    # Add recipient identifiers
    if recipient_id
      payload[:recipient_id] = recipient_id
    elsif tokens && tokens.is_a?(Array)
      payload[:device_tokens] = tokens
    end

    # Add optional parameters
    payload[:priority] = options[:priority] || 'normal'
    payload[:ttl] = options[:ttl] || 86400 # 24 hours default
    payload[:badge] = options[:badge] if options[:badge]
    payload[:sound] = options[:sound] || 'default'
    payload[:category] = options[:category] if options[:category]

    payload
  end

  def perform_request(endpoint, payload, method = :post)
    url = "#{@base_url}#{endpoint}"
    
    options = {
      headers: {
        'Authorization' => "Bearer #{@api_key}",
        'X-Request-ID' => SecureRandom.uuid
      }
    }

    if payload
      options[:body] = payload.to_json
    end

    begin
      response = case method
                 when :post
                   self.class.post(url, options)
                 when :get
                   self.class.get(url, options)
                 else
                   self.class.post(url, options)
                 end

      # Handle different response formats
      if response.code == 200 || response.code == 201
        JSON.parse(response.body)
      else
        {
          'error' => "HTTP #{response.code}: #{response.message}",
          'details' => response.body
        }
      end
    rescue => e
      @logger.error("API request failed: #{e.message}")
      {
        'error' => "Request failed: #{e.message}"
      }
    end
  end
end

```ruby
# number_to_words.rb
class NumberToWords
  ONES = [
    '', 'one', 'two', 'three', 'four', 'five', 'six', 'seven', 'eight', 'nine',
    'ten', 'eleven', 'twelve', 'thirteen', 'fourteen', 'fifteen', 'sixteen',
    'seventeen', 'eighteen', 'nineteen'
  ].freeze

  TENS = [
    '', '', 'twenty', 'thirty', 'forty', 'fifty', 'sixty', 'seventy', 'eighty', 'ninety'
  ].freeze

  SCALES = [
    '', 'thousand', 'million', 'billion', 'trillion', 'quadrillion', 'quintillion'
  ].freeze

  def self.convert(number)
    return 'zero' if number == 0
    
    result = []
    scale_index = 0
    
    while number > 0
      chunk = number % 1000
      if chunk != 0
        chunk_words = convert_chunk(chunk)
        if scale_index > 0
          chunk_words += " #{SCALES[scale_index]}"
        end
        result.unshift(chunk_words)
      end
      number /= 1000
      scale_index += 1
    end
    
    result.join(' ')
  end

  private_class_method def self.convert_chunk(number)
    result = []
    
    # Handle hundreds place
    if number >= 100
      result << ONES[number / 100]
      result << 'hundred'
      number %= 100
    end
    
    # Handle tens and ones place
    if number >= 20
      tens_digit = number / 10
      ones_digit = number % 10
      result << TENS[tens_digit]
      result << ONES[ones_digit] if ones_digit > 0
    elsif number > 0
      result << ONES[number]
    end
    
    result.join(' ')
  end
end

# Example usage
if __FILE__ == $0
  puts NumberToWords.convert(1234)      # => "one thousand two hundred thirty-four"
  puts NumberToWords.convert(0)         # => "zero"
  puts NumberToWords.convert(1000)      # => "one thousand"
  puts NumberToWords.convert(1001)      # => "one thousand one"
  puts NumberToWords.convert(1234567)   # => "one million two hundred thirty-four thousand five hundred sixty-seven"
end
```

This implementation:

1. Handles numbers from 0 up to very large numbers (limited by Ruby's integer size)
2. Properly formats compound numbers like "twenty-one"

4. Handles edge cases like zero and numbers ending in zero
5. Uses a clean, modular approach with private helper methods
6. Includes proper English word formatting (e.g., "one thousand two hundred thirty-four")

The code works by:

- Converting each chunk to words using helper methods

## 🧠 2. `lib/deepl_translator.rb`

```ruby
require 'deepl'
require 'redis'
require 'digest'

class DeepLTranslator
  def initialize(auth_key:, cache_ttl: 3600)
    @translator = DeepL::Translator.new(auth_key)
    @redis = Redis.new
    @cache_ttl = cache_ttl
  end

  def translate(text, target_lang = 'UK')
    # Створюємо унікальний ключ для кешу
    cache_key = "deepl:#{target_lang}:#{Digest::MD5.hexdigest(text)}"

    # Спробуємо отримати з кешу
    cached = @redis.get(cache_key)
    return cached if cached

    # Якщо немає в кеші — перекладаємо
    result = @translator.translate(text, target_lang: target_lang)
    translated_text = result.text

    # Зберігаємо у кеш
    @redis.setex(cache_key, @cache_ttl, translated_text)

    translated_text
  end
end
```

class NumberToWords
  ONES = %w[zero one two three four five six seven eight nine
            ten eleven twelve thirteen fourteen fifteen sixteen
            seventeen eighteen nineteen].freeze

  TENS = %w[zero ten twenty thirty forty fifty sixty seventy eighty ninety].freeze

  THOUSANDS = %w[thousand million billion trillion].freeze

  def self.convert(number)
    return "zero" if number == 0

    words = []

    while number > 0
      chunk = number % 1000
      if chunk != 0
        chunk_words = convert_chunk(chunk)

        words.unshift(chunk_words)

      scale += 1
    end

    if number >= 100
      result << ONES[number / 100]
      result << "hundred"
      number %= 100
    end

    if number >= 20
      tens = TENS[number / 10]
      ones = ONES[number % 10]
      result << tens
      result << ones if ones != "zero"
    elsif number > 0
      result << ONES[number]
    end

    result.join(" ")
  end
end

require 'fuzzy_match'
require 'jaro_winkler'

class CompanyMatcher
  def initialize(companies)
    @companies = companies
  end

  # Пошук збігів за відстанню Левенштейна
  def levenshtein_matches(query, threshold = 0.8)
    matches = []

    @companies.each do |company|
      similarity = FuzzyMatch.similarity(query, company)
      matches << [company, similarity] if similarity >= threshold
    end

    matches.sort_by { |_, sim| -sim }
  end

  # Пошук збігів за відстанню Джаро-Вінклера
  def jaro_winkler_matches(query, threshold = 0.8)
    matches = []

    @companies.each do |company|
      similarity = JaroWinkler.distance(query.downcase, company.downcase)
      matches << [company, similarity] if similarity >= threshold
    end

    matches.sort_by { |_, sim| -sim }
  end
end

# Приклад використання

companies = [
  "Apple Inc.",
  "Microsoft Corporation",
  "Google LLC",
  "Amazon.com Inc.",
  "Tesla Inc.",
  "SpaceX",
  "Meta Platforms Inc.",
  "Netflix Inc."
]

matcher = CompanyMatcher.new(companies)

query = "Appel Inc"
puts "Збіги за відстанню Левенштейна для '#{query}':"
puts matcher.levenshtein_matches(query, 0.7).map { |name, sim| "#{name} (схожість: #{sim.round(2)})" }

puts "\nЗбіги за Джаро-Вінклера для '#{query}':"
puts matcher.jaro_winkler_matches(query, 0.8).map { |name, sim| "#{name} (схожість: #{sim.round(2)})" }
```

    case diff

    when 60..3599

      "#{(diff / 3600).floor} hours ago"
    when 86400..2591999
      "#{(diff / 86400).floor} days ago"
    when 2592000..31535999
      "#{(diff / 2592000).floor} months ago"
    else
      "#{(diff / 31536000).floor} years ago"
    end
  end

I'll create a Ruby solution that extracts text and tables from PDF files using the `pdf-reader` gem and `roo` gem for table extraction.

## Gemfile

```

## Implementation

```ruby
#!/usr/bin/env ruby

require 'pdf-reader'
require 'roo'
require 'csv'
require 'nokogiri'
require 'fileutils'
require 'pathname'

class PDFExtractor
  def initialize(pdf_path)
    @pdf_path = pdf_path
    @reader = PDF::Reader.new(pdf_path)
  end

  # Extract text from PDF
  def extract_text
    text = ""
    @reader.pages.each do |page|
      text += page.text + "\n"
    end
    text
  end

  # Extract tables from PDF (basic implementation)
  def extract_tables
    tables = []
    
    # Use Nokogiri to parse PDF content
    # This is a simplified approach - real PDF table extraction is complex
    content = extract_text
    
    # Find potential tables (simple heuristics)
    lines = content.split("\n")
    current_table = []
    in_table = false
    
    lines.each do |line|
      # Check if line looks like a table row (has multiple columns)
      if line.strip.length > 0 && line.include?("\t") || line.split("  ").length > 3
        if !in_table
          in_table = true
          current_table = []
        end
        current_table << line.strip
      else
        if in_table
          if current_table.length > 1
            tables << current_table
          end
          in_table = false
        end
      end
    end
    
    # Add last table if it exists
    if in_table && current_table.length > 1
      tables << current_table
    end
    
    tables
  end

  # Extract all text and tables from PDF
  def extract_all
    {
      text: extract_text,
      tables: extract_tables
    }
  end

  # Save extracted text to file
  def save_text_to_file(filename = nil)
    filename ||= "extracted_text_#{File.basename(@pdf_path, '.pdf')}.txt"
    File.write(filename, extract_text)
    puts "Text saved to #{filename}"
    filename
  end

  # Save extracted tables to CSV files
  def save_tables_to_csv(prefix = "table")
    tables = extract_tables
    saved_files = []
    
    tables.each_with_index do |table, index|
      filename = "#{prefix}_#{index + 1}.csv"
      CSV.open(filename, 'w') do |csv|
        table.each do |row|
          # Parse the row (assuming tab-separated or space-separated)
          if row.include?("\t")
            csv << row.split("\t")
          elsif row.include?("  ")
            csv << row.split("  ").map(&:strip)
          else
            csv << [row]
          end
        end
      end
      puts "Table saved to #{filename}"
      saved_files << filename
    end
    
    saved_files
  end

  # Save extracted content to structured format
  def save_structured_output(output_dir = "extracted_output")
    FileUtils.mkdir_p(output_dir)
    
    # Save text
    text_file = File.join(output_dir, "text.txt")
    File.write(text_file, extract_text)
    
    # Save tables
    tables = extract_tables
    tables.each_with_index do |table, index|
      csv_file = File.join(output_dir, "table_#{index + 1}.csv")
      CSV.open(csv_file, 'w') do |csv|
        table.each do |row|
          if row.include?("\t")
            csv << row.split("\t")
          elsif row.include?("  ")
            csv << row.split("  ").map(&:strip)
          else
            csv << [row]
          end
        end
      end
    end
    
    puts "Structured output saved to #{output_dir}"
    output_dir
  end
end

# Main script to demonstrate functionality
class PDFExtractorCLI
  def self.run
    puts "PDF Text and Table Extractor"
    puts "=" * 30
    
    # Get PDF file from user or command line
    pdf_file = ARGV[0] || get_pdf_file_from_user
    
    if pdf_file.nil? || !File.exist?(pdf_file)
      puts "Error: PDF file not found or invalid path"
      return
    end
    
    puts "Processing: #{pdf_file}"
    
    # Create extractor
    extractor = PDFExtractor.new(pdf_file)
    
    # Extract content
    puts "\nExtracting content..."
    content = extractor.extract_all
    
    # Display results
    puts "\n" + "=" * 30
    puts "EXTRACTED TEXT:"
    puts "=" * 30
    puts content[:text].first(500) + "..." if content[:text].length > 500
    puts content[:text] if content[:text].length <= 500
    
    puts "\n" + "=" * 30
    puts "EXTRACTED TABLES:"
    puts "=" * 30
    
    if content[:tables].empty?
      puts "No tables found in the PDF"
    else
      content[:tables].each_with_index do |table, index|
        puts "\nTable #{index + 1}:"
        table.each do |row|
          puts "  #{row}"
        end
      end
    end
    
    # Save outputs
    puts "\n" + "=" * 30
    puts "SAVING OUTPUTS:"
    puts "=" * 30
    
    # Save text file
    extractor.save_text_to_file
    
    # Save tables to CSV
    saved_tables = extractor.save_tables_to_csv
    
    # Save structured output
    extractor.save_structured_output
    
    puts "\nExtraction complete!"
    puts "Files created:"
    puts "  - extracted_text_#{File.basename(pdf_file, '.pdf')}.txt"
    saved_tables.each { |file| puts "  - #{file}" }
    puts "  - extracted_output/ directory"
  end
  
  private
  
  def self.get_pdf_file_from_user
    print "Enter the path to the PDF file: "
    input = gets.chomp
    input.empty? ? nil : input
  end
end

# Example usage
if __FILE__ == $0
  PDFExtractorCLI.run
end
```

require 'addressable/uri'

class USAddressNormalizer
  # Регулярний вираз для пошуку поштових адрес США
  ADDRESS_PATTERN = %r{
    \b
    (?<street>\d+\s+[A-Za-z0-9\s]+?(?:St|Street|Ave|Avenue|Rd|Road|Dr|Drive|Ln|Lane|Ct|Court|Pl|Place|Pkwy|Parkway|Cir|Circle|Way|Trail|Blvd|Boulevard|Terrace|Terr|Loop|Highway|Hwy|Court|Circle|Way|Lane|Pl|Place|Dr|Drive|Ave|Avenue|St|Street)?)
    ,?\s+
    (?<city>[A-Za-z\s]+?)
    ,?\s+
    (?<state>[A-Z]{2})
    \s+
    (?<zip>\d{5}(?:-\d{4})?)
    \b
  }x

  def self.normalize(text)
    addresses = []

    text.scan(ADDRESS_PATTERN) do |match|
      street = match[0].strip
      city = match[1].strip
      state = match[2].strip
      zip = match[3].strip

      # Нормалізація
      normalized = {
        street: street,
        city: city.titleize,
        state: state.upcase,
        zip: zip
      }

      addresses << normalized
    end

    addresses
  end
end

require 'levenshtein'

class CompanyFuzzyMatcher
  def initialize(companies)
    @companies = companies
  end

  # Find fuzzy matches using Levenshtein distance
  def find_levenshtein_matches(target_company, threshold = 0.8)
    matches = []
    
    @companies.each do |company|
      next if company == target_company
      
      distance = Levenshtein.distance(target_company, company)
      max_length = [target_company.length, company.length].max
      similarity = max_length.zero? ? 1.0 : 1.0 - (distance.to_f / max_length)
      
      if similarity >= threshold
        matches << {
          company: company,
          similarity: similarity,
          distance: distance
        }
      end
    end
    
    matches.sort_by { |m| -m[:similarity] }
  end

  # Find fuzzy matches using Jaro-Winkler distance
  def find_jaro_winkler_matches(target_company, threshold = 0.8)
    matches = []
    
    @companies.each do |company|
      next if company == target_company
      
      similarity = JaroWinkler.distance(target_company, company)
      
      if similarity >= threshold
        matches << {
          company: company,
          similarity: similarity
        }
      end
    end
    
    matches.sort_by { |m| -m[:similarity] }
  end

  # Find matches using both methods
  def find_both_matches(target_company, levenshtein_threshold = 0.8, jaro_threshold = 0.8)
    levenshtein_matches = find_levenshtein_matches(target_company, levenshtein_threshold)
    jaro_matches = find_jaro_winkler_matches(target_company, jaro_threshold)
    
    # Combine results and remove duplicates
    all_matches = levenshtein_matches + jaro_matches
    
    # Remove duplicates based on company name
    unique_matches = all_matches.uniq { |match| match[:company] }
    
    # Sort by combined similarity score (weighted average)
    unique_matches.sort_by do |match|
      if match[:distance]
        # For Levenshtein matches, use similarity score
        -match[:similarity]
      else
        # For Jaro-Winkler matches, use similarity score
        -match[:similarity]
      end
    end
  end

  # Get company names with similarity scores
  def get_all_similarities(target_company, method = :jaro_winkler)
    case method
    when :levenshtein
      find_levenshtein_matches(target_company)
    when :jaro_winkler
      find_jaro_winkler_matches(target_company)
    else
      raise ArgumentError, "Method must be :levenshtein or :jaro_winkler"
    end
  end
end

```ruby
# lib/translation_service.rb
require 'deepl'
require 'redis'
require 'logger'
require 'json'
require 'dotenv/load'

class TranslationService
  def initialize
    @deep_l = DeepL::Client.new(ENV['DEEPL_AUTH_KEY'])
    @redis = Redis.new(url: ENV['REDIS_URL'] || 'redis://localhost:6379/0')
    @logger = Logger.new(STDOUT)
    @logger.level = Logger::INFO
  end

  # Translate a product description
  def translate_description(description, target_language, source_language: 'EN')
    # Create cache key
    cache_key = "translation:#{source_language}:#{target_language}:#{description.hash}"
    
    # Check if translation is already cached
    cached_translation = @redis.get(cache_key)
    if cached_translation
      @logger.info("Using cached translation for: #{description[0..50]}...")
      return JSON.parse(cached_translation)
    end
    
    # Perform translation
    begin
      translation = @deep_l.translate(
        description,
        source_lang: source_language,
        target_lang: target_language
      )
      
      # Cache the result
      @redis.setex(cache_key, 86400, JSON.dump(translation)) # Cache for 24 hours
      @logger.info("Translated: #{description[0..50]}... -> #{translation.text[0..50]}...")
      
      translation
    rescue DeepL::Error => e
      @logger.error("Translation error: #{e.message}")
      raise
    end
  end

  # Translate multiple descriptions efficiently
  def translate_descriptions(descriptions, target_language, source_language: 'EN')
    translations = []
    
    descriptions.each do |description|
      translations << translate_description(description, target_language, source_language: source_language)
    end
    
    translations
  end

  # Clear translation cache for a specific description
  def clear_cache(description, target_language, source_language: 'EN')
    cache_key = "translation:#{source_language}:#{target_language}:#{description.hash}"
    @redis.del(cache_key)
    @logger.info("Cleared cache for: #{description[0..50]}...")
  end

  # Get cache statistics
  def cache_stats
    # This is a simplified approach - in a real app, you'd want more detailed stats
    @redis.info['keyspace_hits'].to_i
  end
end
```

```ruby
# lib/product_translator.rb
require_relative 'translation_service'
require 'logger'

class ProductTranslator
  def initialize
    @translation_service = TranslationService.new
    @logger = Logger.new(STDOUT)
    @logger.level = Logger::INFO
  end

  # Translate a single product description
  def translate_product(product_name, description, target_language, source_language: 'EN')
    translation = @translation_service.translate_description(
      description, 
      target_language, 
      source_language: source_language
    )
    
    {
      product_name: product_name,
      original_description: description,
      translated_description: translation.text,
      target_language: target_language,
      source_language: source_language,
      translation_time: Time.now
    }
  end

  # Translate multiple products
  def translate_products(products, target_language, source_language: 'EN')
    results = []
    
    products.each do |product|
      begin
        result = translate_product(
          product[:name], 
          product[:description], 
          target_language, 
          source_language: source_language
        )
        results << result
      rescue => e
        @logger.error("Failed to translate product: #{product[:name]} - #{e.message}")
        results << {
          product_name: product[:name],
          error: e.message,
          translation_time: Time.now
        }
      end
    end
    
    results
  end

  # Export translated products to JSON
  def export_translations(translations, filename)
    File.open(filename, 'w') do |file|
      file.write(JSON.pretty_generate(translations))
    end
    @logger.info("Exported #{translations.length} translations to #{filename}")
  end
end

1. **Gemfile** — для встановлення необхідних бібліотек.
2. **Код на Ruby** — основна логіка обчислення Flesch Reading Ease.

## ✅ 1. Gemfile

## ✅ 2. Код на Ruby

```ruby
class FleschReadingEase
  def initialize(text)
    @text = text
  end

  def score
    return 0 if @text.nil? || @text.strip.empty?

    sentences = @text.split(/[.!?]+/).reject(&:empty?)
    words = @text.split(/\s+/).reject(&:empty?)
    syllables = words.sum { |word| count_syllables(word) }

    return 0 if sentences.empty? || words.empty?

    # Формула Flesch Reading Ease
    # 206.835 - (1.015 * (words / sentences)) - (84.6 * (syllables / words))
    words_per_sentence = words.length.to_f / sentences.length
    syllables_per_word = syllables.to_f / words.length

    206.835 - (1.015 * words_per_sentence) - (84.6 * syllables_per_word)
  end

  def readability_level
    score = self.score
    case score
    when 90..100 then "Very Easy"
    when 80...90  then "Easy"
    when 70...80  then "Fairly Easy"
    when 60...70  then "Standard"
    when 50...60  then "Fairly Difficult"
    when 30...50  then "Difficult"
    when 0...30   then "Very Difficult"
    else "Unknown"
    end
  end

  private

  def count_syllables(word)
    word = word.downcase.gsub(/[^a-z]/, '')
    return 0 if word.empty?

    # Простий підхід: кількість голосних + деякі виключення
    vowels = 'aeiouy'
    syllable_count = 0
    prev_was_vowel = false

    word.chars.each do |char|
      is_vowel = vowels.include?(char)
      if is_vowel && !prev_was_vowel
        syllable_count += 1
      end
      prev_was_vowel = is_vowel
    end

    # Видалення "е" в кінці слова (наприклад, "the" -> 0)
    syllable_count -= 1 if word.end_with?('e') && word.length > 2

    # Мінімум 1 склад
    [syllable_count, 1].max
  end
end

2. **main.rb**

```ruby
require 'pg'
require 'openai'
require 'active_record'
require 'dotenv/load'

# Налаштування OpenAI API
OpenAI.configure do |config|
  config.access_token = ENV['OPENAI_API_KEY']
end

# Налаштування з'єднання з PostgreSQL
ActiveRecord::Base.establish_connection(
  adapter: 'postgresql',
  host: ENV['DB_HOST'] || 'localhost',
  port: ENV['DB_PORT'] || 5432,
  database: ENV['DB_NAME'],
  username: ENV['DB_USER'],
  password: ENV['DB_PASSWORD']
)

# Модель документа
class Document < ActiveRecord::Base
  self.table_name = 'documents'
end

# Функція для генерації ембедингу
def generate_embedding(text)
  response = OpenAI::Client.new.complete(
    engine: 'text-similarity-babbage-001',
    prompt: text,
    max_tokens: 0,
    temperature: 0,
    top_p: 1,
    n: 1,
    stream: false
  )
  
  # Витягування ембедингу з відповіді
  embedding = response['data'].first['embedding']
  embedding
end

# Функція для пошуку подібних документів
def search_similar_documents(query_text, limit = 5)
  # Генерація ембедингу запиту
  query_embedding = generate_embedding(query_text)
  
  # Підготовка SQL-запиту для пошуку подібних документів
  sql = <<-SQL
    SELECT id, content, (embedding <#> $1) AS distance
    FROM documents
    ORDER BY embedding <#> $1
    LIMIT $2
  SQL
  
  # Виконання запиту
  results = ActiveRecord::Base.connection.execute(
    ActiveRecord::Base.send(:sanitize_sql_array, [sql, query_embedding, limit])
  )
  
  results
end

  puts "Ембединг: #{embedding.first(5)}..." # Вивести перші 5 значень
  
  # Приклад пошуку подібних документів
  query = "Пошуковий запит"
  similar_docs = search_similar_documents(query, 3)
  
  puts "Подібні документи:"
  similar_docs.each do |doc|
    puts "ID: #{doc['id']}, Відстань: #{doc['distance']}"
  end
end

require 'sentimental'
require 'csv'
require 'json'

class ReviewSentimentClassifier
  def initialize
    @sentiment_analyzer = Sentimental.new
    @sentiment_analyzer.load_defaults
  end

  # Classify a single review
  def classify_review(review_text)
    return 'neutral' if review_text.nil? || review_text.strip.empty?
    
    sentiment_score = @sentiment_analyzer.score(review_text)
    
    case sentiment_score
    when -0.1..0.1
      'neutral'
    when -1.0..-0.1
      'negative'
    else
      'positive'
    end
  end

  # Classify multiple reviews
  def classify_reviews(review_texts)
    review_texts.map do |text|
      {
        text: text,
        sentiment: classify_review(text)
      }
    end
  end

  # Analyze review with detailed breakdown
  def analyze_review_detailed(review_text)
    return { text: review_text, sentiment: 'neutral', score: 0.0 } if review_text.nil? || review_text.strip.empty?
    
    sentiment_score = @sentiment_analyzer.score(review_text)
    sentiment = classify_review(review_text)
    
    {
      text: review_text,
      sentiment: sentiment,
      score: sentiment_score,
      magnitude: sentiment_score.abs
    }
  end

  # Process CSV file with reviews
  def process_csv_file(file_path)
    reviews = []
    
    CSV.foreach(file_path, headers: true) do |row|
      review_text = row['review'] || row['text'] || row[0]
      next if review_text.nil? || review_text.strip.empty?
      
      reviews << {
        id: row['id'] || row[1],
        text: review_text,
        sentiment: classify_review(review_text)
      }
    end
    
    reviews
  end

  # Process JSON file with reviews
  def process_json_file(file_path)
    data = JSON.parse(File.read(file_path))
    reviews = []
    
    if data.is_a?(Array)
      data.each do |item|
        review_text = item['review'] || item['text']
        next if review_text.nil? || review_text.strip.empty?
        
        reviews << {
          id: item['id'],
          text: review_text,
          sentiment: classify_review(review_text)
        }
      end
    else
      # Handle single review object
      review_text = data['review'] || data['text']
      reviews << {
        id: data['id'],
        text: review_text,
        sentiment: classify_review(review_text)
      }
    end
    
    reviews
  end

  # Get sentiment statistics
  def get_sentiment_stats(reviews)
    stats = { positive: 0, negative: 0, neutral: 0 }
    
    reviews.each do |review|
      stats[review[:sentiment].to_sym] += 1
    end
    
    total = stats.values.sum
    stats[:total] = total
    
    stats.each do |key, value|
      stats[key] = (value.to_f / total * 100).round(2) if key != :total
    end
    
    stats
  end

  # Export results to CSV
  def export_to_csv(reviews, output_file)
    CSV.open(output_file, 'w') do |csv|
      csv << ['id', 'text', 'sentiment']
      reviews.each do |review|
        csv << [review[:id], review[:text], review[:sentiment]]
      end
    end
  end
end

# TF-IDF Keyword Extraction and Document Similarity

Here's a complete Ruby solution for computing TF-IDF keywords and finding similar documents.

## Gemfile

```ruby
source 'https://rubygems.org'

gem 'nokogiri'  # For text processing
gem 'classifier-reborn'  # For basic text analysis
gem 'matrix'  # For mathematical operations
gem 'mathn'  # For additional math functionality
gem 'csv'  # For CSV file handling
```

## Implementation

```ruby
require 'nokogiri'
require 'matrix'
require 'csv'
require 'set'

class TFIDFAnalyzer
  def initialize
    @documents = []
    @term_frequency = {}
    @document_frequency = {}
    @idf_values = {}
    @tfidf_matrix = nil
  end

  # Add a document to the collection
  def add_document(text, id = nil)
    doc_id = id || @documents.length
    @documents << { id: doc_id, text: text, tokens: tokenize(text) }
  end

  # Process all documents to calculate TF-IDF
  def process_documents
    # Calculate document frequency for each term
    @documents.each do |doc|
      unique_tokens = doc[:tokens].uniq
      unique_tokens.each do |token|
        @document_frequency[token] = @document_frequency[token].to_i + 1
      end
    end

    # Calculate IDF values
    total_docs = @documents.length.to_f
    @document_frequency.each_key do |term|
      @idf_values[term] = Math.log(total_docs / @document_frequency[term])
    end

    # Calculate TF-IDF matrix
    calculate_tfidf_matrix
  end

  # Tokenize text into lowercase words
  def tokenize(text)
    text.downcase.scan(/[a-z]+/)
  end

  # Calculate TF-IDF matrix
  def calculate_tfidf_matrix
    # Get all unique terms across all documents
    all_terms = Set.new
    @documents.each do |doc|
      all_terms.merge(doc[:tokens])
    end

    # Create TF-IDF matrix
    @tfidf_matrix = []
    @documents.each_with_index do |doc, doc_index|
      tfidf_vector = {}
      term_frequency = Hash.new(0)
      
      # Calculate term frequency
      doc[:tokens].each { |term| term_frequency[term] += 1 }
      
      # Calculate TF-IDF for each term
      all_terms.each do |term|
        tf = term_frequency[term].to_f / doc[:tokens].length.to_f
        idf = @idf_values[term] || 0
        tfidf_vector[term] = tf * idf
      end
      
      @tfidf_matrix[doc_index] = tfidf_vector
    end
  end

  # Get top keywords for a specific document
  def get_keywords(doc_index, top_n = 10)
    return [] if @tfidf_matrix.nil? || doc_index >= @tfidf_matrix.length
    
    keywords = @tfidf_matrix[doc_index].sort_by { |term, tfidf| -tfidf }
    keywords.first(top_n).map { |term, tfidf| { term: term, tfidf: tfidf } }
  end

  # Get keywords for all documents
  def get_all_keywords(top_n = 10)
    keywords_list = []
    @documents.each_with_index do |doc, index|
      keywords_list << {
        document_id: doc[:id],
        document_text: doc[:text][0..100] + "...",
        keywords: get_keywords(index, top_n)
      }
    end
    keywords_list
  end

  # Calculate cosine similarity between two documents
  def cosine_similarity(doc1_index, doc2_index)
    return 0 if @tfidf_matrix.nil? || doc1_index >= @tfidf_matrix.length || doc2_index >= @tfidf_matrix.length
    
    vector1 = @tfidf_matrix[doc1_index]
    vector2 = @tfidf_matrix[doc2_index]
    
    # Get all terms present in either document
    all_terms = (vector1.keys + vector2.keys).uniq
    
    # Create vectors with same dimensions
    v1 = all_terms.map { |term| vector1[term] || 0 }
    v2 = all_terms.map { |term| vector2[term] || 0 }
    
    # Calculate dot product
    dot_product = v1.zip(v2).map { |a, b| a * b }.sum
    
    # Calculate magnitudes
    magnitude1 = Math.sqrt(v1.map { |x| x * x }.sum)
    magnitude2 = Math.sqrt(v2.map { |x| x * x }.sum)
    
    # Calculate cosine similarity
    return 0 if magnitude1 == 0 || magnitude2 == 0
    dot_product / (magnitude1 * magnitude2)
  end

  # Find most similar documents to a given document
  def find_similar_documents(doc_index, max_results = 5)
    return [] if @tfidf_matrix.nil? || doc_index >= @tfidf_matrix.length
    
    similarities = []
    @documents.each_with_index do |doc, index|
      next if index == doc_index
      similarity = cosine_similarity(doc_index, index)
      similarities << { document_id: doc[:id], similarity: similarity }
    end
    
    similarities.sort_by { |s| -s[:similarity] }.first(max_results)
  end

  # Get document information
  def get_document_info
    @documents.map do |doc|
      {
        id: doc[:id],
        text_preview: doc[:text][0..100] + "...",
        word_count: doc[:tokens].length
      }
    end
  end
end

# Example usage
if __FILE__ == $0
  # Create analyzer instance
  analyzer = TFIDFAnalyzer.new
  
  # Sample documents
  documents = [
    "Machine learning is a subset of artificial intelligence that focuses on algorithms and statistical models.",
    "Deep learning uses neural networks with multiple layers to learn from data patterns.",
    "Natural language processing helps computers understand human language and text.",
    "Computer vision allows machines to interpret and understand visual information from the world.",
    "Artificial intelligence encompasses various techniques to create intelligent machines.",
    "Data science combines statistics, programming, and domain expertise to extract insights from data."
  ]
  
  # Add documents
  documents.each_with_index do |text, index|
    analyzer.add_document(text, index)
  end
  
  # Process documents
  analyzer.process_documents
  
  puts "=== Document Information ==="
  analyzer.get_document_info.each do |doc_info|
    puts "ID: #{doc_info[:id]} | Words: #{doc_info[:word_count]} | Preview: #{doc_info[:text_preview]}"
  end
  
  puts "\n=== TF-IDF Keywords ==="
  analyzer.get_all_keywords(5).each do |doc_keywords|
    puts "\nDocument ID: #{doc_keywords[:document_id]}"
    puts "Preview: #{doc_keywords[:document_text]}"
    puts "Keywords:"
    doc_keywords[:keywords].each do |kw|
      puts "  #{kw[:term]} (TF-IDF: #{kw[:tfidf].round(4)})"
    end
  end
  
  puts "\n=== Document Similarity ==="
  # Find similar documents for document 0
  similar_docs = analyzer.find_similar_documents(0, 3)
  puts "Most similar to document 0:"
  similar_docs.each do |sim|
    puts "  Document #{sim[:document_id]} (similarity: #{sim[:similarity].round(4)})"
  end
  
  # Find similar documents for document 3
  similar_docs = analyzer.find_similar_documents(3, 3)
  puts "\nMost similar to document 3:"
  similar_docs.each do |sim|
    puts "  Document #{sim[:document_id]} (similarity: #{sim[:similarity].round(4)})"
  end
end
```

# summarizer.rb
require 'httparty'
require 'dotenv/load'

class ClaudeSummarizer
  include HTTParty

  def initialize(api_key)
    @api_key = api_key
    self.class.default_timeout 30
  end

  def summarize(text, max_length: 200)
    prompt = <<~PROMPT
      Please summarize the following support request in no more than #{max_length} characters:
      
      #{text}
    PROMPT

    response = self.class.post(
      'https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages',
      headers: {
        'Content-Type' => 'application/json',
        'x-api-key' => @api_key,
        'anthropic-version' => '2023-06-01'
      },
      body: {
        model: 'claude-3-haiku-20240307',
        max_tokens: max_length,
        messages: [
          { role: 'user', content: prompt }
        ]
      }.to_json
    )

    if response.success?
      response['content'][0]['text']
    else
      raise "API error: #{response.code} - #{response.body}"
    end
  end
end

Цей інструмент дозволяє витягати іменовані сутності типу `PERSON`, `ORGANIZATION`, `LOCATION` тощо.

```ruby
# ner_extractor.rb

require 'stanford-core-nlp'
require 'json'

# Ініціалізація Stanford CoreNLP
StanfordCoreNLP.use?(:corenlp, '4.5.0') # Використовуємо версію 4.5.0
StanfordCoreNLP.load(:corenlp)

# Функція для витягнення іменованих сутностей
def extract_named_entities(text)
  # Створюємо об'єкт для аналізу
  pipeline = StanfordCoreNLP::Pipeline.new(
    annotators: ['tokenize', 'ssplit', 'pos', 'lemma', 'ner'],
    properties: {
      'ner.useSUTime' => 'false'
    }
  )

  # Виконуємо аналіз
  annotations = pipeline.annotate(text)

  # Отримуємо іменовані сутності
  entities = []
  annotations.get(:ner).each do |annotation|
    entity_text = annotation.get(:original_text)
    entity_type = annotation.get(:ner)
    entities << { text: entity_text, type: entity_type }
  end

  entities
end

# Приклад використання
article_text = <<~TEXT
  Apple Inc. is planning to open a new office in New York City.
  Tim Cook, the CEO of Apple, announced this during the annual conference.
  The company is also investing heavily in environmental sustainability.
TEXT

entities = extract_named_entities(article_text)

puts "Витягнені іменовані сутності:"
entities.each do |entity|
  puts "- #{entity[:text]} (#{entity[:type]})"
end
```

### Пояснення коду:

1. **Gemfile**: Вказує залежності — `stanford-core-nlp` і `json`.
2. **Встановлення гемів**: `bundle install` необхідно для завантаження залежностей.
3. **Код**:
   - Ініціалізується Stanford CoreNLPPipeline з необхідними анотаторами: `tokenize`, `ssplit`, `pos`, `lemma`, `ner`.
   - Функція `extract_named_entities` отримує текст і повертає масив об'єктів, що містять імена сутностей та їх типи.
   - Приклад тексту з новинною статтею, де використані імена організацій, людей та місць.

# profanity_filter.rb
require 'active_support/core_ext/string'
require 'nokogiri'
require 'unicode'

class ProfanityFilter
  # Common profanity words and variations
  PROFANITY_LIST = [
    # Base words
    'damn', 'hell', 'shit', 'crap', 'ass', 'bitch', 'damn', 'dick', 
    'fuck', 'piss', 'poop', 'crap', 'suck', 'tits', 'cock', 'cum',

    'faggot', 'queer', 'dyke', 'retard', 'idiot', 'moron',

    # Common misspellings and variations
    'sh1t', 'sh!t', 'sh*t', 's-h-i-t', 'sh1t', 'sh!t', 'sh*t',
    'f*ck', 'f*cking', 'f*cked', 'f*ckhead', 'f*cking',
    'b!tch', 'b!tch', 'b*tch', 'bitch', 'b!tch',
    'd!ck', 'd!ck', 'd*ck', 'dick', 'd!ck',
    'f*ck', 'f*cking', 'f*cked', 'f*ckhead', 'f*cking',
    'b!tch', 'b!tch', 'b*tch', 'bitch', 'b!tch',
    'a$$', 'a$$', 'a$$', 'ass', 'a$$'
  ].freeze

  # Alternative words that may be considered offensive
  OFFENSIVE_WORDS = [
    'stupid', 'idiot', 'moron', 'retard', 'imbecile', 'dumb', 
    'dumbass', 'dumbshit', 'jerk', 'jerkoff', 'wanker', 'dickhead',
    'asshole', 'butthead', 'arse', 'arsehole', 'butt', 'butts',
    'douchebag', 'douche', 'douchehead', 'dickwad', 'dickweed',
    'prick', 'piss', 'pisses', 'pissing', 'pissed', 'pissed off',
    'cunt', 'cunts', 'cunt', 'cunt', 'bloody', 'bloody hell',
    'bloody hell', 'bloody', 'bloody hell'
  ].freeze

  # Combined list of all offensive words
  ALL_OFFENSIVE_WORDS = (PROFANITY_LIST + OFFENSIVE_WORDS).uniq.freeze

  # Regular expression patterns for matching
  PATTERNS = [
    /\b#{ALL_OFFENSIVE_WORDS.join('|')}\b/i,
    /\b#{ALL_OFFENSIVE_WORDS.map { |word| word.gsub(/./) { |char| char.match?(/[a-zA-Z]/) ? "[#{char.downcase}#{char.upcase}]" : char } }.join('|')}\b/i
  ].freeze

  def initialize(options = {})
    @replacement = options[:replacement] || '*'
    @case_sensitive = options[:case_sensitive] || false
    @whole_words_only = options[:whole_words_only] || true
    @max_replacements = options[:max_replacements] || 100
    @preserve_case = options[:preserve_case] || true
  end

  # Filter profanity from a string
  def filter(text)
    return text if text.nil? || text.empty?
    
    # Clean the text
    cleaned_text = clean_text(text)
    
    # Apply filtering
    filtered_text = apply_filter(cleaned_text)
    
    # Restore original formatting if needed
    restore_formatting(text, filtered_text)
  end

  # Check if text contains profanity
  def contains_profanity?(text)
    return false if text.nil? || text.empty?
    
    cleaned_text = clean_text(text)
    !find_profanity(cleaned_text).empty?
  end

  # Get count of profanity matches
  def profanity_count(text)
    return 0 if text.nil? || text.empty?
    
    cleaned_text = clean_text(text)
    find_profanity(cleaned_text).length
  end

  # Get list of profanity matches
  def find_profanity(text)
    return [] if text.nil? || text.empty?
    
    cleaned_text = clean_text(text)
    matches = []
    
    ALL_OFFENSIVE_WORDS.each do |word|
      next if word.empty?
      
      # Create pattern that matches the word in various cases
      pattern = if @whole_words_only
                  /\b#{Regexp.escape(word)}\b/i
                else
                  Regexp.new(Regexp.escape(word), Regexp::IGNORECASE)
                end
      
      matches.concat(cleaned_text.scan(pattern))
    end
    
    matches.uniq
  end

  private

  def clean_text(text)
    # Remove HTML tags and decode entities
    doc = Nokogiri::HTML::DocumentFragment.parse(text)
    text = doc.text
    
    # Normalize whitespace
    text = text.gsub(/\s+/, ' ').strip
    
    # Remove extra spaces
    text = text.gsub(/\s+/, ' ')
  end

  def apply_filter(text)
    filtered_text = text.dup
    matches = []
    
    # Find all profanity matches
    ALL_OFFENSIVE_WORDS.each do |word|
      next if word.empty?
      
      # Create pattern
      pattern = if @whole_words_only
                  /\b#{Regexp.escape(word)}\b/i
                else
                  Regexp.new(Regexp.escape(word), Regexp::IGNORECASE)
                end
      
      # Find matches
      text.scan(pattern) do |match|
        matches << {
          original: match,
          word: word,
          position: Regexp.last_match.begin(0),
          length: match.length
        }
      end
    end
    
    # Sort by position (descending) to avoid position shifts
    matches.sort_by! { |m| m[:position] }.reverse!
    
    # Replace matches
    replaced_count = 0
    matches.each do |match|
      break if replaced_count >= @max_replacements
      
      replacement = build_replacement(match[:original])
      start_pos = match[:position]
      end_pos = start_pos + match[:length]
      
      filtered_text[start_pos, match[:length]] = replacement
      replaced_count += 1
    end
    
    filtered_text
  end

  def build_replacement(original_word)
    if @preserve_case
      replacement = ''
      original_word.chars.each do |char|
        replacement += if char.match(/[A-Z]/)
                         @replacement.upcase
                       elsif char.match(/[a-z]/)
                         @replacement.downcase
                       else
                         @replacement
                       end
      end
      replacement
    else
      @replacement * original_word.length
    end
  end

  def restore_formatting(original, filtered)
    # For this simple implementation, just return filtered text
    # In a more complex version, we might restore original formatting
    filtered
  end
end

  end

  def average_words_per_sentence

  end

    }
  end

  end

    when 50..59

      "Difficult"

# parser.rb
require 'chronic'
require 'active_support/all'
require 'date'

class NaturalLanguageDateParser
  def self.parse(date_string)
    # First try with Chronic gem for natural language parsing
    begin
      result = Chronic.parse(date_string, now: Time.now)
      return result if result
    rescue => e
      # If Chronic fails, fall back to other methods
    end
    
    # Try with ActiveSupport's time parsing
    begin
      result = Date._parse(date_string)
      if result && !result.empty?
        # Convert to Time object
        time = Time.new(
          result[:year] || Time.now.year,
          result[:mon] || Time.now.month,
          result[:mday] || Time.now.day,
          result[:hour] || 0,
          result[:min] || 0,
          result[:sec] || 0
        )
        return time
      end
    rescue => e
      # Continue to fallback methods
    end
    
    # Try some basic pattern matching for common cases
    case date_string.downcase
    when /next (\w+)/
      day_name = $1
      return parse_next_day(day_name)
    when /today/
      return Time.now.beginning_of_day
    when /tomorrow/
      return Time.now.tomorrow.beginning_of_day
    when /yesterday/
      return Time.now.yesterday.beginning_of_day
    else
      # If all else fails, return nil or raise an error
      return nil
    end
  end
  
  private
  
  def self.parse_next_day(day_name)
    # Find the next occurrence of the specified day
    days = {
      'monday' => 1, 'tuesday' => 2, 'wednesday' => 3, 'thursday' => 4,
      'friday' => 5, 'saturday' => 6, 'sunday' => 7
    }
    
    target_day = days[day_name.downcase]
    return nil unless target_day
    
    current_day = Time.now.wday == 0 ? 7 : Time.now.wday
    days_ahead = (target_day - current_day) % 7
    
    # If it's today, get next week's occurrence
    days_ahead = 7 if days_ahead == 0
    
    next_day = Time.now + (days_ahead * 24 * 60 * 60)
    next_day.beginning_of_day
  end
end

### 2. `config/initializers/i18n.rb` (для додавання українських правил множини)

```ruby
# config/initializers/i18n.rb

# Додаємо українські правила множини
I18n::Backend::Simple.include(I18n::Backend::Pluralization)

# Визначаємо українські правила множини
I18n::Backend::Simple.class_eval do
  def pluralize(locale, entry, count)
    if entry.is_a?(Hash)
      key = case count
            when 1 then :one
            when 2..4 then :few
            when 5..20 then :many
            else :other
            end

      entry[key] || entry[:other] || count
    else
      super
    end
  end
end
```

> У цьому коді ми перевизначаємо метод `pluralize`, щоб додати українські правила:
> - `one` – для 1
> - `few` – для 2, 3, 4
> - `many` – для 5–20
> - `other` – для всіх інших випадків

class EmbeddingService
  EMBEDDING_MODEL = 'text-embedding-3-small'
  BATCH_SIZE = 100
  
  def initialize
    @openai_client = OpenAI::Client.new
  end
  
  def generate_embeddings_for_all_documents
    puts "Generating embeddings for all documents..."
    
    documents = Document.all
    
    documents.each_slice(BATCH_SIZE) do |batch|
      batch.map.with_index do |document, index|
        Concurrent::Future.execute do
          generate_and_save_embedding(document)
        end
      end.map(&:value)
    end
    
    puts "All embeddings generated successfully!"
  end
  
  private
  
  def generate_and_save_embedding(document)
    begin
      response = @openai_client.embeddings(
        model: EMBEDDING_MODEL,
        input: document.content
      )
      
      embedding_vector = response['data'].first['embedding']
      
      # Save embedding to database
      embedding = Embedding.find_or_create_by(document_id: document.id) do |emb|
        emb.embedding = embedding_vector
      end
      
      puts "Generated embedding for document: #{document.title}"
      
    rescue StandardError => e
      puts "Error generating embedding for document #{document.id}: #{e.message}"
    end
  end

  end

    # Generate query embedding
    query_embedding = generate_embedding(query_text)
    
    # Search using cosine similarity with pgvector
    results = @connection.execute(<<-SQL, [query_embedding.to_json, limit])
      SELECT d.id, d.title, d.content, 
             (e.embedding <#> $1::vector) as distance
      FROM documents d
      JOIN embeddings e ON d.id = e.document_id
      ORDER BY distance ASC
      LIMIT $2
    SQL
    
    # Convert to array of hashes
    results.map do |row|
      {
        id: row['id'],
        title: row['title'],
        content: row['content'],
        similarity: 1 - row['distance'].to_f # Convert distance to similarity score
      }
    end
  end
  
  private
  
  def generate_embedding(text)
    # Using the OpenAI client to generate embedding
    response = OpenAI::Client.new.embeddings(
      model: 'text-embedding-3-small',
      input: text
    )
    
    response['data'].first['embedding']
  end

# Обчислення TF-IDF і пошук схожих документів на Ruby

Ось рішення задачі з обчислення TF-IDF та пошуку схожих документів у Ruby:

## Gemfile
```ruby
source 'https://rubygems.org'

gem 'nokogiri'
gem 'classifier-reborn'
gem 'matrix'
gem 'csv'
```

## Код для обчислення TF-IDF та пошуку схожих документів

```ruby
require 'nokogiri'
require 'matrix'
require 'csv'
require 'set'

class TFIDFCalculator
  def initialize(documents)
    @documents = documents
    @vocabulary = build_vocabulary
    @tf_matrix = build_tf_matrix
    @idf_vector = build_idf_vector
    @tfidf_matrix = build_tfidf_matrix
  end

  # Побудова словника з усіх унікальних термінів
  def build_vocabulary
    vocab = Set.new
    @documents.each do |doc|
      doc.downcase.split.each do |word|
        # Видаляємо пунктуацію та додаємо слово до словника
        clean_word = word.gsub(/[^\w]/, '')
        vocab.add(clean_word) if clean_word.length > 0
      end
    end
    vocab.to_a.sort
  end

  # Побудова матриці TF (частота термінів)
  def build_tf_matrix
    matrix = []
    @documents.each do |doc|
      tf_vector = Array.new(@vocabulary.length, 0)
      words = doc.downcase.split
      total_words = words.length
      
      words.each do |word|
        clean_word = word.gsub(/[^\w]/, '')
        next if clean_word.empty?
        
        index = @vocabulary.index(clean_word)
        tf_vector[index] += 1 if index
      end
      
      # Нормалізація частоти
      tf_vector.map! { |count| count.to_f / total_words }
      matrix << tf_vector
    end
    
    matrix
  end

  # Побудова вектора IDF (зворотна частота документів)
  def build_idf_vector
    idf_vector = Array.new(@vocabulary.length, 0)
    
    @vocabulary.each_with_index do |term, index|
      doc_count = @documents.count { |doc| doc.downcase.include?(term) }
      # IDF = log(кількість документів / (кількість документів, що містять терм + 1))
      idf_vector[index] = Math.log(@documents.length.to_f / (doc_count + 1.0))
    end
    
    idf_vector
  end

  # Побудова матриці TF-IDF
  def build_tfidf_matrix
    tfidf_matrix = []
    
    @tf_matrix.each_with_index do |tf_vector, doc_index|
      tfidf_vector = Array.new(@vocabulary.length, 0)
      
      tfidf_vector.each_with_index do |_, index|
        tfidf_vector[index] = tf_vector[index] * @idf_vector[index]
      end
      
      tfidf_matrix << tfidf_vector
    end
    
    tfidf_matrix
  end

  # Обчислення косинусної схожості між документами
  def cosine_similarity(doc1_index, doc2_index)
    vector1 = @tfidf_matrix[doc1_index]
    vector2 = @tfidf_matrix[doc2_index]
    
    # Обчислення скалярного добутку
    dot_product = vector1.zip(vector2).map { |a, b| a * b }.sum
    
    # Обчислення норм
    norm1 = Math.sqrt(vector1.map { |x| x * x }.sum)
    norm2 = Math.sqrt(vector2.map { |x| x * x }.sum)
    
    # Обчислення косинусної схожості
    return 0 if norm1 == 0 || norm2 == 0
    dot_product / (norm1 * norm2)
  end

  # Пошук найближчих документів до заданого
  def find_similar_documents(target_doc_index, top_n = 3)
    similarities = []
    
    @documents.each_index do |index|
      next if index == target_doc_index
      
      similarity = cosine_similarity(target_doc_index, index)
      similarities << [index, similarity]
    end
    
    # Сортуємо за схожістю (від найближчого до найвіддаленішого)
    similarities.sort_by { |_, sim| -sim }.first(top_n)
  end

  # Виведення результатів TF-IDF
  def print_tfidf_results
    puts "Слова у словнику:"
    puts @vocabulary.join(", ")
    puts "\nМатриця TF-IDF:"
    
    @tfidf_matrix.each_with_index do |vector, doc_index|
      puts "Документ #{doc_index + 1}:"
      vector.each_with_index do |value, index|
        puts "  #{@vocabulary[index]}: #{value.round(4)}" if value > 0
      end
      puts
    end
  end

  # Виведення схожих документів
  def print_similar_documents(target_doc_index)
    similar_docs = find_similar_documents(target_doc_index)
    
    puts "Схожі документи до документу #{target_doc_index + 1}:"
    similar_docs.each do |doc_index, similarity|
      puts "  Документ #{doc_index + 1} (схожість: #{similarity.round(4)})"
    end
  end

  # Отримання ключових слів для документа
  def get_top_keywords(doc_index, top_n = 5)
    vector = @tfidf_matrix[doc_index]
    
    keywords = vector.each_with_index
                    .select { |value, _| value > 0 }
                    .sort_by { |value, _| -value }
                    .first(top_n)
                    .map { |value, index| [@vocabulary[index], value] }
    
    keywords
  end

  # Виведення ключових слів для документа
  def print_keywords(doc_index)
    keywords = get_top_keywords(doc_index)
    puts "Ключові слова для документу #{doc_index + 1}:"
    keywords.each do |word, tfidf|
      puts "  #{word}: #{tfidf.round(4)}"
    end
  end
end

# Приклад використання
if __FILE__ == $0
  # Приклад набору документів
  documents = [
    "Машинне навчання - це галузь штучного інтелекту",
    "Штучний інтелект використовує алгоритми для моделювання людського мислення",
    "Нейронні мережі використовуються у машинному навчанні",
    "Тренування моделей вимагає великої кількості даних",
    "Інструменти машинного навчання розробляються для автоматизації процесів"
  ]

  puts "Документи:"
  documents.each_with_index { |doc, i| puts "#{i + 1}. #{doc}" }
  puts

  # Створення калькулятора TF-IDF
  calculator = TFIDFCalculator.new(documents)

  # Вивід результатів TF-IDF
  calculator.print_tfidf_results

  # Вивід ключових слів для кожного документа
  puts "\nКлючові слова для документів:"
  documents.length.times do |i|
    calculator.print_keywords(i)
    puts
  end

  # Пошук схожих документів
  puts "\nПошук схожих документів:"
  3.times do |i|
    calculator.print_similar_documents(i)
    puts
  end
end
```

Цей код реалізує наступне:

1. **TF-IDF обчислення**:
   - Побудову словника з усіх унікальних слів
   - Обчислення TF (частоти термінів)
   - Обчислення IDF (зворотна частота документів)
   - Побудову матриці TF-IDF

2. **Пошук схожих документів**:
   - Обчислення косинусної схожості між документами
   - Пошук найближчих документів до заданого

3. **Функціональність**:
   - Виведення матриці TF-IDF
   - Визначення ключових слів для кожного документа
   - Пошук схожих документів

Для запуску:
1. Збережіть код у файл (наприклад, `tfidf.rb`)
2. Виконайте `bundle install` для встановлення залежностей
3. Запустіть `ruby tfidf.rb`

Результати будуть виведені у консоль з детальними TF-IDF значеннями, ключовими словами та схожими документами.

# DOCX to HTML and Plain Text Converter

Here's a complete Ruby solution for converting DOCX documents to HTML and plain text.

## Gemfile
```ruby
source 'https://rubygems.org'

gem 'docx'
gem 'nokogiri'
gem 'htmlentities'
gem 'fileutils'
```

## Implementation

```ruby
#!/usr/bin/env ruby

require 'docx'
require 'nokogiri'
require 'htmlentities'
require 'fileutils'
require 'pathname'

class DocxConverter
  def initialize(docx_path)
    @docx_path = Pathname.new(docx_path)
    raise ArgumentError, "File does not exist: #{@docx_path}" unless @docx_path.exist?
    raise ArgumentError, "File must be a .docx file: #{@docx_path}" unless @docx_path.extname == '.docx'
  end

  # Convert DOCX to HTML
  def to_html
    docx = Docx::Document.open(@docx_path)
    
    # Create HTML structure
    html_doc = Nokogiri::HTML::DocumentFragment.parse('')
    
    # Add basic HTML structure
    html_doc.add_child(Nokogiri::XML::Node.new('html', html_doc))
    html_html = html_doc.at_css('html')
    
    html_html.add_child(Nokogiri::XML::Node.new('head', html_doc))
    html_head = html_html.at_css('head')
    
    # Add meta charset
    meta_charset = Nokogiri::XML::Node.new('meta', html_doc)
    meta_charset['charset'] = 'UTF-8'
    html_head.add_child(meta_charset)
    
    # Add title
    title = Nokogiri::XML::Node.new('title', html_doc)
    title.content = @docx_path.basename('.docx').to_s
    html_head.add_child(title)
    
    html_html.add_child(Nokogiri::XML::Node.new('body', html_doc))
    html_body = html_html.at_css('body')
    
    # Process paragraphs
    docx.paragraphs.each_with_index do |paragraph, index|
      # Skip empty paragraphs
      next if paragraph.text.strip.empty?
      
      # Create appropriate HTML element based on paragraph style
      element = create_html_element(paragraph, index)
      html_body.add_child(element)
    end
    
    # Process tables
    docx.tables.each_with_index do |table, index|
      table_element = create_table_element(table)
      html_body.add_child(table_element)
    end
    
    # Process lists
    process_lists(docx, html_body)
    
    # Convert to string and clean up
    html_doc.to_html
  end

  # Convert DOCX to plain text
  def to_text
    docx = Docx::Document.open(@docx_path)
    text_parts = []
    
    docx.paragraphs.each do |paragraph|
      # Skip empty paragraphs
      next if paragraph.text.strip.empty?
      
      # Add paragraph text
      text_parts << paragraph.text.strip
    end
    
    # Add table content
    docx.tables.each do |table|
      table.rows.each do |row|
        row.cells.each do |cell|
          text_parts << cell.text.strip
        end
      end
    end
    
    # Join with double newlines
    text_parts.join("\n\n")
  end

  private

  def create_html_element(paragraph, index)
    # Determine element type based on paragraph style
    style = paragraph.style_name
    element = case style
             when /Heading (\d+)/
               "h#{$1}" # h1, h2, h3, etc.
             when /Heading/
               'h1'
             when /List/
               'p'
             else
               'p'
             end
    
    # Create the element
    node = Nokogiri::XML::Node.new(element, html_doc)
    
    # Process text with formatting
    text_content = process_text_formatting(paragraph.text)
    node.content = text_content
    
    node
  end

  def create_table_element(table)
    table_element = Nokogiri::XML::Node.new('table', html_doc)
    table_element['border'] = '1'
    table_element['cellpadding'] = '5'
    
    # Create table body
    tbody = Nokogiri::XML::Node.new('tbody', html_doc)
    table_element.add_child(tbody)
    
    table.rows.each do |row|
      tr = Nokogiri::XML::Node.new('tr', html_doc)
      tbody.add_child(tr)
      
      row.cells.each do |cell|
        td = Nokogiri::XML::Node.new('td', html_doc)
        td.content = cell.text.strip
        tr.add_child(td)
      end
    end
    
    table_element
  end

  def process_lists(docx, html_body)
    # Simple list processing
    list_items = docx.paragraphs.select { |p| p.text.start_with?('-') || p.text.start_with?('*') }
    
    if list_items.any?
      ul = Nokogiri::XML::Node.new('ul', html_doc)
      html_body.add_child(ul)
      
      list_items.each do |item|
        li = Nokogiri::XML::Node.new('li', html_doc)
        li.content = item.text.sub(/^[-*]\s+/, '').strip
        ul.add_child(li)
      end
    end
  end

  def process_text_formatting(text)
    # Simple text formatting processing
    # This would be more comprehensive in a full implementation
    text.strip
  end

  def html_doc
    @html_doc ||= Nokogiri::HTML::DocumentFragment.parse('')
  end
end

# CLI interface
if __FILE__ == $0
  if ARGV.length < 2
    puts "Usage: #{$0} <input.docx> <output.html|output.txt>"
    puts "Example: #{$0} document.docx output.html"
    exit 1
  end

  input_path = ARGV[0]
  output_path = ARGV[1]

  begin
    converter = DocxConverter.new(input_path)
    
    if output_path.end_with?('.html')
      html_content = converter.to_html
      File.write(output_path, html_content)
      puts "Converted #{input_path} to HTML: #{output_path}"
    elsif output_path.end_with?('.txt')
      text_content = converter.to_text
      File.write(output_path, text_content)
      puts "Converted #{input_path} to plain text: #{output_path}"
    else
      puts "Output file must end with .html or .txt"
      exit 1
    end
    
  rescue => e
    puts "Error: #{e.message}"
    exit 1
  end
end
```

## Usage Instructions

1. Create a `Gemfile` with the content above
2. Run `bundle install` to install dependencies
3. Save the implementation code to a file (e.g., `docx_converter.rb`)
4. Make it executable: `chmod +x docx_converter.rb`
5. Use from command line:

require 'numbers_and_words'

# Встановлюємо мову для I18n
I18n.config.available_locales = [:uk]
I18n.locale = :uk

class UkrainianCurrencyConverter
  def self.convert(number)
    return "нуль гривень" if number == 0

    # Використовуємо гем numbers_and_words для перетворення числа в слова
    words = number.to_words(:locale => :uk)

    # Визначаємо відмінок для гривень
    case number % 10
      when 1
        if number % 100 != 11
          "#{words} гривня"
        else
          "#{words} гривень"
        end
      when 2, 3, 4
        if number % 100 != 12 && number % 100 != 13 && number % 100 != 14
          "#{words} гривні"
        else
          "#{words} гривень"
        end
      else
        "#{words} гривень"
    end
  end
end

require 'date'
require 'holidays'

# Визначення державних свят України
UKRAINE_HOLIDAYS = %w[
  New_Year
  Christmas
  Orthodox_Christmas
  Women_Day
  Labour_Day
  Victory_Day
  Independence_Day
  Constitution_Day
  Christmas_Eve
  Easter
].freeze

# Перевірка, чи є дата державним святом в Україні
def ukraine_holiday?(date)
  return false unless date.is_a?(Date)

  # Отримати всі свята для України на цей день
  holidays = Holidays.on(date, :ua)

  # Перевірити, чи є серед них державне свято
  holidays.any? do |holiday|
    UKRAINE_HOLIDAYS.include?(holiday[:name])
  end
end

end

require 'anthropic'

class TicketSummarizer
  def initialize(api_key = ENV['ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'])
    @client = Anthropic::Client.new(api_key: api_key)
  end

  def summarize_ticket(ticket_content, max_length: 200)
    prompt = <<~PROMPT
      Please summarize the following support ticket in #{max_length} characters or less.
      Focus on the core issue, the customer's problem, and any important context.
      Keep it concise and actionable:

      #{ticket_content}
    PROMPT

      response = @client.completions.create(
        model: "claude-3-haiku-20240307",
        prompt: prompt,
        max_tokens: 300,
        temperature: 0.3

      response.content.first.text.strip
    rescue Anthropic::APIError => e
      "Error summarizing ticket: #{e.message}"
    end
  end

  def process_multiple_tickets(tickets)
    tickets.map do |ticket|
      {
        id: ticket[:id],
        summary: summarize_ticket(ticket[:content]),
        original_length: ticket[:content].length
      }
    end
  end
end

class UkrainianAddressParser
  # Визначення регулярних виразів для пошуку частин адреси
  REGEXES = {
    region: /(?:область|обл)\s*(.*?)(?=,\s*місто|,\s*м\s*|місто|м\s*|$)/i,
    city: /(?:місто|м\s*)\s*(.*?)(?=,\s*вул|,\s*в\s*|вул|в\s*|$)/i,
    street: /(?:вул|в\s*)\s*(.*?)(?=,\s*буд|,\s*б\s*|буд|б\s*|$)/i,
    house: /(?:буд|б\s*)\s*(.*?)(?=,\s*кв|,\s*к\s*|кв|к\s*|$)/i,
    apartment: /(?:кв|к\s*)\s*(.*?)(?=$)/i
  }.freeze

  def self.parse(text)
    address = {}

    REGEXES.each do |key, regex|
      match = text.match(regex)
      address[key] = match&.captures&.first&.strip if match
    end

    address
  end
end

```ruby
#!/usr/bin/env ruby
# encoding: utf-8

require 'bundler/setup'
require 'spellchecker'
require 'ukrainian'
require 'text'
require 'linguistics'
require 'mechanize'
require 'nokogiri'

class UkrainianSpellChecker
  def initialize
    @spellchecker = SpellChecker.new
    # Initialize Ukrainian dictionary (we'll build it from available sources)
    @ukrainian_words = load_ukrainian_dictionary
  end

  def check_text(text)
    # Split text into words
    words = text.split(/\s+/)
    
    # Filter out punctuation and numbers
    words = words.select { |word| word.match?(/[а-яіїєґА-ЯІЇЄҐ]/) }
    
    results = []
    words.each do |word|
      # Clean word from punctuation
      clean_word = word.gsub(/[^а-яіїєґА-ЯІЇЄҐ]/, '').downcase
      
      next if clean_word.empty?
      
      # Check if word is spelled correctly
      is_correct = @ukrainian_words.include?(clean_word)
      
      suggestions = []
      if !is_correct
        suggestions = get_suggestions(clean_word)
      end
      
      results << {
        word: word,
        correct: is_correct,
        suggestions: suggestions
      }
    end
    
    results
  end

  def get_suggestions(word)
    # Simple edit distance algorithm for suggestions
    suggestions = []
    @ukrainian_words.each do |dict_word|
      next if dict_word == word
      
      distance = levenshtein_distance(word, dict_word)
      if distance <= 2 && distance > 0
        suggestions << {
          word: dict_word,
          distance: distance
        }
      end
    end
    
    # Sort by distance and return top 5
    suggestions.sort_by { |s| s[:distance] }.first(5)
  end

  private

  def levenshtein_distance(s1, s2)
    # Calculate Levenshtein distance between two strings
    return s2.length if s1.empty?
    return s1.length if s2.empty?

    matrix = Array.new(s1.length + 1) { Array.new(s2.length + 1) }

    (0..s1.length).each { |i| matrix[i][0] = i }
    (0..s2.length).each { |j| matrix[0][j] = j }

    (1..s1.length).each do |i|
      (1..s2.length).each do |j|
        cost = s1[i-1] == s2[j-1] ? 0 : 1
        matrix[i][j] = [
          matrix[i-1][j] + 1,      # deletion
          matrix[i][j-1] + 1,      # insertion
          matrix[i-1][j-1] + cost  # substitution
        ].min
      end
    end

    matrix[s1.length][s2.length]
  end

  def load_ukrainian_dictionary
    # This is a simplified dictionary - in practice, you'd load from a proper dictionary file
    # For demonstration, we'll use a basic set of Ukrainian words
    words = [
      'привіт', 'світ', 'дякую', 'добрий', 'вечір', 'день', 'відповідь',

      'спілкування', 'відмова', 'приклад', 'інформація', 'програма', 'компьютер',
      'місто', 'країна', 'людина', 'дитина', 'сім\'я', 'дім', 'кімната',
      'книга', 'стіл', 'стільці', 'вікно', 'двері', 'світло', 'темрява',
      'сонце', 'місяць', 'зірка', 'хмара', 'дощ', 'сніг', 'вітер',
      'птах', 'риба', 'тварина', 'цвіт', 'дерево', 'квітка', 'пісня',
      'музика', 'мистецтво', 'наука', 'математика', 'історія', 'географія',
      'дітям', 'діти', 'учні', 'вчитель', 'директор', 'працівник', 'робота',
      'домашній', 'квартира', 'вулиток', 'вулиця', 'міст', 'дорога', 'автомобіль',
      'поїзд', 'літак', 'корабель', 'місто', 'село', 'сільська', 'міський',
      'закон', 'право', 'суд', 'заключення', 'право', 'відповідальність', 'обов\'язок'
    ]
    
    # Add more common words
    words << %w[від', 'до', 'на', 'у', 'і', 'та', 'чи', 'або', 'але', 'що', 'який', 'як']
    words.flatten!
    
    # Add variations and common mistakes
    variations = words.map do |word|
      [word, word + 'а', word + 'е', word + 'и', word + 'о', word + 'у']

    words.concat(variations)
