```ruby
gem 'yaml'
```

## Реалізація

```ruby
require 'csv'
require 'date'
require 'terminal-table'
require 'money'
require 'i18n'
require 'yaml'

# Ініціалізація локалізації для української мови
I18n.load_path = Dir[File.expand_path('config/locales/*.yml', __dir__)]
I18n.default_locale = :uk

# Конфігурація валюти
Money.locale_backend = nil
Money.default_currency = Money::Currency.new(:uah, {
  :subunit => "копійки",
  :symbol => "₴",
  :currency_name => "Українська гривня"
})

class Transaction
  attr_accessor :date, :description, :amount, :category

  def initialize(date, description, amount, category = nil)
    @date = date
    @description = description
    @amount = amount.to_f
    @category = category
  end

  def positive_amount?
    @amount > 0
  end

  def formatted_amount
    Money.new(@amount * 100, "UAH").format
  end

  def to_s
    "#{@date.strftime('%d.%m.%Y')} | #{@description.ljust(30)} | #{formatted_amount} | #{@category || 'Не категорізовано'}"
  end
end

class TransactionImporter
  CATEGORIES = {
    "Продукти" => ["супермаркет", "маркет", "магазин", "продукти", "хліб", "молоч", "мясо"],
    "Житло" => ["квартира", "комунал", "газ", "вода", "електро", "оплата"],
    "Транспорт" => ["автобус", "метро", "таксі", "бензин", "заправка", "авто"],
    "Розваги" => ["кіно", "концерт", "ресторан", "кафе", "білет"],
    "Здоров'я" => ["аптека", "лікарня", "ліки", "мед"],
    "Одяг" => ["магазин", "одаг", "шоп", "інтернет-магазин"],
    "Музика" => ["spotify", "apple music", "музика"],
    "Інтернет" => ["інтернет", "мобільний", "зв'язок", "київстар", "вф"],
    "Прочеє" => []
  }.freeze

  def initialize(csv_file)
    @csv_file = csv_file
    @transactions = []
    @categories = CATEGORIES.dup
  end

  def import
    CSV.foreach(@csv_file, headers: true, col_sep: ";", encoding: "windows-1251") do |row|
      next unless valid_row?(row)

      date = parse_date(row)
      description = row["Назва"]
      amount = parse_amount(row)

      transaction = Transaction.new(date, description, amount)
      categorize(transaction)

      @transactions << transaction
    end
  end

  def categorize(transaction)
    description = transaction.description.downcase

    @categories.each do |category, keywords|
      if keywords.any? { |word| description.include?(word) }
        transaction.category = category
        return
      end
    end

    # Додаткова логіка для визначення категорії на основі описів
    if transaction.description.start_with?("ПОПОВНЕННЯ")
      transaction.category = "Поповнення"
    elsif transaction.description.match?(/Переказ|Карта \d+/)
      transaction.category = "Перекази"
    end
  end

  def analyze
    return unless @transactions.any?

    total_income = @transactions.select(&:positive_amount?).sum(&:amount)
    total_expenses = @transactions.reject(&:positive_amount?).sum(&:amount).abs
    total_balance = total_income + total_expenses

    puts "\nАналіз транзакцій:"
    puts "Період: #{@transactions.first.date.strftime('%d.%m.%Y')} - #{@transactions.last.date.strftime('%d.%m.%Y')}"
    puts "Всього доходів: #{Money.new(total_income * 100, "UAH").format}"
    puts "Всього витрат: #{Money.new(total_expenses * 100, "UAH").format}"
    puts "Баланс: #{Money.new(total_balance * 100, "UAH").format}"
    puts "\nРозподіл витрат за категоріями:"

    display_categories_table
  end

  def display_categories_table
    categories_stats = Hash.new(0.0)
    @transactions.reject(&:positive_amount?).each do |t|
      categories_stats[t.category || "Не категорізовано"] += t.amount.abs
    end

    sorted_categories = categories_stats.sort_by { |k, v| -v }

    table = Terminal::Table.new do |t|
      t.title = "Розподіл витрат за категоріями"
      t.headings = ['Категорія', 'Сума', 'Відсоток']
      t.rows = sorted_categories.map do |category, amount|
        percentage = (amount / categories_stats.values.sum * 100).round(2)
        [category, Money.new(amount * 100, "UAH").format, "#{percentage}%"]
      end
    end
    puts table
  end

  private

  def valid_row?(row)
    row["Опис"] && row["Сума"] && row["Сума"] != "0.00" && row["Дата"]
  end

  def parse_date(row)
    Date.parse(row["Дата"])
  rescue ArgumentError
    # Фаллбек для різних форматів дати
    Date.strptime(row["Дата"], "%d.%m.%Y")
  end

  def parse_amount(row)
    # Отримуємо значення з правильного стовпця
    amount = row["Сума"].gsub(",", ".").to_f
    # Якщо сума від'ємна, перетворюємо її на витрати
    amount < 0 ? -amount : amount
  end
end

# Приклад використання
if __FILE__ == $0
  puts "Введіть шлях до файлу виписки CSV:"
  file_path = gets.chomp

  begin
    importer = TransactionImporter.new(file_path)
    importer.import
    importer.analyze
  rescue StandardError => e
    puts "Сталася помилка: #{e.message}"
  end
end
```

## Implementation

```ruby
require 'fedex'
require 'dotenv'
require 'prawn'

# Load environment variables
Dotenv.load

class FedExShipper
  def initialize
    @client = FedEx::Client.new(
      key: ENV['FEDEX_KEY'],
      password: ENV['FEDEX_PASSWORD'],
      account_number: ENV['FEDEX_ACCOUNT_NUMBER'],
      meter_number: ENV['FEDEX_METER_NUMBER']
    )
  end

  def create_shipment
    shipment = FedEx::Shipment.new

    # Set shipment details
    shipment.service_type = 'FEDEX_GROUND' # or other service types
    shipment.packaging_type = 'YOUR_PACKAGING_TYPE'
    shipment.dropoff_type = 'REGULAR_PICKUP'
    shipment.shipper = create_address('SHIPPER')
    shipment.recipient = create_address('RECIPIENT')
    shipment.shipping_charges_payment = create_payment('SHIPPER')

    # Add package
    package = FedEx::Package.new
    package.weight = '2.000' # 2 pounds
    package.weight_units = 'LB'
    package.dimensions = { length: '10', width: '6', height: '4' }
    package.dimension_units = 'IN'
    shipment.add_package(package)

    # Set label format
    shipment.label_format = 'PDF'

    # Create the shipment
    response = @client.create_shipment(shipment)

    if response.success?
      shipment_tracking_number = response.tracking_number
      shipment_label_pdf = response.label_pdf

      # Save the PDF label
      save_pdf_label(shipment_label_pdf, shipment_tracking_number)

      # Return tracking number
      shipment_tracking_number
    else
      raise "Failed to create shipment: #{response.errors.join(', ')}"
    end
  end

  private

  def create_address(role)
    address = FedEx::Address.new
    address.person_name = ENV["#{role}_NAME"]
    address.company_name = ENV["#{role}_COMPANY"]
    address.street_lines = [ENV["#{role}_STREET1"], ENV["#{role}_STREET2"]]
    address.city = ENV["#{role}_CITY"]
    address.state_or_province_code = ENV["#{role}_STATE"]
    address.postal_code = ENV["#{role}_POSTAL_CODE"]
    address.country_code = ENV["#{role}_COUNTRY_CODE"]
    address.phone_number = ENV["#{role}_PHONE"]
    address.residential = ENV["#{role}_RESIDENTIAL"] == 'true'
    address
  end

  def create_payment(role)
    payment = FedEx::Payment.new
    payment.payment_type = 'SENDER'
    payment.account_number = ENV['FEDEX_ACCOUNT_NUMBER']
    payment
  end

  def save_pdf_label(pdf_data, tracking_number)
    filename = "fedex_label_#{tracking_number}.pdf"
    File.binwrite(filename, pdf_data)
    puts "Label saved as #{filename}"
    filename
  end
end

# Example usage
if __FILE__ == $0
  shipper = FedExShipper.new
  begin
    tracking_number = shipper.create_shipment
    puts "Shipment created successfully! Tracking number: #{tracking_number}"
  rescue => e
    puts "Error creating shipment: #{e.message}"
  end
end
```

```ruby
require 'json'
require 'logger'
require 'securerandom'
require 'dotenv/load'

# Configuration class to manage API settings
class MedocConfig
  def self.base_url
    ENV['MEDOC_API_BASE_URL'] || 'https://api.medoc.ua'
  end

  def self.client_id
    ENV['MEDOC_CLIENT_ID'] || raise('MEDOC_CLIENT_ID environment variable is required')
  end

  def self.client_secret
    ENV['MEDOC_CLIENT_SECRET'] || raise('MEDOC_CLIENT_SECRET environment variable is required')
  end

  def self.username
    ENV['MEDOC_USERNAME'] || raise('MEDOC_USERNAME environment variable is required')
  end

  def self.password
    ENV['MEDOC_PASSWORD'] || raise('MEDOC_PASSWORD environment variable is required')
  end

  def self.logger
    @logger ||= Logger.new(STDOUT).tap do |log|
      log.level = ENV['LOG_LEVEL'] || Logger::INFO
      log.formatter = proc do |severity, datetime, progname, msg|
        "#{datetime.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')} #{severity}: #{msg}\n"
      end
    end
  end
end

# Main class for interacting with M.E.Doc API
class MedocInvoiceSender
  include HTTParty
  base_uri MedocConfig.base_url

  # Initialize with authentication
  def initialize
    @auth_token = authenticate
    MedocConfig.logger.info "Successfully authenticated with M.E.Doc API"
  end

  # Authenticate with the M.E.Doc API
  def authenticate
    response = self.class.post(
      '/auth/token',
      body: {
        grant_type: 'password',
        username: MedocConfig.username,
        password: MedocConfig.password,
        client_id: MedocConfig.client_id,
        client_secret: MedocConfig.client_secret
      }.to_json,
      headers: {
        'Content-Type' => 'application/json',
        'Accept' => 'application/json'
      }
    )

    unless response.success?
      error_msg = "Authentication failed: #{response.body}"
      MedocConfig.logger.error error_msg
      raise StandardError, error_msg
    end

    response.parsed_response['access_token']
  end

  # Send an invoice to the Ukrainian tax service
  def send_invoice(invoice_data)
    headers = {
      'Content-Type' => 'application/json',
      'Accept' => 'application/json',
      'Authorization' => "Bearer #{@auth_token}"
    }

    response = self.class.post(
      '/api/invoices',
      body: invoice_data.to_json,
      headers: headers
    )

    if response.success?
      MedocConfig.logger.info "Invoice successfully sent. Response: #{response.parsed_response}"
      response.parsed_response
    else
      error_msg = "Failed to send invoice: #{response.body}"
      MedocConfig.logger.error error_msg
      raise StandardError, error_msg
    end
  end

  # Optional: Get the status of a sent invoice
  def get_invoice_status(invoice_id)
    headers = {
      'Authorization' => "Bearer #{@auth_token}"
    }

    response = self.class.get(
      "/api/invoices/#{invoice_id}/status",
      headers: headers
    )

    if response.success?
      response.parsed_response
    else
      error_msg = "Failed to get invoice status: #{response.body}"
      MedocConfig.logger.error error_msg
      raise StandardError, error_msg
    end
  end
end
```

Here's a complete solution for creating a FedEx shipment, downloading the label as PDF, and storing the tracking number. This uses the `fedex` gem which provides a Ruby interface to FedEx's web services.

## Implementation

```ruby
require 'fedex'
require 'open-uri'
require 'fileutils'

class FedExShipper
  # Initialize with your FedEx credentials and account information
  def initialize
    @client = FedEx::Client.new(
      key: ENV['FEDEX_KEY'],
      password: ENV['FEDEX_PASSWORD'],
      account_number: ENV['FEDEX_ACCOUNT_NUMBER'],
      meter_number: ENV['FEDEX_METER_NUMBER']
    )
  end

  # Create a FedEx shipment and return the tracking number and label URL
  def create_shipment
    # Shipment details
    shipper = FedEx::Shipper.new(
      name: 'Your Company Name',
      address: FedEx::Address.new(
        street_lines: ['123 Main St'],
        city: 'Anytown',
        state: 'CA',
        postal_code: '90210',
        country_code: 'US'
      )
    )

    recipient = FedEx::Recipient.new(
      name: 'Recipient Name',
      address: FedEx::Address.new(
        street_lines: ['456 Oak Ave'],
        city: 'Othertown',
        state: 'NY',
        postal_code: '10001',
        country_code: 'US'
      )
    )

    shipping_charges_payment = FedEx::ShippingChargesPayment.new(
      payment_type: :SENDER
    )

    # Package details
    package = FedEx::Package.new(
      weight: FedEx::Weight.new(
        units: :LB,
        value: 10.0
      ),
      dimensions: FedEx::Dimensions.new(
        length: 10,
        width: 5,
        height: 4,
        units: :IN
      )
    )

    # Request shipment
    request = FedEx::CreateShipmentRequest.new(
      service: :FEDEX_GROUND,
      shipper: shipper,
      recipient: recipient,
      shipping_charges_payment: shipping_charges_payment,
      packages: [package],
      label_response_options: :URL_ONLY
    )

    response = @client.process_shipping(request)

    if response.success?
      tracking_number = response.tracking_number
      label_url = response.label_url

      # Download the label PDF
      download_label(label_url, tracking_number)

      { tracking_number: tracking_number, success: true, message: 'Shipment created successfully' }
    else
      { success: false, message: response.errors.to_s }
    end
  end

  # Download the label PDF and save it with a meaningful filename
  def download_label(label_url, tracking_number)
    label_path = "labels/#{tracking_number}_label.pdf"

    # Create directory if it doesn't exist
    FileUtils.mkdir_p('labels')

    File.open(label_path, 'wb') do |file|
      file.puts URI.open(label_url).read
    end

    label_path
  end
end

# Usage example

  # You should set these environment variables or replace with your actual credentials
  # ENV['FEDEX_KEY'] = 'your_fedex_key'

  # ENV['FEDEX_ACCOUNT_NUMBER'] = 'your_account_number'
  # ENV['FEDEX_METER_NUMBER'] = 'your_meter_number'

  result = fedex.create_shipment

  if result[:success]
    puts "Tracking Number: #{result[:tracking_number]}"
    puts "Label saved as: labels/#{result[:tracking_number]}_label.pdf"
  else
    puts "Error: #{result[:message]}"
  end
end
```

```ruby
  include HTTParty

  def initialize
    @base_uri = ENV['MEDOC_API_BASE_URI'] || 'https://api.medoc.ua'
    @api_key = ENV['MEDOC_API_KEY']
    @username = ENV['MEDOC_API_USERNAME']
    @password = ENV['MEDOC_API_PASSWORD']

  end

    url = "#{@base_uri}/api/v1/invoices"

    # Надсилаємо запит з токеном
    response = self.class.post(
      url,
      headers: {
        'Authorization' => "Bearer #{token}",
        'Content-Type' => 'application/json',
        'Accept' => 'application/json'
      },
      body: invoice_data.to_json
    )

    handle_response(response)
  end

  def authenticate
    response = self.class.post(
      "#{@base_uri}/api/auth/login",
      body: {
        username: @username,
        password: @password
      }.to_json,
      headers: {
        'Content-Type' => 'application/json'
      }
    )

    if response.success?
      JSON.parse(response.body)['access_token']
    else
      raise "Authentication failed: #{response.body}"
    end
  end

  private

  def handle_response(response)
    if response.success?
      JSON.parse(response.body)
    else
      raise "API request failed: #{response.body}"
    end
  end
end
```

# Ruby Implementation for UPS Shipping Rates

Here's a complete solution to get shipping rates from UPS for a parcel with given weight and dimensions. The implementation uses the `ups_ship` gem which provides UPS API functionality.

## Gemfile

```ruby
gem 'httparty', '~> 0.20.0'
gem 'json', '~> 2.6.0'
```

## Implementation

```ruby
require 'ups_ship'
require 'httparty'
require 'json'

class UpsShippingRateCalculator
  attr_reader :access_key, :username, :password, :account_number

  def initialize(access_key, username, password, account_number)
    @access_key = access_key
    @username = username
    @password = password
    @account_number = account_number
  end

  def get_shipping_rates(origin, destination, weight, dimensions)
    # Initialize UPS client
    ups = UPS::Ship.new(
      access_key: access_key,
      username: username,
      password: password,
      account_number: account_number
    )

    # Create a shipment request
    shipment = UPS::Shipment.new(
      shipper: UPS::Shipper.new(
        name: 'Your Company Name',
        address: UPS::Address.new(
          address_line1: origin[:address1],
          address_line2: origin[:address2] || '',
          city: origin[:city],
          state: origin[:state],
          postal_code: origin[:postal_code],
          country: origin[:country]
        )
      ),
      ship_to: UPS::Address.new(
        name: destination[:name],
        address_line1: destination[:address1],
        address_line2: destination[:address2] || '',
        city: destination[:city],
        state: destination[:state],
        postal_code: destination[:postal_code],
        country: destination[:country]
      ),
      package: UPS::Package.new(
        description: 'Sample package',
        weight: UPS::UnitOfMeasurement.new(value: weight, unit: 'lbs'),
        dimensions: UPS::Dimensions.new(
          length: dimensions[:length],
          width: dimensions[:width],
          height: dimensions[:height],
          unit: 'in'
        )
      )
    )

    # Get shipping rates
    rates = ups.rate(shipment)

    # Format and return the rates
    format_rates(rates)
  rescue StandardError => e
    { error: "Failed to get UPS rates: #{e.message}" }
  end

  private

  def format_rates(rates)
    rates.each_with_object([]) do |rate, result|
      result << {
        service: rate.service,
        rate: rate.rate,
        currency: rate.currency,
        delivery_days: rate.delivery_days,
        service_description: rate.service_description
      }
    end
  end
end
```

```ruby
      time = event.css('.time').text.strip
```


### 2. Shopify Sync Worker

Create `app/workers/shopify_sync_worker.rb`:

```ruby
class ShopifySyncWorker
  include Sidekiq::Worker

  sidekiq_options retry: 3

  def perform
    sync_products
    sync_inventory_levels
  end

  private

  def sync_products
    shopify_products = ShopifyAPI::Product.find(:all, limits: 250)

    shopify_products.each do |shopify_product|
      product = Product.find_or_initialize_by(shopify_id: shopify_product.id)

      product.update(
        title: shopify_product.title,
        body_html: shopify_product.body_html,
        vendor: shopify_product.vendor,
        product_type: shopify_product.product_type,
        status: shopify_product.status,
        created_at: shopify_product.created_at,
        updated_at: shopify_product.updated_at,
        handle: shopify_product.handle
      )

      sync_variants(product, shopify_product.variants)
    end
  end

  def sync_variants(product, shopify_variants)
    shopify_variants.each do |shopify_variant|
      variant = product.variants.find_or_initialize_by(shopify_id: shopify_variant.id)

      variant.update(
        title: shopify_variant.title,
        sku: shopify_variant.sku,
        price: shopify_variant.price,
        inventory_quantity: shopify_variant.inventory_quantity,
        weight: shopify_variant.weight,
        requires_shipping: shopify_variant.requires_shipping,
        status: shopify_variant.status
      )

      # We'll handle inventory levels separately in sync_inventory_levels
    end
  end

  def sync_inventory_levels
    inventory_items = ShopifyAPI::InventoryItem.find(:all, limits: 250)

    inventory_items.each do |inventory_item|
      inventory_level = inventory_item.inventory_levels.first

      if inventory_level
        variant = Variant.find_by(shopify_id: inventory_item.id)
        if variant
          variant.update(
            inventory_quantity: inventory_level.available,
            updated_at: inventory_level.updated_at
          )
        end
      end
    end
  end
end
```

### 3. Models

Create `app/models/product.rb`:

```ruby

  validates :shopify_id, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validates :title, presence: true
end
```

### 4. Database Migrations

```bash

rails g model Variant shopify_id:string product:references title:string sku:string price:decimal inventory_quantity:integer weight:decimal requires_shipping:boolean status:string
```

Then run the migrations:

```bash

```

### 5. Configure Sidekiq

Create `config/initializers/sidekiq.rb`:

```ruby
require 'sidekiq'
require 'sidekiq-scheduler'

Sidekiq.configure_server do |config|
  config.redis = { url: 'redis://localhost:6379/0' }
end

Sidekiq.configure_client do |config|

end

# Schedule the sync every hour
Sidekiq.configure_server do |config|
  config.on(:startup) do
    schedule = {
      'sync_products' => {
        'class' => 'ShopifySyncWorker',
        'cron' => '0 * * * *', # Every hour at the start of the hour
        'enabled' => true
      }

end
```

# Ruby Implementation for Comparing and Buying Shipping Labels via EasyPost API

Here's a complete solution that includes the Gemfile and implementation code:

## Gemfile

```ruby
source 'https://rubygems.org'

gem 'easypost', '~> 6.0' # Official EasyPost Ruby gem
gem 'dotenv', '~> 2.7'    # For loading environment variables from .env file
```

## Implementation

```ruby
require 'easypost'
require 'dotenv/load'

class ShippingRateComparer
  def initialize(api_key)
    EasyPost.api_key = api_key
  end

  # Compare rates from multiple carriers and buy the cheapest label
  def compare_and_buy_cheapest_label(params)
    # Create a shipment
    shipment = EasyPost::Shipment.create(
      to_address: params[:to_address],
      from_address: params[:from_address],
      parcels: [params[:parcel]]
    )

    # Get all rates from different carriers
    shipment.refresh_rates

    # Find the cheapest rate
    cheapest_rate = find_cheapest_rate(shipment)

    if cheapest_rate
      # Buy the cheapest label
      bought_label = shipment.buy(rate: cheapest_rate)

      {
        success: true,
        label: bought_label,
        carrier: cheapest_rate.carrier,
        service: cheapest_rate.service,
        rate: cheapest_rate.rate
      }
    else
      {
        success: false,
        error: "No valid shipping rates available"
      }
    end
  end

  private

  # Find the cheapest rate from the available options
  def find_cheapest_rate(shipment)
    rates = shipment.rates.select { |rate| rate.rate && rate.rate > 0 }

    return nil if rates.empty?

    rates.min_by { |rate| rate.rate }
  end
end
```

## Example Usage

```ruby
# Load environment variables from .env file
# Create a .env file with your EasyPost API key: EASYPOST_API_KEY=your_api_key_here
Dotenv.load

# Example parameters for a shipment

    name: "John Doe",

    city: "New York",

    zip: "10001",

    phone: "555-555-5555"
  },

    zip: "94105",
    country: "US",
    phone: "415-555-5555"
  },
  parcel: {
    length: 10.2,
    width: 7.5,
    height: 4.0,
    weight: 2.0
  }
}

# Compare and buy the cheapest label
result = comparer.compare_and_buy_cheapest_label(params)

if result[:success]
  puts "Successfully bought label with #{result[:carrier]} #{result[:service]}"
  puts "Cost: $#{sprintf('%.2f', result[:rate])}"
  puts "Label URL: #{result[:label].postage_label.url}"
  puts "Tracking code: #{result[:label].tracking_code}"
else
  puts "Error: #{result[:error]}"

```

## How It Works

1. **Initialization**: The `ShippingRateComparer` class is initialized with your EasyPost API key.

2. **Creating a Shipment**: The `compare_and_buy_cheapest_label` method creates a shipment object with the provided parameters (to address, from address, and parcel dimensions/weight).

3. **Refreshing Rates**: The method calls `refresh_rates` to get shipping rate quotes from all available carriers (USPS, UPS, FedEx, DHL, etc.).

4. **Finding the Cheapest Rate**: The `find_cheapest_rate` helper method filters out invalid rates and finds the one with the lowest cost.

5. **Buying the Label**: If a valid rate is found, the method uses the `buy` method to purchase the shipping label.

6. **Returning Results**: The method returns a hash with the result, including the purchased label, carrier, service, and rate.

## Requirements

1. You need an EasyPost account and API key.
2. Create a `.env` file in your project root with your API key: `EASYPOST_API_KEY=your_api_key_here`
3. Install the required gems by running `bundle install`

### 2. Sync Model

Create `app/models/shopify_sync.rb`:

```ruby
class ShopifySync
  def self.sync_products
    Rails.logger.info "Starting Shopify product sync..."

    # Fetch products from Shopify
    products = ShopifyAPI::Product.find(:all, params: { limit: 250 })

    products.each do |product|
      process_product(product)
    end

    Rails.logger.info "Finished syncing #{products.count} products"
  end

  def self.sync_inventory
    Rails.logger.info "Starting Shopify inventory sync..."

    # Fetch inventory items from Shopify
    inventory_items = ShopifyAPI::InventoryItem.find(:all, params: { limit: 250 })

    inventory_items.each do |inventory_item|
      process_inventory_item(inventory_item)
    end

    Rails.logger.info "Finished syncing #{inventory_items.count} inventory items"
  end

  private

  def self.process_product(shopify_product)
    # Find or create corresponding product in your database
    product = Product.find_or_initialize_by(shopify_id: shopify_product.id)

    product.update(
      title: shopify_product.title,
      handle: shopify_product.handle,
      body_html: shopify_product.body_html,
      vendor: shopify_product.vendor,
      product_type: shopify_product.product_type,

      updated_at: shopify_product.updated_at,
      published_at: shopify_product.published_at,
      status: shopify_product.status,
      tags: shopify_product.tags
    )

    # Sync variants
    shopify_product.variants.each do |variant|
      process_variant(variant, product)
    end
  end

  def self.process_variant(shopify_variant, product)
    variant = Variant.find_or_initialize_by(shopify_id: shopify_variant.id, product: product)

    variant.update(
      shopify_id: shopify_variant.id,
      sku: shopify_variant.sku,
      barcode: shopify_variant.barcode,
      price: shopify_variant.price,
      compare_at_price: shopify_variant.compare_at_price,
      requires_shipping: shopify_variant.requires_shipping,
      taxable: shopify_variant.taxable,
      inventory_management: shopify_variant.inventory_management,
      inventory_policy: shopify_variant.inventory_policy,
      inventory_quantity: shopify_variant.inventory_quantity,
      option1: shopify_variant.option1,
      option2: shopify_variant.option2,
      option3: shopify_variant.option3,
      weight: shopify_variant.weight,
      weight_unit: shopify_variant.weight_unit
    )
  end

  def self.process_inventory_item(shopify_inventory_item)
    inventory_item = InventoryItem.find_or_initialize_by(shopify_id: shopify_inventory_item.id)

    inventory_item.update(
      shopify_id: shopify_inventory_item.id,
      sku: shopify_inventory_item.sku,
      barcode: shopify_inventory_item.barcode,
      requires_shipping: shopify_inventory_item.requires_shipping,
      cost: shopify_inventory_item.cost,
      country_code_of_origin: shopify_inventory_item.country_code_of_origin,
      country_origin: shopify_inventory_item.country_origin,
      province_code_of_origin: shopify_inventory_item.province_code_of_origin,
      harmonized_system_code: shopify_inventory_item.harmonized_system_code,
      inventory_item_id: shopify_inventory_item.inventory_item_id
    )

    # Sync inventory levels
    locations = ShopifyAPI::InventoryLevel.find(:all, params: { inventory_item_ids: shopify_inventory_item.id, location_ids: 'all' })
    locations.each do |location|
      process_inventory_level(location, inventory_item)
    end
  end

  def self.process_inventory_level(shopify_level, inventory_item)
    inventory_level = InventoryLevel.find_or_initialize_by(
```

# Ruby Implementation for USPS Address Validation

Here's a complete solution for validating and normalizing a US shipping address using the USPS Address API.

## Gemfile

```ruby
source 'https://rubygems.org'

gem 'httparty'
gem 'activesupport' # For string normalization
```

## Implementation

```ruby
require 'httparty'
require 'active_support/core_ext/string'

class USPSAddressValidator
  include HTTParty

  # USPS Address Validation API endpoint
  API_ENDPOINT = 'https://api.usps.com/address-validation/v3/address/validate'

  # USPS API credentials - you'll need to get these from USPS
  # In production, these should come from environment variables or a config file
  USERID = ENV['USPS_API_USERID'] || 'YOUR_USPS_API_USERID'
  PASSWORD = ENV['USPS_API_PASSWORD'] || 'YOUR_USPS_API_PASSWORD'

  def initialize
    @options = {
      headers: {
        'Content-Type' => 'application/json',
        'Accept' => 'application/json'
      },
      basic_auth: {
        username: USERID,
        password: PASSWORD
      }
    }
  end

  # Main method to validate and normalize an address
  def validate_address(address_params)
    begin
      response = self.class.post(
        API_ENDPOINT,
        body: build_request_body(address_params).to_json,
        headers: @options[:headers],
        basic_auth: @options[:basic_auth]
      )

      if response.success?
        parse_response(response.body)
      else
        handle_error(response)
      end
    rescue StandardError => e
      { error: "API request failed: #{e.message}" }
    end
  end

  private

  def build_request_body(address_params)
    {
      "input_id": "00001",
      "return_carrier_route": true,
      "return_dpv": true,
      "return_footnotes": true,
      "return_analysis": true,
      "address": {
        "name": address_params[:name] || '',
        "firm": address_params[:firm] || '',
        "address1": address_params[:address1] || '',
        "address2": address_params[:address2] || '',
        "city": address_params[:city] || '',
        "state": address_params[:state] || '',
        "zipcode": address_params[:zipcode] || '',
        "plus4code": address_params[:plus4code] || ''
      }
    }
  end

  def parse_response(response_body)
    data = JSON.parse(response_body)

    if data['input_id'] == '00002'
      # USPS returns 00002 for successful validation
      normalized_address = data['address']
      {
        success: true,
        normalized_address: {
          name: normalized_address['name'],
          firm: normalized_address['firm'],
          address1: normalized_address['address'],
          address2: normalized_address['address2'],
          city: normalized_address['city'],
          state: normalized_address['state'],
          zipcode: normalized_address['zipcode'],
          plus4code: normalized_address['plus4code'],
          carrier_route: normalized_address['carrier_route'],
          dpv_confirmation: normalized_address['dpv_confirmation'],
          dpv_cmra: normalized_address['dpv_cmra'],
          dpv_not_for_mail: normalized_address['dpv_not_for_mail'],
          dpv_active: normalized_address['dpv_active'],
          dpv_vacant: normalized_address['dpv_vacant'],
          dpv_footnotes: normalized_address['dpv_footnotes'],
          analysis: normalized_address['analysis']
        }
      }
    else
      {
        success: false,
        errors: data['errors'] || ["Address validation failed"],
        suggestions: data['suggestions'] || []
      }
    end
  end

  def handle_error(response)
    {
      success: false,
      error: "USPS API error: #{response.code}",
      message: response.body
    }
  end
end
```

## Usage Example

```ruby
# Example usage
validator = USPSAddressValidator.new

address_params = {
  name: "John Doe",
  address1: "123 Main St",
  city: "Anywhere",
  state: "CA",
```

1. **API Credentials**: You'll need to obtain credentials from USPS to use their API. These should be stored securely (not hardcoded) in environment variables or a configuration file.

2. **Error Handling**: The code includes basic error handling, but you may want to expand it based on your application's needs.

3. **Rate Limits**: Be aware of USPS API rate limits and implement appropriate retry logic if needed.

4. **Address Fields**: The USPS API expects specific field names and formats. The implementation maps common address fields to what the API expects.

5. **Testing**: In a production environment, you should add unit tests for this class.

```ruby
require 'dotenv'

require 'active_record'

# Load environment variables
Dotenv.load

LOGGER.formatter = proc do |severity, datetime, progname, msg|
  "#{datetime.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')} [#{severity}] #{msg}\n"
end

# Database configuration

  database: 'stock_manager.db'
)

# Database schema
ActiveRecord::Schema.define do
  create_table :products, force: true do |t|
    t.string :name, null: false
    t.string :description
    t.integer :stock_quantity, null: false, default: 0
    t.string :ebay_item_id
    t.timestamps
  end

# Product model
class Product < ActiveRecord::Base
  validates :name, presence: true
  validates :stock_quantity, numericality: { greater_than_or_equal_to: 0 }

  after_save :update_ebay_listing
end

# eBay API Client
class EbayClient
  def initialize
    @config = {
      token: ENV['EBAY_API_TOKEN'],
      sandbox: ENV['EBAY_SANDBOX'] == 'true' ? true : false
    }

    @client = EbayApi::Client.new(@config)
  end

  def list_item(product)
    LOGGER.info "Listing product #{product.id} on eBay: #{product.name}"

    item = {
      title: product.name,
      description: product.description,
      quantity: product.stock_quantity,
      price: 10.00,  # You would typically get this from the product
      category_id: '377',  # Electronics category as example
      condition_id: '1000',  # New condition
      return_policy: {
        returns_accepted: true,
        returns_within: '30',
        refund_method: 'MoneyBack',
        shipping_cost_paid_by: 'Buyer'
      }
    }

    response = @client.add_item(item)
    product.ebay_item_id = response.item_id
    product.save

    LOGGER.info "Successfully listed on eBay. Item ID: #{response.item_id}"
  rescue StandardError => e
    LOGGER.error "Failed to list on eBay: #{e.message}"
    raise
  end

  def update_quantity(item_id, quantity)
    LOGGER.info "Updating quantity for eBay item #{item_id} to #{quantity}"

    @client.update_inventory(item_id, quantity: quantity)
  rescue StandardError => e
    LOGGER.error "Failed to update eBay quantity: #{e.message}"
    raise
  end
end

# Stock Updater
class StockUpdater
  def self.update_all
    products = Product.where.not(ebay_item_id: nil)
    client = EbayClient.new

    products.each do |product|
      if product.ebay_item_id.nil? || product.stock_quantity <= 0
        # Unlist if no quantity or not listed
        client.unlist_item(product.ebay_item_id) if product.ebay_item_id
        product.update!(ebay_item_id: nil)
      else
        # Update quantity on eBay
        client.update_quantity(product.ebay_item_id, product.stock_quantity)
      end
    end
  rescue StandardError => e
    LOGGER.error "Stock update failed: #{e.message}"
    raise
  end
end
```

### 2. Main Application Code

```ruby
# app/amazon_order_fetcher.rb

require 'rest-client'
require 'jwt'
require 'oj'
require 'logger'
require 'config'

module AmazonOrderFetcher
  class << self
    def configure
      @config = Config.new(name: 'amazon_sp_api', environment: ENV['RACK_ENV'] || 'development')
      @logger = Logger.new($stderr)
      @logger.level = Logger::INFO

      # Initialize AWS S3 client if credentials are present
      if @config.params.dig(:aws_access_key_id) && @config.params.dig(:aws_secret_access_key)
        require 'aws-sdk-s3'
        @s3_client = Aws::S3::Client.new(
          region: @config.params.dig(:region) || 'us-east-1',
          access_key_id: @config.params.dig(:aws_access_key_id),
          secret_access_key: @config.params.dig(:aws_secret_access_key)
        )
      end

      self
    end

    def fetch_new_orders(start_date: nil, end_date: nil, marketplace_ids: nil)
      configure unless @config

      # Get access token
      access_token = get_access_token

      # Prepare request parameters
      params = {
        CreatedAfter: start_date || (Time.now - 30.days).iso8601, # Default to last 30 days
        CreatedBefore: end_date&.iso8601
      }

      params[:MarketplaceIds] = marketplace_ids if marketplace_ids

      # Make the API request
      orders = []
      next_token = nil
      begin
        response = make_sp_api_request(
          'GET',
          '/orders/v0/orders',
          access_token: access_token,
          params: params.merge({ 'NextToken' => next_token } if next_token)
        )

        orders += response['payload']['Orders'] || []

        next_token = response['payload']['NextToken']
      end while next_token

      orders
    rescue StandardError => e
      @logger.error "Failed to fetch orders: #{e.message}"
      @logger.error e.backtrace.join("\n")
      raise
    end

    def save_orders(orders, format: :json, storage: :memory)
      configure unless @config

      case format
      when :json
        data = orders.to_json
        case storage
        when :memory
          save_to_memory(data)
        when :s3
          save_to_s3(data)
        else
          raise "Unsupported storage option: #{storage}"
        end
      else
        raise "Unsupported format: #{format}"
      end
    end

    private

    def get_access_token
      configure unless @config

      # Generate JWT token
      now = Time.now.to_i
      jwt_payload = {
        'iss': @config.params.dig(:lwa_client_id),
        'scope': 'amazon.com::mws:feeds',
        'exp': now + 60 * 60, # 1 hour expiry
        'sub': 'cspaapi'
      }
      jwt = JWT.encode(jwt_payload, @config.params.dig(:lwa_client_secret), 'HS256')

      # Request access token
      response = RestClient.post(
        'https://api.amazon.com/auth/o2/token',
        {
          grant_type: 'refresh_token',
          refresh_token: @config.params.dig(:refresh_token),
          client_id: @config.params.dig(:lwa_client_id),
          client_secret: @config.params.dig(:lwa_client_secret)
        },
        { content_type: :url_encoded, accept: :json }
      )

      token_response = Oj.load(response.body)
      token_response['access_token']
    rescue RestClient::ExceptionWithResponse => e
      @logger.error "Failed to get access token: #{e.response}"
      raise
    end

    def make_sp_api_request(method, endpoint, access_token:, params: {})
      configure unless @config

      headers = {
        'x-amz-access-token': access_token,
        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
        'Accept': 'application/json'
      }

      url = "https://sellingpartnerapi-na.amazon.com#{endpoint}"

      response = RestClient::Request.execute(
        method: method,
        url: url,
        headers: headers,
        parameters: params
      )

      Oj.load(response)
    rescue RestClient::ExceptionWithResponse => e
      @logger.error "SP-API request failed: #{e.response}"
      raise
    end

    def save_to_memory(data)
      # In a real application, you might save to a database here
      @logger.info "Saving orders to memory (in-memory storage not implemented in this example)"
    end

    def save_to_s3(data)
      configure unless @config

      bucket_name = 'your-orders-bucket' # Replace with your bucket name
      file_name = "orders_#{Time.now.utc.iso8601.gsub(/[:.]/, '-')}.json"

      @s3_client.put_object(
        bucket: bucket_name,
        key: file_name,
        body: data
      )

      @logger.info "Saved orders to S3: s3://#{bucket_name}/#{file_name}"
    end
  end
end
```

```ruby
    @from_address = from_address

  def find_cheapest_rate
    shipment = EasyPost::Shipment.create(
```

## Реалізація

```ruby
# app/feed_generator.rb
require 'nokogiri'
require 'builder'
require 'active_support/core_ext/object/to_query'

class FeedGenerator
  attr_reader :items

  def initialize(items)
    @items = items
  end

  def generate_xml
    xml = Builder::XmlMarkup.new(indent: 2)
    xml.instruct! :xml, version: "1.0", encoding: "UTF-8"

    xml.rss version: "2.0", "xmlns:g" => "http://base.google.com/ns/1.0" do
      xml.channel do
        xml.title "Product Feed"
        xml.link "https://example.com"
        xml.description "Product feed for Google Merchant Center"

        items.each do |item|
          xml.item do
            xml.title item[:title]
            xml.link item[:url]
            xml.description item[:description]
            xml.g[:id] item[:id]
            xml.g[:price] item[:price].to_f.to_s # Google expects string values
            xml.g[:currency] "USD" # or your currency
            xml.g[:availability] item[:availability] || "in stock"

            # Optional fields
            if item[:image]
              xml.g[:image_link] item[:image]
            end

            if item[:brand]
              xml.g[:brand] item[:brand]
            end

            if item[:category]
              xml.g[:product_category] item[:category]
            end

            if item[:condition]
              xml.g[:condition] item[:condition]
            end
          end
        end
      end
    end

    xml.target!
  end

  def save_to_file(filename)
    File.open(filename, 'w') do |file|
      file.write(generate_xml)
    end
  end
end
```

## Реалізація

```ruby
# app/lib/ebay_synchronizer.rb
require 'ebay-api'
require 'logger'

class EbaySynchronizer
  def initialize(database_path, ebay_config)
    @logger = Logger.new(STDOUT)
    @logger.level = Logger::INFO

    # Ініціалізація eBay API
    @ebay = Ebay::API.new(
      app_id: ebay_config[:app_id],
      cert_id: ebay_config[:cert_id],
      dev_id: ebay_config[:dev_id],
      token: ebay_config[:token]
    )

    # Ініціалізація бази даних
    require 'sqlite3'
    @db = SQLite3::Database.new(database_path)
  end

  def sync_products
    @logger.info "Початок синхронізації товарів з eBay"

    # Отримуємо всі товари з бази, які потрібно виставити
    products = fetch_products_to_sync
    products.each do |product|
      sync_product(product)
    end

    @logger.info "Синхронізація завершена"
  end

  private

  def fetch_products_to_sync
    # Запит для отримання товарів, які потрібно виставити або оновити
    @db.execute(<<-SQL)
      SELECT * FROM products
      WHERE (ebay_item_id IS NULL OR updated_at > last_sync_time)
        AND quantity > 0
    SQL
  end

  def sync_product(product)
    @logger.info "Синхронізація товару: #{product['name']} (ID: #{product['id']})"

    begin
      if product['ebay_item_id'].nil?
        # Виставляємо новий товар
        item = create_ebay_item(product)
        update_product_with_ebay_id(product['id'], item[:item_id])
      else
        # Оновлюємо існуючий товар
        update_ebay_item(product)
      end

      @logger.info "Успішно синхронізовано товар: #{product['name']}"
    rescue => e
      @logger.error "Помилка при синхронізації товару #{product['name']}: #{e.message}"
      # Тут можна додати логіку для повторної спроби або відмітки про помилку
    end
  end

  def create_ebay_item(product)
    # Створюємо новий товар на eBay
    item_details = {
      title: product['name'],
      description: product['description'],
      category: product['category'],
      quantity: product['quantity'].to_i,
      price: product['price'].to_f,
      currency: 'USD', # або інша валюта за потребою
      shipping_cost: product['shipping_cost'].to_f,
      condition: 'NEW', # або інша умова
      returns_accepted: true,
      return_policy: {
        returns_within: 'Days_30',
        refund_method: 'MoneyBack',
        shipping_cost_paid_by: 'Buyer'
      }
    }

    response = @ebay.add_item(item_details)
    raise "eBay API помилка: #{response.error_message}" unless response.success?

    {
      item_id: response.item_id,
      listing_id: response.listing_id
    }
  end

  def update_ebay_item(product)
    # Оновлюємо існуючий товар на eBay
    item_details = {
      quantity: product['quantity'].to_i,
      price: product['price'].to_f
    }

    response = @ebay.update_item(
      item_id: product['ebay_item_id'],
      details: item_details
    )

    raise "eBay API помилка: #{response.error_message}" unless response.success?
  end

  def update_product_with_ebay_id(product_id, ebay_item_id)
    @db.execute(
      "UPDATE products SET ebay_item_id = ?, last_sync_time = datetime('now') WHERE id = ?",
      [ebay_item_id, product_id]
    )
  end
end
```

## Приклад використання

```ruby
gem 'active_model' # Для валідації даних (якщо потрібно)
```

## Реалізація коду

```ruby
# app/usps_address_validator.rb
require 'httparty'
require 'usps_address_validation'

class USPSAddressValidator
  USPS_API_URL = 'https://production.shippingapis.com/ShippingAPI.dll'.freeze
  USERNAME = ENV['USPS_USERNAME'] # Ваш USPS API username

  class InvalidAddressError < StandardError; end

  def initialize
    @usps = USPSAddressValidation.new(USERNAME)
  end

  # Основний метод для перевірки адреси
  def validate_and_normalize(address_params)
    validate_params(address_params)

    response = @usps.validate_address(
      address1: address_params[:address1],
      address2: address_params[:address2],
      city: address_params[:city],
      state: address_params[:state],
      zip5: address_params[:zip_code].to_s[0..4]
    )

    if response.success?
      normalize_response(response.address)
    else
      raise InvalidAddressError, "USPS validation failed: #{response.error}"
    end
  rescue USPSAddressValidation::USPSError => e
    raise InvalidAddressError, "USPS API error: #{e.message}"
  end

  private

  def validate_params(params)
    required_fields = [:address1, :city, :state, :zip_code]
    missing_fields = required_fields.select { |field| params[field].blank? }

    unless missing_fields.empty?
      raise ArgumentError, "Missing required fields: #{missing_fields.join(', ')}"
    end
  end

  def normalize_response(address)
    {
      address1: address[:Address1].strip,
      address2: address[:Address2]&.strip,
      city: address[:City].strip,
      state: address[:State].strip,
      zip_code: format_zip_code(address[:Zip5], address[:Zip4]),
      carrier_route: address[:CarrierRoute],
      delivery_point: address[:DeliveryPoint]
    }
  end

  def format_zip_code(zip5, zip4)
    if zip5.blank? && zip4.blank?
      nil
    elsif zip4.blank?
      zip5
    else
      "#{zip5}-#{zip4}"
    end
  end
end
```

## Приклад використання

```ruby
# example_usage.rb
require_relative 'app/usps_address_validator'

validator = USPSAddressValidator.new

begin
  # Приклад адреси для перевірки
  address_params = {
    address1: "123 main st",
    address2: "apt 4b",
    city: "San Francisco",
    state: "CA",
    zip_code: "94105"
  }

  normalized_address = validator.validate_and_normalize(address_params)
  puts "Normalized address:"
  puts normalized_address
rescue USPSAddressValidator::InvalidAddressError => e
  puts "Address validation failed: #{e.message}"
rescue ArgumentError => e
  puts "Invalid input: #{e.message}"
end
```


2. Створіть файл `.env` у кореневому каталозі проекту і додайте:


3. Для розробки можна використовувати тестовий сервер USPS:

   ```ruby
   USPS_API_URL = 'https://testing.shippingapis.com/ShippingAPI.dll'
   ```

## Особливості реалізації

1. Клас `USPSAddressValidator` інкапсулює всю логіку роботи з USPS API
2. Метод `validate_and_normalize` приймає хеш з параметрами адреси і повертає нормалізовану адресу
3. Реалізована базова валідація вхідних даних

# Ruby Implementation for Google Merchant Center XML Feed

Here's a complete solution for exporting a product catalogue as a Google Merchant Center XML feed:

## Gemfile

## Implementation

```ruby
require 'nokogiri'
require 'time'

# Product model (adjust according to your actual implementation)
class Product
  attr_accessor :id, :title, :description, :link, :image_link, :price, :brand,
                :mpn, :gtin, :availability, :condition, :product_type,
                :google_product_category, :sale_price, :sale_price_effective_date

  def initialize(attributes = {})
    attributes.each do |key, value|
      send("#{key}=", value) if respond_to?("#{key}=")
    end
  end
end

class XmlFeedGenerator
  # Example products - replace with your actual data source
  def self.example_products
    [
      Product.new(
        id: '12345',
        title: 'Premium Wireless Headphones',
        description: 'High-quality wireless headphones with noise cancellation',
        link: 'https://example.com/products/wireless-headphones',
        image_link: 'https://example.com/images/headphones.jpg',
        price: 199.99,
        brand: 'SoundMaster',
        mpn: 'SM-WH-1000',
        gtin: '012345678912',
        availability: 'in stock',
        condition: 'new',
        product_type: 'Headphones > Wireless',
        google_product_category: 'Electronics > Audio > Headphones',
        sale_price: 149.99,
        sale_price_effective_date: Time.now.to_s
      ),
      Product.new(
        id: '67890',
        title: 'Stainless Steel Water Bottle',
        description: 'Insulated water bottle that keeps drinks cold for 24 hours',
        link: 'https://example.com/products/water-bottle',
        image_link: 'https://example.com/images/bottle.jpg',
        price: 29.99,
        brand: 'HydroFlask',
        mpn: 'HF-B-32',
        gtin: '098765432109',
        availability: 'in stock',
        condition: 'new',
        product_type: 'Bottles > Water Bottles',
        google_product_category: 'Sports & Outdoors > Outdoor Recreation > Water Bottles'
      )
    ]
  end

  def self.generate_feed(products = example_products, feed_url = 'https://example.com/feed.xml')
    builder = Nokogiri::XML::Builder.new do |xml|
      xml.rss('version' => '2.0', 'xmlns:g' => 'http://base.google.com/ns/1.0') do
        xml.channel do
          xml.title('My Store Product Feed')
          xml.link(feed_url)
          xml.description('Product feed for My Store')
          xml.g.lastUpdate(Time.now.utc.iso8601)

          products.each do |product|
            xml.item do
              xml.title(product.title)
              xml.link(product.link)
              xml.description(product.description)
              xml.g.id(product.id)
              xml.g.image_link(product.image_link)
              xml.g.price(product.price.to_s)
              xml.g.brand(product.brand) if product.brand
              xml.g.mpn(product.mpn) if product.mpn
              xml.g.gtin(product.gtin) if product.gtin
              xml.g.availability(product.availability) if product.availability
              xml.g.condition(product.condition) if product.condition
              xml.g.product_type(product.product_type) if product.product_type
              xml.g.google_product_category(product.google_product_category) if product.google_product_category

              if product.sale_price
                xml.g.sale_price(product.sale_price.to_s)
                xml.g.sale_price_effective_date(product.sale_price_effective_date) if product.sale_price_effective_date
              end
            end
          end
        end
      end
    end

    builder.to_xml
  end

  # Save to file
  def self.save_to_file(products = example_products, filename = 'google_shopping_feed.xml')
    xml = generate_feed(products)
    File.write(filename, xml)
    puts "Feed generated and saved to #{filename}"
  end
end

# Example usage
if __FILE__ == $0
  # Uncomment to generate a sample feed
  # XmlFeedGenerator.save_to_file

  # Or generate with your own products:
  # products = ProductRepository.get_all_products # Your actual product data
  # XmlFeedGenerator.save_to_file(products, 'my_feed.xml')
end
```

## How to Use This Code

1. First, install the required gems:
   ```bash
   bundle install
   ```

2. Replace the example products in `example_products` method with your actual product data. You can:
   - Query your database
   - Read from a CSV/JSON file
   - Use an API to fetch products

3. To generate the feed:
   - For a sample feed: `XmlFeedGenerator.save_to_file`
   - For your actual products: `XmlFeedGenerator.save_to_file(your_products, 'custom_feed.xml')`

## Important Notes

1. This implementation follows Google's requirements for Merchant Center feeds:
   - Uses the RSS format with Google's namespace
   - Includes all required fields (id, title, description, link, price, availability)
   - Supports optional fields like brand, gtin, etc.

2. You'll need to:
   - Replace the example products with your actual product data
   - Ensure all required fields are populated
   - Validate your feed using Google's test tools

3. For large catalogs, consider:
   - Generating the feed periodically
   - Implementing incremental updates
   - Using a background job to generate the feed

4. Google's documentation for feed specifications can be found here: https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/160161

# Ruby код для генерації EAN-13 штрихкодів і створення PDF-етикеток

## Gemfile

```ruby
source 'https://rubygems.org'

# Основні геми для роботи
gem 'barby'              # Для генерації штрихкодів
gem 'barby-rbpdf'        # Для генерації PDF з штрихкодами
gem 'pry'                # Консоль для відладки (опціонально)
```

## Реалізація коду

```ruby
require 'barby'
require 'barby/barcode/ean_13'
require 'barby/outputter/rbpdf_outputter'

class BarcodeGenerator
  def initialize(output_file = 'barcodes.pdf')
    @output_file = output_file
  end

  # Генерація штрихкоду EAN-13 для single product
  def generate_barcode(product_code, options = {})
    # Перевірка валідності коду (EAN-13 повинен бути 13 цифр)
    raise ArgumentError, "EAN-13 code must be 13 digits" unless product_code.to_s.match?(/^\d{13}$/)

    barcode = Barby::Ean13.new(product_code)

    options = {
      xdim: 1,           # Ширина стрілок
      height: 100,       # Висота штрихкоду
      text: product_code # Чи показувати текст під штрихкодом
    }.merge(options)

    {
      barcode: barcode,
      options: options
    }

      margin: 10,             # Відступи (mm)
      columns: 2,             # Кількість колонок

    }.merge(options)

    Barby::Outputter::RBPdfOutputter.new(
      filename: @output_file,
      page_size: options[:page_size],
      margin: options[:margin],
      layout: "grid",
      columns: options[:columns],
      rows: options[:rows]

      products.each do |product_code, product_name|
        barcode_info = generate_barcode(product_code)

        # Створюємо PDF з штрихкодом і ім'ям товару
        outputter << barcode_info[:barcode].to_png(

            text: product_code,
            text_distance: 5

          font: 'Helvetica',
          size: 10,
          align: :center
        )
      end
    end

    puts "PDF етикетки успішно створено: #{@output_file}"
  end
```

# Ruby Implementation for EAN-13 Barcode Generation and PDF Label Printing

Here's a complete solution to generate EAN-13 barcodes and print them on PDF labels. I'll break it down into two parts: the Gemfile and the implementation.

## Gemfile

```ruby
source 'https://rubygems.org'

gem 'barby'
gem 'chunky_png'
gem 'prawn'
gem 'prawn-barby'
```

This Gemfile includes:
- `barby` - For generating barcodes
- `chunky_png` - PNG image processing (dependency of barby)
- `prawn` - For PDF generation
- `prawn-barby` - Integration between Prawn and Barby

## Implementation

```ruby
require 'barby'
require 'barby/barcode/ean_13'
require 'barby/barcode/upc_e'
require 'prawn'
require 'prawn/barby'

# Configuration for the labels
LABEL_CONFIG = {
  width: 100,       # mm
  height: 50,       # mm
  margin: 5,        # mm
  barcode_height: 30, # mm
  font_size: 8     # pt
}.freeze

class BarcodeLabelGenerator
  def initialize
    @products = []
  end

  # Add a product with its EAN-13 code
  def add_product(ean13_code, name, description = nil)
    # Validate EAN-13 code (must be 12 or 13 digits)
    ean13_code = ean13_code.to_s
    raise ArgumentError, "EAN-13 code must be 12 or 13 digits" unless ean13_code.match?(/^\d{12,13}$/)

    # If 12 digits, convert to EAN-13 (add check digit)
    if ean13_code.length == 12
      check_digit = calculate_ean13_check_digit(ean13_code)
      ean13_code = "#{ean13_code}#{check_digit}"
    end

    @products << {
      ean13: ean13_code,
      name: name,
      description: description
    }
  end

  # Generate a PDF with all the barcodes
  def generate_pdf(filename)
    Prawn::Document.generate(filename, page_size: [LABEL_CONFIG[:width] * 28.3465, LABEL_CONFIG[:height] * 28.3465]) do |pdf|
      pdf.font_families.update('Helvetica' => { normal: Rails.root.join('app/assets/fonts/Helvetica.ttf') }) if Rails.respond_to?(:root)
      pdf.font 'Helvetica'

      @products.each do |product|
        # Create barcode
        barcode = Barby::Ean13.new(product[:ean13])
        png = barcode.to_png({ height: LABEL_CONFIG[:barcode_height] * 28.3465 }) # Convert mm to points

        # Add label to PDF
        pdf.start_new_page unless pdf.starting_page_number == 1

        # Add barcode
        pdf.image png, at: [LABEL_CONFIG[:margin] * 28.3465, (LABEL_CONFIG[:height] - LABEL_CONFIG[:barcode_height] - 10) * 28.3465],
                   width: (LABEL_CONFIG[:width] - 2 * LABEL_CONFIG[:margin]) * 28.3465

        # Add text below barcode
        pdf.text product[:ean13], at: [LABEL_CONFIG[:margin] * 28.3465, 10 * 28.3465], size: LABEL_CONFIG[:font_size]
        pdf.text product[:name], at: [LABEL_CONFIG[:margin] * 28.3465, 5 * 28.3465], size: LABEL_CONFIG[:font_size]
        pdf.text product[:description], at: [LABEL_CONFIG[:margin] * 28.3465, 0 * 28.3465], size: LABEL_CONFIG[:font_size] if product[:description]
      end
    end
  end

  private

  # Calculate EAN-13 check digit
  def calculate_ean13_check_digit(ean12)
    sum = 0
    ean12.chars.each_with_index do |digit, index|
      factor = (index % 2 == 0) ? 1 : 3
      sum += digit.to_i * factor
    end
    (10 - (sum % 10)) % 10
  end
end

# Example usage
if __FILE__ == $0
  generator = BarcodeLabelGenerator.new

  # Add some products (with 12 or 13 digit EAN-13 codes)
  generator.add_product('501234567890', 'Product 1', 'Description for product 1')
  generator.add_product('50123456789', 'Product 2', 'Description for product 2') # Will be converted to 13 digits
  generator.add_product('5412345678901', 'Product 3', 'Description for product 3')

  # Generate PDF
  generator.generate_pdf('barcode_labels.pdf')
  puts "Barcode labels generated successfully! PDF saved as barcode_labels.pdf"
end
```

## How to Use

1. Install the required gems by running `bundle install`
2. Create a new Ruby file (e.g., `barcode_generator.rb`) and paste the implementation code
3. Run the script with `ruby barcode_generator.rb`
4. The script will generate a PDF file named `barcode_labels.pdf` with the barcodes

## Customization

You can adjust the label configuration by modifying the `LABEL_CONFIG` hash:
- `width` and `height`: Dimensions of the label in millimeters
- `margin`: Margin around the barcode in millimeters
- `barcode_height`: Height of the barcode in millimeters
- `font_size`: Font size for the text in points

The example shows how to add products with either 12-digit (which will be converted to 13-digit EAN-13) or 13-digit EAN-13 codes, along with product names and descriptions.

## Implementation

### 1. Background Job

```ruby
# app/jobs/import_product_prices_job.rb
class ImportProductPricesJob < ApplicationJob
  queue_as :default

  def perform(file_path)
    spreadsheet = Roo::Excelx.new(file_path) # for .xlsx files
    # spreadsheet = Roo::Excel.new(file_path) # for .xls files

    # Skip header row
    spreadsheet.each_row_offset(1) do |row|
      # Assuming columns: product_id, product_name, price, currency, etc.
      product_data = {
        product_id: row[0].to_s.strip,
        product_name: row[1].to_s.strip,
        price: row[2].to_f,
        currency: row[3].to_s.strip.upcase,
        # Add other fields as needed
        updated_at: DateTime.now
      }

      # Look up or create product
      product = Product.find_or_initialize_by(product_id: product_data[:product_id])
      product.assign_attributes(product_data)
      product.save!

      # You could also use upsert_all for bulk operations
      # Product.upsert_all([product_data], unique_by: :product_id)
    end
  end
end
```

### 8. Performance Considerations

For very large files, you might want to:

1. Add batch processing (process 100 rows at a time)
2. Add progress tracking

```ruby
# Example batch processing in the job
def perform(file_path)
  spreadsheet = Roo::Excelx.new(file_path)
  batch_size = 100
  row_number = 2 # skip header

  while row_number <= spreadsheet.last_row
    batch = []
    (0...batch_size).each do |i|
      break if row_number > spreadsheet.last_row
      row = spreadsheet.row(row_number + i)
      batch << process_row(row)
      row_number += 1
    end

    Product.import batch, on_duplicate_key_update: [:price, :currency, :updated_at]
  end
end

def process_row(row)
  {
    product_id: row[0].to_s.strip,
    product_name: row[1].to_s.strip,
    price: row[2].to_f,
    currency: row[3].to_s.strip.upcase,
    updated_at: DateTime.now
  }
end
```

```ruby
      },
```

### 1. Configuration (config/initializers/s3.rb)

### 2. Image Uploader Service

```ruby
# app/services/image_uploader.rb
require 'mini_magick'

class ImageUploader
  def initialize(file, product_id)
    @file = file
    @product_id = product_id
    @bucket = S3_BUCKET
  end

  def upload
    # Generate unique filename
    filename = generate_filename

    # Upload original image
    original_key = "products/#{@product_id}/originals/#{filename}"
    upload_to_s3(@file, original_key)

    # Generate and upload thumbnails
    generate_thumbnails(filename)

    # Return public URLs
    {
      original: public_url(original_key),
      thumbnail: public_url("products/#{@product_id}/thumbnails/thumb_#{filename}"),
      medium: public_url("products/#{@product_id}/thumbnails/medium_#{filename}")
    }
  end

  private

  def generate_filename
    "#{SecureRandom.uuid}.#{file_extension}"
  end

  def file_extension
    @file.original_filename.split('.').last.downcase
  end

  def upload_to_s3(file, key)
    obj = @bucket.object(key)
    obj.upload_file(file.path)
    obj.acl.put(acl: 'public-read') # Make the file publicly accessible
  end

  def generate_thumbnails(filename)
    # Thumbnail (small)
    thumbnail = MiniMagick::Image.open(@file.path)
    thumbnail.resize "200x200^"
    thumbnail.gravity 'center'
    thumbnail.extent "200x200"
    thumbnail.write "tmp/thumb_#{filename}"

    # Medium size
    medium = MiniMagick::Image.open(@file.path)
    medium.resize "800x800>"
    medium.write "tmp/medium_#{filename}"

    # Upload generated images
    upload_to_s3("tmp/thumb_#{filename}", "products/#{@product_id}/thumbnails/thumb_#{filename}")
    upload_to_s3("tmp/medium_#{filename}", "products/#{@product_id}/thumbnails/medium_#{filename}")

    # Cleanup temporary files
    File.delete("tmp/thumb_#{filename}") if File.exist?("tmp/thumb_#{filename}")
    File.delete("tmp/medium_#{filename}") if File.exist?("tmp/medium_#{filename}")
  end

  def public_url(key)
    "https://#{@bucket.name}.s3.amazonaws.com/#{key}"
  end
end
```

# Ruby Implementation for Abandoned Cart Reminder Emails via Klaviyo

Here's a complete solution for sending abandoned cart reminder emails through Klaviyo when users leave items in their cart.

## Gemfile

## Implementation

```ruby
# app/abandoned_cart_reminder.rb
require 'klaviyo-client'
require 'dotenv/load'

class AbandonedCartReminder
  def initialize
    @klaviyo = Klaviyo::Client.new(
      api_key: ENV['KLAVIYO_API_KEY'],
      private_key: ENV['KLAVIYO_PRIVATE_KEY']
    )
  end

  # Trigger when a user leaves the cart page
  def track_cart_abandonment(user_id, cart_items, total_price, time_spent)
    # Track the event in Klaviyo
    @klaviyo.track(
      user_id: user_id,
      event: 'Abandoned Cart',
      properties: {
        cart_items: cart_items,
        total_price: total_price,
        time_spent: time_spent,
        timestamp: Time.now.utc.iso8601
      }
    )

    # Optionally add the user to a Klaviyo list for segmentation
    add_user_to_abandoned_cart_list(user_id)
  end

  private

  def add_user_to_abandoned_cart_list(user_id)
    @klaviyo.list_subscribe(
      list_id: ENV['KLAVIYO_ABANDONED_CART_LIST_ID'],
      profiles: [{ email: user_id }] # Assuming user_id is an email
    )
  end
end
```

### 3. Create the Product model

```ruby
# app/models/product.rb
class Product < ApplicationRecord
  # Define your product attributes here
  # These should match the fields you want to manage in WooCommerce

  validates :name, presence: true
  validates :sku, uniqueness: true, allow_nil: true

  def sync_to_woocommerce
    woocommerce_product = {
      name: name,
      slug: name.parameterize,
      type: 'simple',
      sku: sku,
      manage_stock: manage_stock?,
      stock_quantity: stock_quantity,
      regular_price: regular_price.to_s,
      sale_price: sale_price.to_s,
      description: description,
      status: status
    }

    # Handle categories
    if categories.present?
      woocommerce_product[:categories] = categories.map { |cat| { id: cat } }
    end

    # Handle tags
    if tags.present?
      woocommerce_product[:tags] = tags.map { |tag| { id: tag } }
    end

    # Create or update the product
    if woocommerce_id.present?
      WooCommerce.put("products/#{woocommerce_id}", woocommerce_product)
    else
      response = WooCommerce.post('products', woocommerce_product)
      self.update(woocommerce_id: response.body['id'])
    end
  rescue StandardError => e
    Rails.logger.error "Error syncing product to WooCommerce: #{e.message}"
    false
  end

  def fetch_from_woocommerce
    return false unless woocommerce_id.present?

    response = WooCommerce.get("products/#{woocommerce_id}")
    product_data = response.body

    update(
      name: product_data['name'],
      sku: product_data['sku'],
      price: product_data['price'],
      stock_quantity: product_data['stock_quantity'],
      status: product_data['status'],
      description: product_data['description'],
      regular_price: product_data['regular_price'],
      sale_price: product_data['sale_price'],
      manage_stock: product_data['manage_stock'],
      # Update categories and tags if needed
    )
  rescue StandardError => e
    Rails.logger.error "Error fetching product from WooCommerce: #{e.message}"
    false
  end

  def delete_from_woocommerce
    return false unless woocommerce_id.present?

    WooCommerce.delete("products/#{woocommerce_id}")
    self.update(woocommerce_id: nil)
  rescue StandardError => e
    Rails.logger.error "Error deleting product from WooCommerce: #{e.message}"
    false
  end
end
```

```ruby
# nova_poshta_client.rb
require 'httparty'
require 'json'

class NovaPoshtaClient
  include HTTParty

  BASE_URL = 'https://api.novaposhta.ua/v2/Json/'.freeze

  attr_reader :api_key

  def initialize(api_key)
    @api_key = api_key
  end

  # Create a new waybill (express invoice)
  def create_waybill(waybill_data)
    response = self.class.post(
      BASE_URL + 'createWaybill',
      body: create_request_body(waybill_data),
      headers: { 'Content-Type' => 'application/json' }
    )

    parse_response(response)
  end

  private

  def create_request_body(waybill_data)
    {
      'modelName' => 'Waybill',
      'calledMethod' => 'createWaybill',
      'methodProperties' => {
        'WayBillData' => waybill_data
      },
      'apiKey' => api_key
    }.to_json
  end

  def parse_response(response)
    parsed = JSON.parse(response.body)
    if parsed['success']
      parsed['data']
    else
      raise StandardError, parsed['errors'].join(', ')
    end
  end
end
```

Here's a complete solution that includes a Gemfile and implementation code:

## Gemfile

```ruby
source 'https://rubygems.org'

gem 'uber-direct'  # Official Uber Direct Ruby client
gem 'httparty'     # For making HTTP requests (if needed)
gem 'dotenv'       # For environment variable management
```

## Implementation

```ruby
require 'uber-direct'
require 'dotenv'

# Load environment variables from .env file
Dotenv.load

class OrderDeliveryService
  def initialize
    @client = UberDirect::Client.new(
      access_token: ENV['UBER_ACCESS_TOKEN'],
      server_token: ENV['UBER_SERVER_TOKEN']
    )
  end

  # Books a delivery courier for a ready order
  # @param delivery_details [Hash] Details about the delivery
  # @option delivery_details [String] :pickup_latitude Latitude of pickup location
  # @option delivery_details [String] :pickup_longitude Longitude of pickup location
  # @option delivery_details [String] :dropoff_latitude Latitude of dropoff location
  # @option delivery_details [String] :dropoff_longitude Longitude of dropoff location
  # @option delivery_details [String] :pickup_phone_number Phone number for pickup
  # @option delivery_details [String] :dropoff_phone_number Phone number for dropoff
  # @option delivery_details [String] :pickup_name Name for pickup
  # @option delivery_details [String] :dropoff_name Name for dropoff
  # @option delivery_details [String] :pickup_instructions Instructions for pickup
  # @option delivery_details [String] :dropoff_instructions Instructions for dropoff
  # @option delivery_details [String] :weight Weight of package in pounds
  # @option delivery_details [String] :value Value of package
  # @return [Hash] Uber Direct API response
  def book_delivery(delivery_details)
    # Validate required parameters
    required_params = %i[
      pickup_latitude pickup_longitude dropoff_latitude dropoff_longitude
      pickup_phone_number dropoff_phone_number pickup_name dropoff_name
    ]

    missing_params = required_params.reject { |param| delivery_details.key?(param) }
    unless missing_params.empty?
      raise ArgumentError, "Missing required parameters: #{missing_params.join(', ')}"
    end

    # Request a quote
    quote_response = @client.quote(
      pickup_latitude: delivery_details[:pickup_latitude],
      pickup_longitude: delivery_details[:pickup_longitude],
      dropoff_latitude: delivery_details[:dropoff_latitude],
      dropoff_longitude: delivery_details[:dropoff_longitude],
      pickup_phone_number: delivery_details[:pickup_phone_number],
      dropoff_phone_number: delivery_details[:dropoff_phone_number],
      pickup_name: delivery_details[:pickup_name],
      dropoff_name: delivery_details[:dropoff_name],
      pickup_instructions: delivery_details[:pickup_instructions],
      dropoff_instructions: delivery_details[:dropoff_instructions],
      weight: delivery_details[:weight],
      value: delivery_details[:value]
    )

    # Handle the quote response
    if quote_response&.dig('error') || quote_response['error']
      raise "Failed to get quote: #{quote_response&.dig('error', 'message') || quote_response['error']['message']}"
    end

    # Create the delivery request
    delivery_request = {
      pickup_latitude: delivery_details[:pickup_latitude],
      pickup_longitude: delivery_details[:pickup_longitude],
      dropoff_latitude: delivery_details[:dropoff_latitude],
      dropoff_longitude: delivery_details[:dropoff_longitude],
      pickup_phone_number: delivery_details[:pickup_phone_number],
      dropoff_phone_number: delivery_details[:dropoff_phone_number],
      pickup_name: delivery_details[:pickup_name],
      dropoff_name: delivery_details[:dropoff_name],
      pickup_instructions: delivery_details[:pickup_instructions],
      dropoff_instructions: delivery_details[:dropoff_instructions],
      weight: delivery_details[:weight],
      value: delivery_details[:value],
      quote_id: quote_response['quote']['id']
    }

    # Create the delivery
    @client.create_delivery(delivery_request)
  end
end
```

Настройка Elasticsearch Создайте файл `config/initializers/elasticsearch.rb`: ```ruby # config/initializers/elasticsearch.rb require 'elasticsearch/model' Elasticsearch::Model.client = Elasticsearch::Client.new( url: ENV.fetch('ELASTICSEARCH_URL', 'http://localhost:9200'), retry_on_failure: 5, log: true ) ``` ### 2. Модель Product (группа) ```ruby # app/models/product.rb class Product < ApplicationRecord include Elasticsearch::Model include Elasticsearch::Model::Callbacks # Атрибуты модели belongs_to :category has_many :product_options # Настройки для Elasticsearch settings index: { number_of_shards: 1, number_of_replicas: 1 } do mapping dynamic: 'false' do indexes :title, type: 'text', analyzer: 'standard' indexes :description, type: 'text', analyzer: 'standard' indexes :price, type: 'float' indexes :category_id, type: 'integer' indexes :brand, type: 'keyword' indexes :in_stock, type: 'boolean' indexes :created_at, type: 'date' indexes :updated_at, type: 'date' end end # Метод для реиндексации def self.reindex __elasticsearch__.create_index!(force: true) find_in_batches do |batch| __elasticsearch__.import(batch, refresh: true) end end # Метод для поиска с фильтрами и фасетами def self.search(query, filters = {}) search_definition = { query: { bool: { must: [ { multi_match: { query: query, fields: ['title^3', 'description'], fuzziness: 'AUTO' }} ], filter: [] } }, aggs: { brands: { terms: { field: 'brand' } }, categories: { terms: { field: 'category_id' } }, price_ranges: { range: { field: 'price', ranges: [ { to: 50.0 }, { from: 50.0, to: 100.0 }, { from: 100.0, to: 200.0 }, { from: 200.0 } ] } }, in_stock: { terms: { field: 'in_stock' } } } } # Добавляем фильтры filters.each do |key, values| if key == 'price_range' price_range = values search_definition[:query][:bool][:filter] << { range: { price: { gte: price_range[:min], lte: price_range[:max] } } } else search_definition[:query][:bool][:filter] << { terms: { key.to_s => values } } end end __elasticsearch__.search(search_definition) end end ``` ### 3. Контроллер для поиска ```ruby # app/controllers/search_controller.rb class SearchController < ApplicationController def products query = params[:query] || '*' filters = { category_id: params[:category_ids], brand: params[:brands], in_stock: params[:in_stock], price_range: { min: params[:min_price].to_f, max: params[:max_price].to_f } }.compact results = Product.search(query, filters) @products = results.hits.hits.map { |hit| Product.new(hit['_source']) } @facets = { brands: results.aggregations['brands'].buckets, categories: results.aggregations['categories'].buckets, price_ranges: results.aggregations['price_ranges'].buckets, in_stock: results.aggregations['in_stock'].buckets } respond_to do |format| format.html format.json { render json: @products } end end end ``` ### 4. Collaborative Filtering Model ```ruby # collaborative_filtering.rb require 'matrix' require 'set' class CollaborativeFilter attr_reader :user_items, :item_users, :user_similarity def initialize @user_items = {} # { user_id => Set[item_id, ...] } @item_users = {} # { item_id => Set[user_id, ...] } @user_similarity = {} # { user_id => { other_user_id => similarity_score } } end # Add a user's order to the dataset def add_order(user_id, item_ids) # Add to user_items @user_items[user_id] ||= Set.new @user_items[user_id].merge(item_ids) # Add to item_users item_ids.each do |item_id| @item_users[item_id] ||= Set.new @item_users[item_id].add(user_id) end end # Calculate similarity between two users using Jaccard index def jaccard_similarity(user1, user2) intersection = @user_items[user1] & @user_items[user2] union = @user_items[user1] | @user_items[user2] union.empty? ? 0.0 : intersection.size.to_f / union.size end # Precompute similarity scores for all users def compute_similarities user_ids = @user_items.keys user_ids.each do |user1| @user_similarity[user1] = {} user_ids.each do |user2| next if user1 == user2 similarity = jaccard_similarity(user1, user2) @user_similarity[user1][user2] = similarity end end end # Get recommendations for a user def recommend(user_id, n = 5) return [] unless @user_similarity[user_id] # Get similar users similar_users = @user_similarity[user_id].sort_by { |_, sim| -sim }.to_h # Collect all items from similar users, excluding items the user already has recommended_items = @user_items[user_id] ? {} : {} similar_users.each do |other_user, _| next unless other_user @user_items[other_user].each do |item_id| next if recommended_items.key?(item_id) next if @user_items[user_id]&.include?(item_id) # Initialize or increment score recommended_items[item_id] ||= 0 recommended_items[item_id] += @user_similarity[user_id][other_user] end end # Sort by score and return top n recommendations recommended_items.sort_by { |_, score| -score }.map { |item_id, _| item_id }.first(n) end end ``` ### 2. # app.rb
```ruby
require 'httparty'

  include HTTParty
```
