## Implementation

### 1. CommerceML Service (app/services/commerce_ml_service.rb)

```ruby
require 'nokogiri'
require 'builder'

class CommerceMLService
  COMMERCEML_NAMESPACE = 'http://www.1c.ru/CommerceML'
  COMMERCEML_SCHEMA = 'http://www.1c.ru/CommerceML/commerceML.xsd'

  def initialize(remote_url: nil, api_key: nil)
    @remote_url = remote_url || Rails.application.credentials.dig(:commerce_ml, :remote_url)
    @api_key = api_key || Rails.application.credentials.dig(:commerce_ml, :api_key)
  end

  def exchange_data
    # This would typically be triggered by a scheduled job
    export_products
    export_orders
    import_products
    import_prices
  end

  def export_products
    products = Product.for_export
    xml = build_export_xml(products, 'Products')
    send_request(xml, 'export_products')
  end

  def export_orders
    orders = Order.for_export
    xml = build_export_xml(orders, 'Orders')
    send_request(xml, 'export_orders')
  end

  def import_products
    response = get_commerce_ml_data('import_products')
    parse_import_response(response, 'Products')
  end

  def import_prices
    response = get_commerce_ml_data('import_prices')
    parse_import_response(response, 'Prices')
  end

  private

  def build_export_xml(records, record_type)
    xml = Builder::XmlMarkup.new(indent: 2)
    xml.instruct! :xml, version: '1.0', encoding: 'UTF-8'
    xml.tag!('CommerceML', 'xmlns' => COMMERCEML_NAMESPACE, 'xmlns:xsi' => 'http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance', 'xsi:schemaLocation' => "#{COMMERCEML_NAMESPACE} #{COMMERCEML_SCHEMA}") do
      xml.tag!(record_type) do
        records.each do |record|
          xml.tag!('КоммерческаяИнформация') do
            if record.is_a?(Product)
              build_product_xml(xml, record)
            elsif record.is_a?(Order)
              build_order_xml(xml, record)
            end
          end
        end
      end
    end
    xml.target!
  end

  def build_product_xml(xml, product)
    xml.tag!('Каталог', 'РеквизитТипа' => 'Справочник.Номенклатура') do
      xml.tag!('Наименование') { xml.text! product.name }
      xml.tag!('Артикул') { xml.text! product.sku }
      xml.tag!('Описание') { xml.text! product.description }
      xml.tag!('Группы') do
        xml.tag!('Группа', 'ИД' => product.category.id, 'Наименование' => product.category.name)
      end
      xml.tag!('Цены') do
        xml.tag!('Цена', 'ТипЦены' => 'Розничная', 'ЦенаЗаЕдиницу' => product.price.to_f)
      end
    end
  end

  def build_order_xml(xml, order)
    xml.tag!('ЗаказПоставщику', 'Номер' => order.number, 'Дата' => order.created_at.to_date, 'Комментарий' => order.notes) do
      xml.tag!('Контрагент') do
        xml.tag!('Наименование') { xml.text! order.customer.name }
        xml.tag!('Адрес') { xml.text! order.customer.address }
      end
      xml.tag!('Товары') do
        order.order_items.each do |item|
          xml.tag!('Товар', 'ИД' => item.product.sku, 'Наименование' => item.product.name, 'Количество' => item.quantity.to_i, 'Цена' => item.price.to_f, 'Сумма' => (item.quantity * item.price).to_f)
        end
      end
    end
  end

  def send_request(xml, action)
    response = RestClient.post(
      @remote_url,
      xml,
      {
        content_type: 'text/xml; charset=utf-8',
        accept: 'text/xml',
        'Authorization' => "Bearer #{@api_key}" if @api_key
      }
    )
    response
  end

  def get_commerce_ml_data(action)
    response = RestClient.get(
      @remote_url,
      {
        params: { action: action },
        accept: 'text/xml',
        'Authorization' => "Bearer #{@api_key}" if @api_key
      }
    )
    response.body
  end

  def parse_import_response(response, response_type)
    doc = Nokogiri::XML(response)
    case response_type
    when 'Products'
      parse_products(doc)
    when 'Prices'
      parse_prices(doc)
    end
  end

  def parse_products(doc)
    products = []
    doc.xpath('//ns:Каталог', 'ns' => COMMERCEML_NAMESPACE).each do |catalog|
      name = catalog.at_xpath('ns:Наименование', 'ns' => COMMERCEML_NAMESPACE)&.text
      sku = catalog.at_xpath('ns:Артикул', 'ns' => COMMERCEML_NAMESPACE)&.text
      description = catalog.at_xpath('ns:Описание', 'ns' => COMMERCEML_NAMESPACE)&.text
      category = catalog.at_xpath('ns:Группы/ns:Группа', 'ns' => COMMERCEML_NAMESPACE) do |group|
        { id: group['ИД'], name: group.at_xpath('ns:Наименование', 'ns' => COMMERCEML_NAMESPACE)&.text }
      end

      products << {
        name: name,
        sku: sku,
        description: description,
        category: category,
        updated_at: Time.current
      }
    end
    products
  end

  def parse_prices(doc)
    prices = []
    doc.xpath('//ns:Цен', 'ns' => COMMERCEML_NAMESPACE).each do |price|
      sku = price.at_xpath('ns:Товар/ns:ИД', 'ns' => COMMERCEML_NAMESPACE)&.text
      price_value = price.at_xpath('ns:Цен/ns:ЦенаЗаЕдиницу', 'ns' => COMMERCEML_NAMESPACE)&.text&.to_f
      price_type = price.at_xpath('ns:ТипЦены', 'ns' => COMMERCEML_NAMESPACE)&.text

      prices << {
        sku: sku,
        value: price_value,
        price_type: price_type,
        updated_at: Time.current
      }
    end
    prices
  end
end
```

    products_data.each do |product_data|
      category = Category.find_or_initialize_by(id: product_data[:category][:id])
      category.update(name: product_data[:category][:name]) if category.new_record?

      product = find_or_initialize_by(sku: product_data[:sku])
      product.assign_attributes(
        name: product_data[:name],
        description: product_data[:description],
        category: category,
        updated_at: product_data[:updated_at]
      )
      product.save!
    end
  end

```ruby
# app.rb
require 'httparty'
require 'dotenv'
require 'json'

# Load environment variables
Dotenv.load

class GlovoAPI
  include HTTParty
  base_uri 'https://apidist.glovoy.com'

  def initialize
    @access_token = ENV['GLOVO_ACCESS_TOKEN']
    @api_key = ENV['GLOVO_API_KEY']
    @store_id = ENV['GLOVO_STORE_ID']
    @base_headers = {
      'Authorization' => "Bearer #{@access_token}",
      'X-API-KEY' => @api_key,
      'Content-Type' => 'application/json'
    }
  end

  # Get available delivery times
  def get_delivery_times
    response = self.class.get(
      '/v2/delivery-times',
      headers: @base_headers,
      query: { store_id: @store_id }
    )
    handle_response(response)
  end

  # Create an order
  def create_order(order_params)
    response = self.class.post(
      '/v2/orders',
      headers: @base_headers,
      body: order_params.to_json,
      query: { store_id: @store_id }
    )
    handle_response(response)
  end

  # Track an order
  def track_order(order_id)
    response = self.class.get(
      "/v2/orders/#{order_id}",
      headers: @base_headers
    )
    handle_response(response)
  end

  # Cancel an order
  def cancel_order(order_id)
    response = self.class.delete(
      "/v2/orders/#{order_id}",
      headers: @base_headers
    )
    handle_response(response)
  end

  private

  def handle_response(response)
    if response.success?
      JSON.parse(response.body)
    else
      raise "Glovo API Error: #{response.code} - #{response.message}"
    end
  end
end

        }

```ruby
# app/services/keycrm_client.rb
require 'httparty'

class KeyCRMClient
  include HTTParty

  # Initialize the client with API credentials
  def initialize
    @options = Rails.application.config.keycrm
    @base_url = @options[:base_url]
    @timeout = @options[:timeout]
  end

  # Authenticate with KeyCRM
  def authenticate
    headers = {
      'Authorization' => "Basic #{Base64.strict_encode64("#{@options[:api_key]}:#{@options[:api_secret]}")}"
    }

    self.class.base_uri(@base_url)
    self.class.default_options.merge(timeout: @timeout, headers: headers)
  end

  # Sync an order to KeyCRM
  def sync_order(order)
    authenticate

    response = self.class.post('/orders', body: order.to_json, headers: { 'Content-Type' => 'application/json' })

    if response.success?
      { success: true, data: response.parsed_response }
    else
      { success: false, error: response.parsed_response || response.message }
    end
  end

  # Get an order from KeyCRM
  def get_order(order_id)
    authenticate

    response = self.class.get("/orders/#{order_id}")

    if response.success?
      { success: true, data: response.parsed_response }
    else
      { success: false, error: response.parsed_response || response.message }
    end
  end

  # Update an order in KeyCRM
  def update_order(order_id, order_data)
    authenticate

    response = self.class.put("/orders/#{order_id}", body: order_data.to_json, headers: { 'Content-Type' => 'application/json' })

    if response.success?
      { success: true, data: response.parsed_response }
    else
      { success: false, error: response.parsed_response || response.message }
    end
  end
end
```

```ruby
# lib/bas_order_exporter.rb
require 'httpclient'
require 'nokogiri'
require 'uuidtools'
require 'json'
require 'xmlsimple'
require 'logger'
require 'rescue'

class BasOrderExporter
  BAS_API_URL = 'https://api.bas.com.ua/orders'.freeze
  BUSINESS_ID = ENV['BAS_BUSINESS_ID'] || 'YOUR_BUSINESS_ID'
  API_KEY = ENV['BAS_API_KEY'] || 'YOUR_API_KEY'

  def initialize
    @logger = Logger.new(STDOUT)
    @logger.level = Logger::INFO
    @client = HTTPClient.new
  end

  # Main method to export order to BAS
  # @param order_data [Hash] Hash containing order information
  # @return [Hash] Response from BAS API
  def export_order(order_data)
    Rescue.try do
      validate_order_data(order_data)
      generate_bas_xml(order_data)
    rescue StandardError => e
      @logger.error "Error in export_order: #{e.message}"
      raise
    end
  end

  private

  # Validate the order data before processing
  # @param order_data [Hash] Order data to validate
  # @raise [ArgumentError] if required fields are missing
  def validate_order_data(order_data)
    required_fields = %w[order_number date customer_name items total_amount]

    missing_fields = required_fields.reject { |f| order_data.key?(f) }
    unless missing_fields.empty?
      raise ArgumentError, "Missing required fields: #{missing_fields.join(', ')}"
    end

    if order_data[:items].empty?
      raise ArgumentError, "Order must contain at least one item"
    end
  end

  # Generate BAS-compatible XML from order data
  # @param order_data [Hash] Validated order data
  # @return [String] XML string for BAS API
  def generate_bas_xml(order_data)
    builder = Nokogiri::XML::Builder.new do |xml|
      xml.order do
        xml.order_number(order_data[:order_number] || UUIDTools::UUID.timestamp_create.to_s)
        xml.date(order_data[:date])

        xml.customer do
          xml.name(order_data[:customer_name])
          xml.tax_code(order_data[:customer_tax_code] || '')
        end

        xml.items do
          order_data[:items].each do |item|
            xml.item do
              xml.name(item[:name] || '')
              xml.quantity(item[:quantity].to_s)
              xml.price(item[:price].to_s)
              xml.tax_rate(item[:tax_rate] || '20') # Default to 20% VAT
              xml.total(item[:total].to_s)
            end
          end
        end

        xml.total_amount(order_data[:total_amount].to_s)
        xml.payment_method(order_data[:payment_method] || 'cash')
        xml.delivery_method(order_data[:delivery_method] || 'self_pickup')
        xml.notes(order_data[:notes] || '')
      end
    end

    builder.to_xml
  end

  # Send the order to BAS API
  # @param xml_data [String] XML data to send
  # @return [Hash] Response from BAS API
  def send_to_bas(xml_data)
    headers = {
      'Content-Type' => 'application/xml',
      'X-Business-Id' => BUSINESS_ID,
      'X-API-Key' => API_KEY
    }

    response = @client.post(BAS_API_URL, xml_data, headers)

    unless response.success?
      error_msg = "BAS API request failed: #{response.status_code} - #{response.body}"
      @logger.error error_msg
      raise StandardError, error_msg
    end

    parse_bas_response(response.body)
  end

  # Parse the response from BAS API
  # @param response_body [String] Response body from BAS API
  # @return [Hash] Parsed response data
  def parse_bas_response(response_body)
    # This would parse the XML response from BAS
    # Implementation depends on BAS API response format
    # For this example, we'll return a simple hash
    {
      success: true,
      order_id: 'BAS-12345',
      status: 'Received',
      message: 'Order successfully exported to BAS'
    }
  end
end
```

## Implementation

### 1. CommerceML Service

```ruby
# app/services/commerce_ml_service.rb
class CommerceMLService
  def initialize(shop_id, login, password, base_url: 'http://localhost:8080')
    @shop_id = shop_id
    @login = login
    @password = password
    @base_url = base_url
  end

  def fetch_catalogue
    response = HTTParty.post(
      "#{@base_url}/hs/commerce_ml.php",
      body: build_initialization_request,
      headers: { 'Content-Type' => 'application/xml' }
    )

    unless response.success?
      raise "Failed to fetch catalogue: #{response.body}"
    end

    parse_catalogue_response(response.body)
  end

  def send_order(order_data)
    response = HTTParty.post(
      "#{@base_url}/hs/commerce_ml.php",
      body: build_order_request(order_data),
      headers: { 'Content-Type' => 'application/xml' }
    )

    unless response.success?
      raise "Failed to send order: #{response.body}"
    end

    parse_order_response(response.body)
  end

  private

  def build_initialization_request
    Nokogiri::XML::Builder.new do |xml|
      xml.CommerceML {
        xml.@version "2.07"
        xml.@encoding "UTF-8"

        xml.Headers {
          xml.Version {
            xml.@Major "2"
            xml.@Minor "07"
          }
          xml.Terminal {
            xml.@ID "RubyShop"
            xml.@Description "Ruby CommerceML Client"
          }
          xml.Name {
            xml.@Type "Client"
            xml.@Value "RubyShop"
          }
          xml.Password {
            xml.@Value @password
          }
          xml.@Date "#{Time.now.strftime('%Y%m%d%H%M%S')}"
          xml.@Number "1"
          xml.@Mode "Pull"
          xml.@Directory ""
          xml.@FileLimit "100"
          xml.@Convert "True"
          xml.@Lock "False"
          xml.@Service "False"
          xml.@TestMode "False"
          xml.@TypeOperation "Catalog"
        }
      }
    end.to_xml
  end

  def build_order_request(order_data)
    Nokogiri::XML::Builder.new do |xml|
      xml.CommerceML {
        xml.@version "2.07"
        xml.@encoding "UTF-16"

        xml.Headers {
          xml.Version {
            xml.@Major "2"
            xml.@Minor "07"
          }
          xml.Terminal {
            xml.@ID "RubyShop"
            xml.@Description "Ruby CommerceML Client"
          }
          xml.Name {
            xml.@Type "Client"
            xml.@Value "RubyShop"
          }
          xml.Password {
            xml.@Value @password
          }
          xml.@Date "#{Time.now.strftime('%Y%m%d%H%M%S')}"
          xml.@Number "1"
          xml.@Mode "Pull"
          xml.@Directory ""
          xml.@FileLimit "100"
          xml.@Convert "True"
          xml.@Lock "False"
          xml.@Service "False"
          xml.@TestMode "False"
          xml.@TypeOperation "Catalog"
        }

        xml.Catalog {
          xml.@Mode "Full"
          xml.@UpdateTime "#{Time.now.strftime('%Y%m%d%H%M%S')}"
          xml.CatalogGroup {
            xml.@ParentGroupID "0"
            xml.@ID "Orders"
            xml.@Name "Заказы"
            xml.@Description "Файл с заказами"

            order_data.each do |order|
              xml.CatalogItem {
                xml.@ID order[:id]
                xml.@ParentGroupID "Orders"
                xml.@Article "Order#{order[:id]}"
                xml.@Name "Order ##{order[:id]}"
                xml.@Description "Order from #{order[:created_at]}"

                xml.Property {
                  xml.@Name "CustomerName"
                  xml.@Value order[:customer_name]
                }

                xml.Property {
                  xml.@Name "CustomerEmail"
                  xml.@Value order[:customer_email]
                }

                xml.Property {
                  xml.@Name "DeliveryAddress"
                  xml.@Value order[:delivery_address]
                }

                xml.Property {
                  xml.@Name "TotalAmount"
                  xml.@Value order[:total_amount]
                }

                order[:items].each do |item|
                  xml.CatalogItem {
                    xml.@ID "Item#{item[:id]}"
                    xml.@ParentGroupID order[:id]
                    xml.@Article item[:product_code]
                    xml.@Name item[:product_name]
                    xml.@Description item[:product_description]
                    xml.@Quantity item[:quantity]
                    xml.@Price item[:price]
                    xml.@Sum item[:quantity] * item[:price]
                  }
                end
              }
            end
          }
        }
      }
    end.to_xml
  end

  def parse_catalogue_response(xml_string)
    doc = Nokogiri::XML(xml_string)

    products = []
    doc.search('//CatalogItem').each do |item|
      product = {
        id: item['ID'],
        name: item.at_xpath('Name')&.text,
        description: item.at_xpath('Description')&.text,
        price: item.at_xpath('Price')&.text&.to_f,
        quantity: item.at_xpath('Quantity')&.text&.to_i,
        article: item['Article']
      }

      properties = {}
      item.search('Property').each do |prop|
        properties[prop['Name']] = prop['Value']
      end

      products << product.merge(properties)
    end

    products
  end

  def parse_order_response(xml_string)
    doc = Nokogiri::XML(xml_string)

    orders = []
    doc.search('//CatalogItem').each do |item|
      next unless item.at_xpath('Property[@Name="CustomerName"]')

      order = {
        id: item['ID'],
        customer_name: item.at_xpath('Property[@Name="CustomerName"]')['Value'],
        customer_email: item.at_xpath('Property[@Name="CustomerEmail"]')['Value'],
        delivery_address: item.at_xpath('Property[@Name="DeliveryAddress"]')['Value'],
        total_amount: item.at_xpath('Property[@Name="TotalAmount"]')['Value']&.to_f,
        created_at: item.at_xpath('Property[@Name="CreatedAt"]')&.text
      }

      items = []
      item.search('CatalogItem').each do |order_item|
        items << {
          id: order_item['ID'],
          product_code: order_item['Article'],
          product_name: order_item.at_xpath('Name')&.text,
          product_description: order_item.at_xpath('Description')&.text,
          quantity: order_item.at_xpath('Quantity')&.text&.to_i,
          price: order_item.at_xpath('Price')&.text&.to_f
        }
      end

      orders << order.merge(items: items)
    end

    orders
  end
end
```

### 2. Model for 1C Integration

```ruby
# app/models/one_c_integration.rb
class OneCIntegration
  def self.sync_catalogue
    service = CommerceMLService.new(
      ENV['ONE_C_SHOP_ID'],
      ENV['ONE_C_LOGIN'],
      ENV['ONE_C_PASSWORD'],
      base_url: ENV['ONE_C_BASE_URL']
    )

    products = service.fetch_catalogue

    products.each do |product|
      Product.where(article: product[:article]).first_or_create do |p|
        p.name = product[:name]
        p.description = product[:description]
        p.price = product[:price]
        p.quantity = product[:quantity]
      end
    end
  end

  def self.send_orders
    service = CommerceMLService.new(
      ENV['ONE_C_SHOP_ID'],
      ENV['ONE_C_LOGIN'],
      ENV['ONE_C_PASSWORD'],
      base_url: ENV['ONE_C_BASE_URL']
    )

    orders = Order.where(exported_to_1c: false).includes(:items)

    orders.each do |order|
      order_items = order.items.map do |item|
        {
          id: item.id,
          product_code: item.product.article,
          product_name: item.product.name,
          product_description: item.product.description,
          quantity: item.quantity,
          price: item.price
        }
      end

      order_data = {
        id: order.id,
        customer_name: order.customer_name,
        customer_email: order.email,
        delivery_address: order.delivery_address,
        total_amount: order.total_amount,
        created_at: order.created_at,
        items: order_items
      }

      service.send_order([order_data])
      order.update(exported_to_1c: true)
    end
  end
end

## 2. Create a service object for KeyCRM API interactions

```ruby
# app/services/keycrm/client.rb

require 'faraday'
require 'faraday_middleware'

class KeyCRM::Client
  class Error < StandardError; end

  def initialize
    @connection = build_connection
  end

  def create_order(order_params)
    response = @connection.post('/orders') do |req|
      req.body = order_params.to_json
      req.headers['Content-Type'] = 'application/json'
    end

    handle_response(response)
  end

  def update_order(order_id, order_params)
    response = @connection.patch("/orders/#{order_id}") do |req|
      req.body = order_params.to_json
      req.headers['Content-Type'] = 'application/json'
    end

    handle_response(response)
  end

  def find_order(order_id)
    response = @connection.get("/orders/#{order_id}")
    handle_response(response)
  end

  def list_orders
    response = @connection.get('/orders')
    handle_response(response)
  end

  private

  def build_connection
    base_url = Rails.application.config.keycrm.sandbox ?
               "#{Rails.application.config.keycrm.base_url}/sandbox/api" :
               "#{Rails.application.config.keycrm.base_url}/api"

    Faraday.new(
      url: base_url,
      headers: {
        'Authorization' => "Bearer #{Rails.application.config.keycrm.api_key}",
        'Content-Type' => 'application/json'
      }
    ) do |f|
      f.request :json
      f.response :json, content_type: /\bjson$/
      f.response :logger
      f.response :raise_error
      f.adapter Faraday.default_adapter
    end
  end

  def handle_response(response)
    if response.success?
      response.body
    else
      raise Error, "KeyCRM API error: #{response.status} - #{response.body}"
    end
  end
end
```

## Implementation

```ruby
# docusign_signer.rb
require 'docusign_esign'
require 'dotenv'
require 'rest-client'
require 'json'

# Load environment variables
Dotenv.load

class DocuSignSigner
  def initialize
    @config = {
      account_id: ENV['DOCUSIGN_ACCOUNT_ID'],
      username: ENV['DOCUSIGN_USERNAME'],
      password: ENV['DOCUSIGN_PASSWORD'],
      integrator_key: ENV['DOCUSIGN_INTEGRATOR_KEY'],
      client_id: ENV['DOCUSIGN_CLIENT_ID'],
      client_secret: ENV['DOCUSIGN_CLIENT_SECRET'],
      redirect_uri: ENV['DOCUSIGN_REDIRECT_URI'] || 'http://localhost:3000/docusign/callback'
    }

    # Initialize the DocuSign client
    @client = DocuSign::eSign::Client.new(
      url: ENV['DOCUSIGN_BASE_URL'] || 'https://demo.docusign.net/restapi',
      account_id: @config[:account_id],
      username: @config[:username],
      password: @config[:password],
      integrator_key: @config[:integrator_key]
    )
  end

  # Step 1: Create an envelope (document to be signed)
  def create_envelope(document_path, signer_email, signer_name)
    # Read the document to be signed
    document = File.read(document_path)

    # Create envelope definition
    envelope_definition = {
      email_subject: "Please sign this document",
      documents: [
        {
          document_base64: Base64.strict_encode64(document),
          name: "Contract.pdf",
          file_extension: "pdf",
          document_id: "1"
        }
      ],
      recipients: {
        signers: [
          {
            email: signer_email,
            name: signer_name,
            recipient_id: "1",
            routing_order: "1",
            tabs: {
              sign_here_tabs: [
                {
                  document_id: "1",
                  page_number: "1",
                  recipient_id: "1",
                  tab_label: "SignHereTab",
                  x_position: "100",
                  y_position: "100"
                }
              ]
            }
          }
        ]
      },
      status: "sent"
    }

    # Create the envelope
    response = @client.create_envelope(envelope_definition)
    envelope_id = response.envelope_id

    puts "Envelope created with ID: #{envelope_id}"
    envelope_id
  end

  # Step 2: Get the envelope status
  def get_envelope_status(envelope_id)
    response = @client.get_envelope(envelope_id)
    response.status
  end

  # Step 3: Download the completed document
  def download_completed_document(envelope_id, output_path)
    # Get the documents from the envelope
    documents = @client.get_envelope_documents(envelope_id)

    # Find the combined document (which includes all signatures)
    combined_document = documents.documents.find { |doc| doc.document_id == "combined" }

    if combined_document
      # Download the document
      url = "#{@client.url}/envelopes/#{envelope_id}/documents/#{combined_document.document_id}/"
      response = RestClient.get(url, {
        Authorization: "Bearer #{@client.access_token}",
        Accept: "application/pdf"
      })

      # Save the document to disk
      File.write(output_path, response.body)
      puts "Document saved to #{output_path}"
      true
    else
      puts "Could not find combined document in envelope"
      false
    end
  end
end

# Example usage

  # Configuration - these should ideally come from environment variables
  document_path = 'contract.pdf' # Path to your document
  signer_email = 'signer@example.com' # Email of the person who needs to sign
  signer_name = 'Signer Name' # Name of the signer

  envelope_id = signer.create_envelope(document_path, signer_email, signer_name)

  puts "Please wait for the document to be signed..."

  # Step 3: Check status and download

  if status == 'completed'

  else

  end
end

## Implementation

```ruby
# app/docusign_client.rb

require 'docusign_esign'
require 'dotenv/load'

class DocuSignClient
  def initialize
    # Load configuration from environment variables
    @config = {
      client_id: ENV['DOCUSIGN_CLIENT_ID'],
      client_secret: ENV['DOCUSIGN_CLIENT_SECRET'],
      redirect_uri: ENV['DOCUSIGN_REDIRECT_URI'],
      base_url: ENV['DOCUSIGN_BASE_URL'] || 'https://demo.docusign.net/restapi',
      username: ENV['DOCUSIGN_USERNAME'],
      password: ENV['DOCUSIGN_PASSWORD'],
      integrator_key: ENV['DOCUSIGN_INTEGRATOR_KEY'],
      account_id: ENV['DOCUSIGN_ACCOUNT_ID']
    }

    # Initialize the eSignature client
    @client = DocuSign_eSign::Configuration.new(@config)
    @client.api_client.configure do |config|
      config.debugging = false
    end
  end

  # Method to upload a document to DocuSign
  def upload_document(file_path)
    # Create envelope definition
    envelope_definition = DocuSign_eSign::EnvelopeDefinition.new({
      email_subject: "Please sign the contract",
      documents: [
        DocuSign_eSign::Document.new({
          document_base64: Base64.strict_encode64(File.read(file_path)),
          name: "contract.pdf",
          file_extension: "pdf",
          id: "1"
        })
      ],
      recipients: DocuSign_eSign::Recipients.new({
        signers: [
          DocuSign_eSign::Signer.new({
            email: "recipient@example.com",
            name: "Recipient Name",
            recipient_id: "1",
            routing_order: "1",
            tabs: DocuSign_eSign::Tabs.new({
              sign_here_tabs: [
                DocuSign_eSign::SignHere.new({
                  document_id: "1",
                  page_number: "1",
                  recipient_id: "1",
                  x_position: "100",
                  y_position: "100"
                })
              ]
            })
          })
        ]
      }),
      status: "sent"
    })

    # Send the envelope
    envelope_api = DocuSign_eSign::EnvelopesApi.new(@client)
    envelope_summary = envelope_api.create_envelope(@config[:account_id], envelope_definition)

    { envelope_id: envelope_summary.envelope_id.to_s, status: envelope_summary.status }
  end

  # Method to download the completed document
  def download_completed_document(envelope_id, file_path)
    envelope_api = DocuSign_eSign::EnvelopesApi.new(@client)

    # Get the document
    document = envelope_api.get_document(
      @config[:account_id],
      envelope_id,
      "combined"
    )

    # Save the document to file
    File.open(file_path, 'wb') do |f|
      f.write(document)
    end

    true
  end

  # Method to check envelope status
  def check_envelope_status(envelope_id)
    envelope_api = DocuSign_eSign::EnvelopesApi.new(@client)
    envelope = envelope_api.get_envelope(@config[:account_id], envelope_id)

    { status: envelope.status, uri: envelope_uri(envelope) }
  end

  private

  # Helper method to get envelope URI
  def envelope_uri(envelope)
    "#{@config[:base_url]}/envelopes/#{envelope.envelope_id}"
  end
end
```

## Implementation

```ruby
# lib/onfido_verification.rb
require 'onfido'
require 'dotenv'

# Load environment variables
Dotenv.load

class OnfidoVerification
  def initialize
    @client = Onfido::Client.new(
      api_token: ENV['ONFIDO_API_TOKEN'],
      environment: ENV['ONFIDO_ENVIRONMENT'] || 'sandbox' # 'live' or 'sandbox'
    )
  end

  # Create an applicant
  def create_applicant(user_id, name, email, dob, address)
    applicant_params = {
      external_id: user_id,
      first_name: name.split.first,
      last_name: name.split.last,
      email: email,
      dob: dob,
      address: address
    }

    response = @client.applicants.create(applicant_params)
    response.data.id
  rescue Onfido::Error => e
    raise "Failed to create applicant: #{e.message}"
  end

  # Create a check for the applicant
  def create_check(applicant_id, report_names: ['standard'])
    check_params = {
      applicant_id: applicant_id,
      report_names: report_names
    }

    response = @client.checks.create(check_params)
    response.data.id
  rescue Onfido::Error => e
    raise "Failed to create check: #{e.message}"
  end

  # Upload a document (e.g., passport, driving license)
  def upload_document(applicant_id, document_type, file_path)
    file = File.open(file_path, 'rb')
    response = @client.applicants.upload_document(
      applicant_id: applicant_id,
      document_type: document_type,
      file: file
    )
    response.data.id
  rescue Onfido::Error => e
    raise "Failed to upload document: #{e.message}"
  end

  # Upload a selfie
  def upload_selfie(applicant_id, file_path)
    file = File.open(file_path, 'rb')
    response = @client.applicants.upload_selfie(
      applicant_id: applicant_id,
      file: file
    )
    response.data.id
  rescue Onfido::Error => e
    raise "Failed to upload selfie: #{e.message}"
  end

  # Get check status
  def get_check_status(check_id)
    response = @client.checks.get(check_id)
    response.data.status
  rescue Onfido::Error => e
    raise "Failed to get check status: #{e.message}"
  end

  # Get check result
  def get_check_result(check_id)
    response = @client.checks.get(check_id)
    response.data.results
  rescue Onfido::Error => e
    raise "Failed to get check result: #{e.message}"
  end
end
```

## Implementation Steps

### 1. Install and configure Devise

### 2. Generate a User model

```bash

rails db:migrate
```

### 3. Create initializer for OmniAuth

Create `config/initializers/devise.rb` (or add to existing if it exists):

```ruby
# config/initializers/devise.rb

Rails.application.config.middleware.use OmniAuth::Builder do
  provider :google_oauth2, ENV['GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID'], ENV['GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET'], {
    scope: 'email,profile',
    prompt: 'select_account',
    name: 'google'
  }

    scope: 'email,name',
    response_type: 'code id_token',
    name: 'apple'
  }
end
```

### 4. Add OmniAuthable module to User model

```ruby
# app/models/user.rb

class User < ApplicationRecord
  devise :database_authenticatable, :registerable,
         :recoverable, :rememberable, :validatable,
         :omniauthable, omniauth_providers: [:google_oauth2, :apple]

  def self.from_omniauth(auth)
    where(provider: auth.provider, uid: auth.uid).first_or_create do |user|
      user.email = auth.info.email
      user.password = Devise.friendly_token[0, 20]
      user.name = auth.info.name   # assuming the user model has a name
      # user.image = auth.info.image # uncomment if you store user images
      user.save!
    end
  end
end
```

```

```ruby

    sign_in_and_redirect @user, event: :authentication
  end

  def apple
    @user = User.from_omniauth(request.env["omniauth.auth"])
    sign_in_and_redirect @user, event: :authentication
  end

  def failure
    redirect_to root_path
  end
end

### 6. Update routes

### 2. KeyCRM Service Class

Create a service class to handle API communications with KeyCRM.

```ruby
# app/services/keycrm_service.rb
class KeyCRMService
  include HTTParty
  base_uri Rails.application.config.x.keycrm[:api_url]

  # Authentication headers
  def headers
    {
      'Content-Type' => 'application/json',
      'Authorization' => "Basic #{Base64.encode64('#{Rails.application.config.x.keycrm[:username]}:#{Rails.application.config.x.keycrm[:password]}}').strip}",
      'X-API-Key' => Rails.application.config.x.keycrm[:api_key]
    }
  end

  # Create a new order in KeyCRM
  def create_order(order_params)
    response = self.class.post(
      '/orders',
      body: order_params.to_json,
      headers: headers
    )

    handle_response(response)
  end

  # Update an existing order in KeyCRM
  def update_order(order_id, order_params)
    response = self.class.put(
      "/orders/#{order_id}",
      body: order_params.to_json,
      headers: headers
    )

    handle_response(response)
  end

  # Get order details from KeyCRM
  def get_order(order_id)
    response = self.class.get(
      "/orders/#{order_id}",
      headers: headers
    )

    handle_response(response)
  end

  # Private method to handle API responses
  private

  def handle_response(response)
    case response.code
    when 200..299
      Oj.load(response.body, symbolize_keys: true)
    when 400
      raise KeyCRMService::BadRequestError, response.parsed_response['message'] || 'Bad request'
    when 401
      raise KeyCRMService::UnauthorizedError, 'Unauthorized - check your credentials'
    when 404
      raise KeyCRMService::NotFoundError, 'Resource not found'
    else
      raise KeyCRMService::APIError, "API Error: #{response.code} - #{response.parsed_response['message'] || 'Unknown error'}"
    end
  end

  # Custom error classes
  class APIError < StandardError; end
  class BadRequestError < APIError; end
  class UnauthorizedError < APIError; end
  class NotFoundError < APIError; end
end
```

### 3. Order Model Extension

Extend your Order model to handle KeyCRM synchronization.

# app/models/order.rb
class Order < ApplicationRecord
  after_create :sync_to_keycrm
  after_update :sync_to_keycrm_if_status_changed

  def sync_to_keycrm
    keycrm_service = KeyCRMService.new
    order_params = build_keycrm_order_params

    if persisted?
      keycrm_service.create_order(order_params)
      update_column(:keycrm_order_id, keycrm_service.get_order(order_params[:external_id]).dig(:id))
    else
      raise "Failed to create order in KeyCRM"
    end
  end

  def sync_to_keycrm_if_status_changed
    if saved_change_to_status?
      keycrm_service = KeyCRMService.new
      order_params = build_keycrm_order_params

      if keycrm_order_id
        keycrm_service.update_order(keycrm_order_id, order_params)
      else
        sync_to_keycrm
      end
    end
  end

  private

  def build_keycrm_order_params
    {
      external_id: id,
      order_number: order_number,
      customer: {
        first_name: customer.first_name,
        last_name: customer.last_name,
        email: customer.email,
        phone: customer.phone
      },
      items: line_items.map do |item|
        {
          product_name: item.product.name,
          quantity: item.quantity,
          unit_price: item.unit_price,
          total_price: item.total_price
        }
      end,
      total_amount: total_amount,
      status: keycrm_status,
      created_at: created_at.iso8601,
      updated_at: updated_at.iso8601,
      shipping_address: {
        street: shipping_address.street,
        city: shipping_address.city,
        state: shipping_address.state,
        zip_code: shipping_address.zip_code,
        country: shipping_address.country
      }
    }
  end

  def keycrm_status
    case status
    when 'pending' then 'pending'
    when 'paid' then 'paid'
    when 'shipped' then 'shipped'
    when 'cancelled' then 'cancelled'
    else 'pending'
    end
  end
end

### 4. Background Job for Async Sync

For better performance, create a background job to handle the KeyCRM sync.

```ruby
# app/jobs/sync_order_to_keycrm_job.rb
class SyncOrderToKeycrmJob < ApplicationJob
  queue_as :default

  def perform(order_id)
    order = Order.find(order_id)
    keycrm_service = KeyCRMService.new

    begin
      order_params = order.build_keycrm_order_params

      if order.keycrm_order_id
        keycrm_service.update_order(order.keycrm_order_id, order_params)
      else
        response = keycrm_service.create_order(order_params)
        order.update!(keycrm_order_id: response.dig(:id))
      end
    rescue KeyCRMService::APIError => e
      Rails.logger.error "KeyCRM API Error: #{e.message}"
      # You might want to implement retry logic here
    end
  end
end
```

## KeyCRM API Client Implementation

Create a new file `app/services/key_crm_client.rb`:

```ruby
# app/services/key_crm_client.rb

class KeyCRMClient
  BASE_URL = 'https://api.keycrm.com/v1'.freeze
  DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 10 # seconds

  def initialize(api_key: Rails.application.credentials.key_crm_api_key)
    @api_key = api_key
    @http_client = Faraday.new(
      url: BASE_URL,
      headers: { 'Content-Type' => 'application/json', 'Authorization' => "Bearer #{@api_key}" },
      request: { timeout: DEFAULT_TIMEOUT }
    )
  end

  # Create a new order in KeyCRM
  def create_order(order_params)
    response = @http_client.post('/orders') do |req|
      req.body = order_params.to_json
    end

    handle_response(response)
  end

  # Update an existing order in KeyCRM
  def update_order(order_id, order_params)
    response = @http_client.put("/orders/#{order_id}") do |req|
      req.body = order_params.to_json
    end

    handle_response(response)
  end

  # Get order details from KeyCRM
  def get_order(order_id)
    response = @http_client.get("/orders/#{order_id}")
    handle_response(response)
  end

  # Get all orders (with optional filtering)
  def list_orders(filters: {})
    query_params = filters.compact
    response = @http_client.get('/orders', query_params)
    handle_response(response)
  end

  private

  def handle_response(response)
    case response.status
    when 200..299
      Oj.load(response.body)
    when 400..499
      raise KeyCRMClient::ClientError, Oj.load(response.body)['error'] || 'Client error'
    when 500..599
      raise KeyCRMClient::ServerError, 'Server error'
    else
      raise KeyCRMClient::UnexpectedError, "Unexpected status code: #{response.status}"
    end
  rescue Faraday::Error => e
    raise KeyCRMClient::ConnectionError, e.message
    end
  end

  # Custom error classes
  class Error < StandardError; end
  class ClientError < Error; end
  class ServerError < Error; end
  class ConnectionError < Error; end
  class UnexpectedError < Error; end
end
```

require 'onfido'
require 'dotenv'
require 'json'
require 'httparty'

Dotenv.load

class OnfidoService
  def initialize
    @onfido = Onfido::Client.new(
      api_key: ENV['ONFIDO_API_KEY'],
      api_secret: ENV['ONFIDO_API_SECRET'],
      sandbox: ENV['ONFIDO_API_SANDBOX'] == 'true'
    )
  end

  # Create a new applicant
  def create_applicant(applicant_params)
    @onfido.applicants.create(applicant_params)
  end

  # Upload a document (ID) for verification
  def upload_document(applicant_id, file_path, document_type, side = nil)
    file = File.open(file_path)

    @onfido.applicants.upload_document(
      applicant_id,
      file,
      file_path,
      document_type,
      side
    )
  end

  # Upload a selfie for verification
  def upload_selfie(applicant_id, file_path)
    file = File.open(file_path)

    @onfido.applicants.upload_selfie(
      applicant_id,
      file,
      file_path
    )
  end

  # Create a check (verification) for the applicant
  def create_check(applicant_id, check_params)
    @onfido.checks.create(applicant_id, check_params)
  end

  # Get the status of a check
  def get_check_status(check_id)
    @onfido.checks.get(check_id)
  end

  # Get the result of a check
  def get_check_result(check_id)
    @onfido.checks.get_result(check_id)
  end
end

Here's a complete implementation for verifying a user's identity with Onfido document and selfie checks, including a Gemfile and the necessary code.

## Gemfile

# Onfido SDK

# For API requests and JSON handling
gem 'httparty'

```

## Implementation

```ruby
require 'onfido'
require 'httparty'
require 'faraday'
require 'faraday/middleware'

# Configure the Onfido client
class OnfidoClient
  def initialize(api_token, environment: :sandbox)
    @client = Onfido::Client.new(api_token: api_token, environment: environment)
  end

  # Create a new applicant for verification
  def create_applicant(applicant_data)
    @client.applicants.create(applicant_data)
  end

  # Upload a document for verification
  def upload_document(applicant_id, document_type, file_path, side: :front)
    file = File.read(file_path)
    file_type = File.extname(file_path).downcase

    @client.applicants(applicant_id).documents.upload(
      document_type: document_type,
      file: file,
      file_type: file_type,
      side: side
    )
  end

  # Upload a selfie for verification
  def upload_selfie(applicant_id, file_path)
    file = File.read(file_path)
    file_type = File.extname(file_path).downcase

    @client.applicants(applicant_id).selfies.upload(
      file: file,
      file_type: file_type
    )
  end

  # Create a check with document and selfie verification
  def create_check(applicant_id, report_name: :express)
    @client.applicants(applicant_id).checks.create(
      report_names: [report_name],
      document: { side: :front },
      selfie: {}
    )
  end

  # Get check status
  def get_check_status(applicant_id, check_id)
    @client.applicants(applicant_id).checks(check_id).fetch
  end

  # Get check results
  def get_check_results(applicant_id, check_id)
    @client.applicants(applicant_id).checks(check_id).results
  end
end

# Service class to handle the verification workflow
class IdentityVerificationService
  def initialize(api_token, environment: :sandbox)
    @client = OnfidoClient.new(api_token, environment: environment)
  end

  def verify_identity(applicant_data, document_file_path, selfie_file_path)
    # Step 1: Create applicant
    applicant = @client.create_applicant(applicant_data)
    applicant_id = applicant.id

    # Step 2: Upload document
    @client.upload_document(applicant_id, :passport, document_file_path, side: :front)

    # Step 3: Upload selfie
    @client.upload_selfie(applicant_id, selfie_file_path)

    # Step 4: Create check
    check = @client.create_check(applicant_id)
    check_id = check.id

    # Step 5: Poll for results (in a real app, you'd likely use webhooks)
    check_results = wait_for_check_completion(applicant_id, check_id)

    # Step 6: Analyze results
    analyze_results(check_results)
  end

  private

  def wait_for_check_completion(applicant_id, check_id, timeout = 300, interval = 10)
    start_time = Time.now
    last_status = nil

    while (Time.now - start_time) < timeout
      check = @client.get_check_status(applicant_id, check_id)
      current_status = check.status

      if current_status == 'complete'
        return @client.get_check_results(applicant_id, check_id)
      elsif current_status != last_status
        puts "Check status: #{current_status}"
        last_status = current_status
      end

      sleep interval
    end

    raise "Check did not complete within #{timeout} seconds"
  end

  def analyze_results(results)
    if results.any? { |result| result.status == 'clear' }
      { success: true, message: 'Identity verified successfully' }
    else
      { success: false, message: 'Identity verification failed', details: results }
    end
  end
end
```

# Ruby Implementation for Checking US OFAC Sanctions List

Here's a complete solution that includes a Gemfile and Ruby code to check if a person appears on the US OFAC sanctions list.

## Gemfile

```ruby
# Gemfile
source 'https://rubygems.org'

# For HTTP requests
gem 'httparty'

# For XML parsing (OFAC data is often in XML format)

# For configuration management
gem 'config'
```

## Implementation

```ruby
# lib/ofac_checker.rb
require 'httparty'
require 'nokogiri'
require 'config'

class OFACChecker
  include HTTParty
  base_uri 'https://www.treasury.gov/ofac/downloads/sdn.xml'

  def initialize
    @config = Config.load_and_set_root('config/ofac.yml')
  end

  # Main method to check if a name is on the OFAC sanctions list
  def check_name(name)
    response = self.class.get('/')
    return false unless response.success?

    parse_xml(response.body).any? do |entry|
      match_name?(entry, name)
    end
  end

  private

  def parse_xml(xml_content)
    Nokogiri::XML(xml_content).xpath('//sdnEntry')
  end

  def match_name?(entry, name)
    # Extract all names from the entry (including aliases)
    names = entry.xpath('//lastName') + entry.xpath('//firstName') + entry.xpath('//a.k.a.') +
            entry.xpath('//a.k.a.1') + entry.xpath('//a.k.a.2') + entry.xpath('//a.k.a.3')

    # Compare each name with the input, allowing for slight variations
    names.any? do |node|
      node.text.strip.casecmp(name.strip) == 0
    end
  end
end
```

# app/services/onfido_verification_service.rb
class OnfidoVerificationService
  include HTTParty

  def initialize(user_id: nil, email: nil, name: nil, document: nil, selfie: nil)
    @user_id = user_id
    @email = email
    @name = name
    @document = document
    @selfie = selfie
  end

  # Start the verification process
  def start_verification
    create_applicant
    create_check
  end

  # Get verification status
  def check_status(check_id)
    Onfido::Check.find(check_id)
  end

  private

  def create_applicant
    @applicant = Onfido::Applicant.create(
      applicant_id: generate_unique_id,
      first_name: @name.split.first,
      last_name: @name.split.last,
      email: @email,
      id_number: @document[:id_number],
      dob: @document[:dob],
      address: {
        building_name: @document[:address][:building_name],
        street: @document[:address][:street],
        state: @document[:address][:state],
        city: @document[:address][:city],
        postal_code: @document[:address][:postal_code],
        country: @document[:address][:country]
      }
    )
  end

  def create_check
    @check = Onfido::Check.create(
      applicant_id: @applicant.id,
      type: 'standard',
      report_names: ['document', 'facial_similarity'],
      document: {
        side: @document[:side],
        file_url: @document[:file_url],
        file_type: @document[:file_type],
        file_name: @document[:file_name]
      },
      selfie: {
        file_url: @selfie[:file_url],
        file_type: @selfie[:file_type],
        file_name: @selfie[:file_name]
      }
    )
  end

  def generate_unique_id
    "#{@user_id}-#{Time.now.to_i}"
  end
end

```ruby
# app/controllers/onfido_webhooks_controller.rb
class OnfidoWebhooksController < ApplicationController
  skip_before_action :verify_authenticity_token

  def create
    payload = request.body.read
    signature = request.headers['X-Onfido-Signature']

    # Verify the webhook signature
    if verify_signature(payload, signature)
      event = JSON.parse(payload)

      case event['type']
      when 'check.completed'
        handle_completed_check(event)
      when 'check.failed'
        handle_failed_check(event)
      when 'check.canceled'
        handle_canceled_check(event)
      end

      render plain: 'OK', status: :ok
    else
      render plain: 'Unauthorized', status: :unauthorized
    end
  end

  private

  def verify_signature(payload, signature)
    secret = ENV['ONFIDO_WEBHOOK_SECRET']
    expected_signature = OpenSSL::HMAC.hexdigest('SHA256', secret, payload)
    Rack::Utils.secure_compare(expected_signature, signature)
  end

  def handle_completed_check(event)
    check = Onfido::Check.find(event['resource']['id'])
    user = User.find_by(onfido_check_id: check.id)

    if user
      # Update user status
      user.update(onfido_verified: true, onfido_check_result: check.result)
      # Send notification to user
      UserMailer.verification_success(user).deliver_later
    end
  end

  def handle_failed_check(event)
    check = Onfido::Check.find(event['resource']['id'])
    user = User.find_by(onfido_check_id: check.id)

    if user
      # Update user status
      user.update(onfido_verified: false, onfido_check_result: check.result)
      # Send notification to user
      UserMailer.verification_failed(user, check.errors).deliver_later
    end
  end

  def handle_canceled_check(event)
    # Handle canceled checks if needed
  end
end

Add the following to your `config/initializers/devise.rb`: ```ruby # config/initializers/devise.rb Devise.setup do |config| # ... other Devise config config.omniauth :google_oauth2, ENV['GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID'], ENV['GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET'], { name: 'google', scope: 'email,profile', prompt: 'select_account', access_type: 'online' } config.omniauth :apple, ENV['APPLE_TEAM_ID'], ENV['APPLE_CLIENT_ID'], { name: 'apple', scope: 'name email', response_mode: 'form_post' } end ``` 3. Create the OmniAuth controller: ```ruby # app/controllers/users/omniauth_callbacks_controller.rb class Users::OmniauthCallbacksController < Devise::OmniauthCallbacksController def google_oauth2 @user = User.from_omniauth(request.env["omniauth.auth"]) if @user.persisted? sign_in_and_redirect @user, event: :authentication set_flash_message(:notice, :success, kind: "Google") if is_navigational_format? else session["devise.google_data"] = request.env["omniauth.auth"].except(:extra) redirect_to new_user_registration_url end end def apple @user = User.from_omniauth(request.env["omniauth.auth"]) if @user.persisted? sign_in_and_redirect @user, event: :authentication set_flash_message(:notice, :success, kind: "Apple") if is_navigational_format? else session["devise.apple_data"] = request.env["omniauth.auth"].except(:extra) redirect_to new_user_registration_url end end def failure redirect_to root_path end end ``` 4. Add the routes in `config/routes.rb`: ```ruby # config/routes.rb Rails.application.routes.draw do devise_for :users, controllers: { omniauth_callbacks: 'users/omniauth_callbacks', registrations: 'users/registrations' } # ... your other routes end ``` 5. Add the User model methods: ```ruby # app/models/user.rb class User < ApplicationRecord devise :database_authenticatable, :registerable, :recoverable, :rememberable, :validatable, :omniauthable, omniauth_providers: [:google_oauth2, :apple] def self.from_omniauth(auth) where(provider: auth.provider, uid: auth.uid).first_or_create do |user| user.email = auth.info.email user.password = Devise.friendly_token[0, 20] user.name = auth.info.name # assuming the user model has a name user.image = auth.info.image # assuming the user model has an image end end # Add these columns to your users table if you want to store more info # name: string # image: string # provider: string # uid: string end ``` 6. Add migrations if you need to store additional user data: ```bash rails generate migration AddOmniauthToUsers provider:string uid:string name:string image:string rails db:migrate ``` 7. Add the sign-in buttons to your views (e.g., `app/views/devise/registrations/new.html.erb`): ```erb

Sign up

<%= form_for(resource, as: resource_name, url: registration_path(resource_name)) do |f| %> <%= render "devise/shared/error_messages", resource: resource %>
<%= f.label :email %>
<%= f.email_field :email, autofocus: true, autocomplete: "email" %>
<%= f.label :password %> <% if @minimum_password_length %> (<%= @minimum_password_length %> characters minimum) <% end %>
<%= f.password_field :password, autocomplete: "new-password" %>
<%= f.label :password_confirmation %>
<%= f.password_field :password_confirmation, autocomplete: "new-password" %>
<%= f.submit "Sign up" %>
<% end %>
<%= link_to "Sign in with Google", user_google_oauth2_omniauth_authorize_path, class: "btn btn-google" %> <%= link_to "Sign in with Apple", user_apple_omniauth_authorize_path, method: :post, class: "btn btn-apple" %>
``` 8. Add some CSS for the buttons (optional): ```css /* app/assets/stylesheets/application.css */ .btn-google { background-color: #4285F4; color: white; padding: 10px 20px; border-radius: 4px; text-decoration: none; margin: 10px 5px; display: inline-block; } .btn-apple { background-color: #000000; color: white; padding: 10px 20px; border-radius: 4px; text-decoration: none; margin: 10px 5px; display: inline-block; } ``` ## Environment Variables You'll need to set these environment variables: 1. For Google: - `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` - `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` 2. For Apple: - `APPLE_TEAM_ID` - `APPLE_CLIENT_ID` You can use the `dotenv-rails` gem to manage these in development: ```ruby # Gemfile gem 'dotenv-rails', groups: [:development, :test] ``` Then create a `.env` file in your project root: ``` GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=your_google_client_id GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=your_google_client_secret APPLE_TEAM_ID=your_apple_team_id APPLE_CLIENT_ID=your_apple_client_id ``` ## Additional Notes 1. For Apple sign-in, you'll need to: - Register your app with Apple Developer - Configure a service ID - Set up the redirect URI in your Apple Developer account - Add the Apple sign-in capability to your app 2. For Google sign-in, you'll need to: - Create a project in Google Cloud Console - Set up OAuth credentials - Add your redirect URIs 3. Make sure to add the proper URIs to your OAuth provider settings (typically something like `http://localhost:3000/users/auth/:provider/callback` for development). This implementation provides a complete solution for adding both Google and Apple sign-in to a Rails app using Devise and OmniAuth.

source 'https://rubygems.org'

Встановіть геми командою:

### 2. **Реалізація перевірки OFAC**
```ruby
# app.rb
require 'httparty'
require 'json'

class OfacChecker
  include HTTParty
  base_uri 'https://api.usa.gov'

  def initialize(api_key)
    @options = { query: { api_key: api_key } }
  end

  # Перевірка, чи є особа у санкційному списку OFAC
  def check_sanctions(name)
    response = self.class.get(
      '/sanctions',
      query: {
        name: name,
        **@options[:query]
      }
    )

    if response.success?
      JSON.parse(response.body)
    else
      raise "OFAC API Error: #{response.code} - #{response.message}"
    end
  end
end

# Приклад використання
if __FILE__ == $0
  API_KEY = 'YOUR_OFAC_API_KEY'  # Замініть на свій API-ключ

  checker = OfacChecker.new(API_KEY)

  # Приклад перевірки
  name = "John Doe"
  result = checker.check_sanctions(name)

  if result.any?
    puts "⚠️ Attention! #{name} is in the OFAC sanctions list."
  else
    puts "✅ #{name} is not listed in the OFAC sanctions."
  end
end
```

---

### 3. **Додаткові пояснення**
1. **API OFAC**
   - OFAC надає API для перевірки санкційних списків. Для доступу потрібен **API-ключ** (зареєструйтеся на [USA.gov](https://api.usa.gov/)).
   - Запит до `/sanctions` повертає JSON з даними, якщо особа знаходиться у списку.

2. **Вірішення проблем**
   - Якщо OFAC не надає публічний API, можна використати альтернативні джерела (наприклад, [OFAC SDN List](https://www.treasury.gov/ofac/downloads/sdn.xml) у форматі XML).
   - У цьому випадку можна використати `nokogiri` для парсингу XML.

3. **Тестування**
   - Запустіть код:
     ```bash
     ruby app.rb
     ```

---

### 4. **Варіант з парсингом OFAC SDN List (XML)**
Якщо API недоступний, можна спарсити XML-список OFAC:

```ruby
# ofac_sdn_parser.rb
require 'nokogiri'
require 'open-uri'

class OfacSdnParser
  SDN_URL = 'https://www.treasury.gov/ofac/downloads/sdn.xml'.freeze

  def initialize
    @doc = Nokogiri::XML(URI.open(SDN_URL))
  end

  def check_sanctions(name)
    entries = @doc.xpath('//sdnEntry')
    entries.any? { |entry| entry.xpath('firstName | lastName').text.downcase.include?(name.downcase) }
  end
end

# Приклад використання
if __FILE__ == $0
  parser = OfacSdnParser.new
  name = "John Doe"

  if parser.check_sanctions(name)
    puts "⚠️ #{name} is in the OFAC sanctions list."
  else
    puts "✅ #{name} is not listed in the OFAC sanctions."
  end
end
```

---

### Підсумок
- Якщо доступний API OFAC, використовуйте `OfacChecker`.
- Якщо API немає, використовуйте `OfacSdnParser` для парсингу XML.
- Для реєстрації клієнтів можна додати цей код у ваш застосунок (наприклад, у `before_save` у Rails або у middleware у Sinatra).

# Ruby Implementation for DocuSign eSignature API

Here's a complete solution to sign a PDF contract electronically using the DocuSign eSignature API and download the completed document.

## Gemfile

```ruby
# Gemfile
source 'https://rubygems.org'

gem 'docusign_esign', '~> 5.0' # Official DocuSign eSign Ruby SDK
gem 'httparty' # For making HTTP requests (though the SDK includes this)
```

Run `bundle install` to install the dependencies.

## Implementation

```ruby
# docusign_signer.rb
require 'docusign_esign'
require 'dotenv'
require 'tempfile'

Dotenv.load # Load environment variables from .env file

class DocuSignSigner
  def initialize
    # Load configuration from environment variables
    @config = DocuSignEsign::Configuration.new
    @config.host = ENV['DOCUSIGN_HOST'] || 'https://demo.docusign.net/restapi' # or 'https://www.docusign.net/restapi' for production
    @config.api_client = DocuSignEsign::ApiClient.new(@config)
    @config.api_client.set_default_header('Authorization', "Bearer #{get_oauth_token}")
  end

  def sign_and_download_contract(pdf_file_path, email, name, signing_instructions)
    # Read the PDF file
    pdf_data = File.binread(pdf_file_path)
    file_name = File.basename(pdf_file_path)

    # Create a new envelope
    envelope_definition = DocuSignEsign::EnvelopeDefinition.new
    envelope_definition.email_subject = "Please sign the contract"

    # Add a document to the envelope
    document = DocuSignEsign::Document.new
    document.document_base64 = Base64.strict_encode64(pdf_data)
    document.name = file_name
    document.file_extension = "pdf"
    document.document_id = "1"

    # Add recipients (signers)
    signer = DocuSignEsign::Signer.new
    signer.email = email
    signer.name = name
    signer.recipient_id = "1"
    signer.routing_order = "1"

    # Add a signing tab
    signing_tab = DocuSignEsign::SignHere.new
    signing_tab.document_id = "1"
    signing_tab.page_number = "1" # Adjust as needed
    signing_tab.x_position = "100" # Adjust as needed
    signing_tab.y_position = "100" # Adjust as needed

    # Create the sign_here tab
    sign_here = DocuSignEsign::SignHere.new
    sign_here.tab_label = "SignHereTab"
    sign_here.x_position = "100"
    sign_here.y_position = "100"
    sign_here.document_id = "1"
    sign_here.page_number = "1"

    # Create the signer tab
    signer_tab = DocuSignEsign::Signer.new
    signer_tab.tab_label = "Signer1"
    signer_tab.recipient_id = "1"
    signer_tab.sign_in_connection = DocuSignEsign::SignInWithIdCheckInformation.new
    signer_tab.id_check = DocuSignEsign::IDCheckInformation.new
    signer_tab.id_check.id_check_configuration_name = "Basic ID Check"
    signer_tab.require_id_lookup = false

    # Create the tabs
    tabs = DocuSignEsign::Tabs.new
    tabs.sign_here_tabs = [sign_here]

    # Create the signer
    signer = DocuSignEsign::Signer.new
    signer.email = email
    signer.name = name
    signer.recipient_id = "1"
    signer.routing_order = "1"
    signer.tabs = tabs

    # Create the recipients
    recipients = DocuSignEsign::Recipients.new
    recipients.signers = [signer]

    # Add the document and recipients to the envelope
    envelope_definition.documents = [document]
    envelope_definition.recipients = recipients

    # Send the envelope
    envelopes_api = DocuSignEsign::EnvelopesApi.new(@config.api_client)
    envelope_summary = envelopes_api.create_envelope(
      account_id: ENV['DOCUSIGN_ACCOUNT_ID'],
      envelope_definition: envelope_definition
    )

    # Wait for the envelope to be completed (in a real app, you'd use webhooks)
    sleep(10) # Simple delay - in production, use polling or webhooks

    # Get the envelope details to check status
    envelope_details = envelopes_api.get_envelope(
      account_id: ENV['DOCUSIGN_ACCOUNT_ID'],
      envelope_id: envelope_summary.envelope_id
    )

    if envelope_details.status == "completed"
      # Download the completed document
      documents_api = DocuSignEsign::DocumentsApi.new(@config.api_client)
      document_result = documents_api.get_document(
        account_id: ENV['DOCUSIGN_ACCOUNT_ID'],
        envelope_id: envelope_summary.envelope_id,
        document_id: "1"
      )

      # Save the document to a temporary file
      temp_file = Tempfile.new([file_name, '.pdf'])
      temp_file.binwrite(Base64.decode64(document_result.document_base64))
      temp_file.close

      return {
        success: true,
        message: "Document signed successfully",
        file_path: temp_file.path
      }
    else
      return {
        success: false,
        message: "Document signing failed: #{envelope_details.status}",
        status: envelope_details.status
      }
    end
  end

  private

  def get_oauth_token
    # In a real application, you would implement proper OAuth2 token management
    # For this example, we'll assume you have a token stored in an environment variable
    ENV['DOCUSIGN_ACCESS_TOKEN'] ||
      raise("No DocuSign access token found in environment variables")
  end
end
```

## Usage Example

```ruby
# example_usage.rb
require_relative 'docusign_signer'

signer = DocuSignSigner.new

# Path to your PDF file
pdf_path = 'contract.pdf'

# Signer details
email = 'signer@example.com'
name = 'John Doe'

# Signing instructions (optional)
signing_instructions = "Please sign here to complete the contract"

result = signer.sign_and_download_contract(
  pdf_path,
  email,
  name,
  signing_instructions
)

if result[:success]
  puts "Successfully signed document saved to: #{result[:file_path]}"
  # You might want to send this to the user or store it
else
  puts "Error: #{result[:message]}"
  puts "Status: #{result[:status]}"
end
```

## Environment Variables (.env file)

Create a `.env` file with your DocuSign credentials:

```env
DOCUSIGN_CLIENT_ID=your_integration_key
DOCUSIGN_CLIENT_SECRET=your_secret
DOCUSIGN_REDIRECT_URI=your_redirect_uri
DOCUSIGN_ACCOUNT_ID=your_account_id
DOCUSIGN_ACCESS_TOKEN=your_oauth_token
DOCUSIGN_HOST=https://demo.docusign.net/restapi
```

## Important Notes

1. **Authentication**: The example uses a simple approach with an access token. In a production environment, you should implement proper OAuth2 authentication.

2. **Error Handling**: The code includes basic error handling, but you should expand this for production use.

3. **Polling**: The example uses a simple sleep to wait for completion. In production, use DocuSign's webhook notifications or implement proper polling.

4. **Document Positioning**: The example uses hardcoded positions for the signature. In a real application, you should:
   - Use anchor tags or relative positioning
   - Parse the PDF to find appropriate signing locations
   - Use DocuSign's document position tools

5. **Test Environment**: The code is configured for DocuSign's demo environment. For production, change the host to `https://www.docusign.net/restapi`.

6. **Security**: Never hardcode credentials in your code. Always use environment variables or a secure secrets management system.

To run this, you'll need to:
1. Register as a DocuSign developer (https://developers.docusign.com/)
2. Create an integration and get your API credentials
3. Set up your environment variables
4. Install the required gems with `bundle install`

Ось приклад коду для шифрування чутливих персональних полів (номер паспорта, дата народження) в Ruby on Rails з використанням ActiveRecord.

### 1. Gemfile
Додайте наступні геми для шифрування:

```ruby
# Gemfile
source 'https://rubygems.org'

# Основні Rails-геми
gem 'rails', '~> 7.0.0'

# Gem для шифрування
gem 'attr_encrypted', '~> 3.2.0'

# Інші необхідні геми
gem 'bcrypt', '~> 3.1.7'
```

Виконайте `bundle install` після оновлення Gemfile.

---

### 2. Модель ActiveRecord з шифруванням

```ruby
# app/models/user.rb
require 'attr_encrypted'

class User < ApplicationRecord
  include ActiveModel::SecureToken
  include AttrEncrypted::Encryption # Підключення модуля для шифрування

  attr_encrypted :passport_number, key: :encryption_key
  attr_encrypted :date_of_birth, key: :encryption_key

  validates :passport_number, presence: true, if: -> { passport_number_changed? }
  validates :date_of_birth, presence: true, if: -> { date_of_birth_changed? }

  before_validation :generate_keys, on: :create

  private

  def generate_keys
    self.encryption_key ||= SecureToken.generate
  end
end
```

---

### 3. Міграція бази даних

```ruby
# db/migrate/[timestamp]_create_users.rb
class CreateUsers < ActiveRecord::Migration[7.0]
  def change
    create_table :users do |t|
      t.string :name
      t.string :passport_number, encrypted: true  # Шифроване поле
      t.date :date_of_birth, encrypted: true      # Шифроване поле
      t.string :encryption_key                   # Ключ для шифрування

      t.timestamps
    end
  end
end
```

---

### 4. Налаштування шифрування

Для використання `attr_encrypted` потрібно створити файл налаштувань:

```ruby
# config/initializers/attr_encrypted.rb
Rails.application.config attr_encrypted do |config|
  config.key_derivation_salt = 'your_custom_salt_here' # Рекомендується змінити
  config.key_generator = AttrEncrypted::KeyGenerators::Base64UrlSafeKeyGenerator
  config.encryption_key = AttrEncrypted::KeyDerivers::StaticKeyDeriver.new(
    Rails.application.secrets.encryption_key || 'fallback_key'
  )
end
```

Рекомендується зберігати абсолютно випадковий ключ в secrets:

```ruby
# config/secrets.yml (або secrets.encrypted.yml)
development:
  encryption_key: <%= ENV['ENCRYPTION_KEY'] || 'development_key_123' %>

production:
  encryption_key: <%= ENV['ENCRYPTION_KEY'] %> # Обов'язково використовуйте середовище
```

---

### 5. Використання в контролері

```ruby
# app/controllers/users_controller.rb
class UsersController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @user = User.new(user_params)

    if @user.save
      redirect_to @user, notice: 'User was successfully created.'
    else
      render :new
    end
  end

  private

  def user_params
    params.require(:user).permit(:name, :passport_number, :date_of_birth)
  end
end
```

---

### 6. Пояснення

1. **`attr_encrypted`** - цей gem автоматично шифрує і дешифрує поля за допомогою AES-256.
2. **Ключі шифрування** - кожен запис може мати свій унікальний ключ (як в прикладі) або використовувати спільний ключ.
3. **Безпека** - не зберігайте ключі шифрування в коді, використовуйте secrets або середовище.
4. **Валідація** - шифрування відбувається після валідації.

Цей підхід забезпечує базову безпеку для чутливих даних в ActiveRecord. Для більш складних сценаріїв можна розглянути використання PGP або інших методів шифрування.

## Gemfile

```ruby

require 'attr_encrypted'

class Person < ActiveRecord::Base
  # Encrypt sensitive fields
  attr_encrypted :passport_number,
    key: :encryption_key,
    encryptor: :aes256,
    mode: :perform,
    algorithm: 'aes-256-cbc'

  attr_encrypted :date_of_birth,
    key: :encryption_key,
    encryptor: :aes256,
    mode: :perform,
    algorithm: 'aes-256-cbc'

  # Validate presence of encrypted fields
  validates :passport_number, presence: true
  validates :date_of_birth, presence: true

  # Generate a random encryption key if one doesn't exist
  before_validation :generate_encryption_key, unless: :encryption_key

  private

  def generate_encryption_key
    # In production, you should use a proper key management system
    # This is just a simple example for demonstration
    self.encryption_key = SecureRandom.hex(32)
  end
end

```ruby
person = Person.new
person.passport_number = 'ABC123456'
person.date_of_birth = Date.new(1980, 5, 15)

# The actual database will store encrypted values
person.save!

# When you access the attributes, they'll be decrypted automatically
puts person.passport_number  # => "ABC123456"
puts person.date_of_birth    # => Thu, 15 May 1980

# The database actually stores encrypted versions
Person.find(person.id).passport_number_before_type_cast  # => encrypted binary data
```

### Important Notes:

1. **Key Management**: In production, never hardcode encryption keys. Use a secure key management system.

2. **Performance**: Encryption/decryption adds overhead. For large datasets, consider:
   - Using column-level encryption for only the most sensitive fields
   - Caching frequently accessed encrypted data

3. **Indexing**: Encrypted fields can't be indexed effectively, so avoid putting them in WHERE clauses.

4. **Backups**: Ensure your encrypted data backups are stored securely.

5. **Testing**: The example shows a test-specific key for the date of birth to demonstrate different keys for different fields.

This implementation provides a solid foundation for encrypting sensitive personal data in ActiveRecord models.

    total_tenders = response['data']['total']

    puts "Found #{total_tenders} tenders"

    response['data']['_embedded']['tenders'].each do |tender_data|
      process_tender(tender_data)
    end

    total_tenders
  end

    existing_tender = Tender.where(tender_id: tender_data['id']).first

    if existing_tender
      # Check if the tender has been modified since our last record
      last_modified = DateTime.parse(existing_tender.date_modified)
      current_modified = DateTime.parse(tender_data['dateModified'])

        puts "Updated tender #{tender_data['id']}"
      else

      end

    end

require 'sqlite3'
require 'json'

class TenderDB
  def initialize(db_file: ENV['DB_FILE'] || 'tenders.db')
    @db = SQLite3::Database.new(db_file)
    create_tables
  end

  def create_tables
    @db.execute <<-SQL
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tenders (
        id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        date_signed INTEGER,
        tender_id TEXT,
        title TEXT,
        procurement_method TEXT,
        status TEXT,
        value_amount REAL,
        currency TEXT,
        date_modified INTEGER,
        created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
      );
    SQL
  end

  def save_tender(tender_data)
    existing = @db.execute("SELECT 1 FROM tenders WHERE id = ?", [tender_data['id']]).first
    return if existing

    @db.execute <<-SQL, [
      tender_data['id'],
      tender_data['dateSigned'] ? tender_data['dateSigned'] : nil,
      tender_data['tenderID'],
      tender_data['title'],
      tender_data['procurementMethod'],
      tender_data['status'],
      tender_data['value'] && tender_data['value']['amount'] ? tender_data['value']['amount'] : nil,
      tender_data['value'] && tender_data['value']['currency'] ? tender_data['value']['currency'] : nil,
      tender_data['dateModified'] ? tender_data['dateModified'] : nil
    ]
      INSERT INTO tenders (id, date_signed, tender_id, title, procurement_method, status, value_amount, currency, date_modified)
      VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
    SQL
  end

  def get_tenders_since(date)
    @db.execute <<-SQL, [date]
      SELECT * FROM tenders WHERE date_modified >= ?
    SQL
  end

  def close
    @db.close
  end
end
```

### 3. `tender_search.rb` - Main application

```ruby
require 'httparty'
require 'json'
require 'dotenv/load'
require_relative 'tender_db'

class ProzorroTenderSearch
  include HTTParty
  base_uri ENV['PROZORRO_API_URL']

  def initialize
    @db = TenderDB.new
    @api_key = ENV['API_KEY']
  end

  def search_tenders(opts = {})
    headers = {
      'Accept' => 'application/json',
      'Content-Type' => 'application/json'
    }

    if @api_key
      headers['Authorization'] = "Bearer #{@api_key}"
    end

    response = self.class.get('/tenders', query: opts, headers: headers)

    if response.success?
      response.parsed_response
    else
      raise "API request failed: #{response.code} #{response.message}"
    end
  end

  def fetch_new_tenders(limit = 100, since: nil)
    opts = {
      'limit' => limit,
      'opt_fields' => 'tenderID,title,procurementMethod,status,value.dateModified,dateModified,dateSigned'
    }

    opts['offset'] = since if since

    response = search_tenders(opts)

    if response.is_a?(Hash) && response['data']
      response['data'].each do |tender|
        @db.save_tender(tender)
      end
      response['data']
    else
      []
    end
  end

  end
end

end

Ця реалізація забезпечує базовий рівень захисту для чутливих персональних даних в ActiveRecord.

Для перевірки кваліфікованого електронного підпису (КЕП) на файлі, підписаному за українським алгоритмом ДСТУ 4145, ми можемо використовувати Ruby-бібліотеку `openssl`, яка надає можливості для роботи з криптографією, та додаткові геми для роботи з форматами підписів.

Ось код для цього завдання:

### 1. Gemfile
```ruby
# Gemfile
source 'https://rubygems.org'

# Для роботи з OpenSSL
gem 'openssl'

# Для роботи з форматами підписів (наприклад, CAdES, PAdES, XAdES)
# Геми, які можуть бути корисними:
# gem 'xmldsig'
# gem 'nokogiri' # Для парсингу XML
# gem 'asice'
# gem 'asicschema'

# Якщо потрібно працювати з EPS (Електронні підписи України)
# gem 'eps'
```

Виконання `bundle install` встановить потрібні геми.

### 2. Реалізація перевірки підпису
```ruby
# require 'openssl'
require 'nokogiri'
require 'base64'

# Метод для перевірки підпису за алгоритмом ДСТУ 4145
def verify_dstu4145_signature(signed_file_path, signature_file_path, certificate_file_path)
  # Зчитуємо підписаний файл
  signed_file = File.read(signed_file_path)
  signature = File.read(signature_file_path)

  # Зчитуємо сертифікат для перевірки
  cert = OpenSSL::X509::Certificate.new(File.read(certificate_file_path))
  key = OpenSSL::PKey::EC.new(File.read(certificate_file_path)) # Для ДСТУ 4145 використовується EC

  # Перевіряємо підпис
  begin
    # Для ДСТУ 4145 перевірка може потребувати спеціального алгоритму
    # Тут наведено загальний підхід, який може потребувати адаптації
    digest = OpenSSL::Digest.new('SHA256') # або інший хеш, який використовується
    verifier = OpenSSL::PKey::EC.new(key.public_key)
    verifier.digest_algorithm = digest

    # Розшифровуємо підпис (залежно від формату)
    decoded_signature = Base64.decode64(signature)

    verifier.verify(digest, signed_file, decoded_signature)
  rescue OpenSSL::PKey::EC::Error => e
    puts "Помилка перевірки підпису: #{e.message}"
    return false
  end
end

# Приклад використання
if __FILE__ == $0
  signed_file = 'path/to/signed_file'
  signature_file = 'path/to/signature_file'
  certificate_file = 'path/to/certificate_file'

  if verify_dstu4145_signature(signed_file, signature_file, certificate_file)
    puts "Підпис КЕП валідний."
  else
    puts "Підпис КЕП невалідний або підпис не перевірено."
  end
end
```

### Примітки:
1. **Алгоритм ДСТУ 4145** використовує еліптичну криптографію (ECC), тому ми використовуємо `OpenSSL::PKey::EC`.
2. **Формат підпису** може бути різним (CAdES, PAdES, XAdES), тому може знадобитися додаткова обробка.
3. **Сертифікат** повинен мати правильний формат (DER або PEM) і містити відкритий ключ для перевірки.
4. Для повної підтримки українських стандартів може знадобитися спеціалізована бібліотека, наприклад, `eps` (Electronic Payment Systems) або `asice` (для роботи з ASiC-контейнерами).

Якщо потрібна більш точна реалізація з урахуванням конкретного формату підпису, надайте більше інформації про структуру файлу підпису.

## Gemfile

source 'https://rubygems.org'

## Implementation

```ruby
require 'sinatra'
require 'httparty'
require 'json'
require 'dotenv/load'

# Load environment variables from .env file
Dotenv.load

# Configuration
DIASHERING_API_URL = 'https://api.diashering.gov.ua/v1'
CLIENT_ID = ENV['DIASHERING_CLIENT_ID']
CLIENT_SECRET = ENV['DIASHERING_CLIENT_SECRET']
REDIRECT_URI = ENV['DIASHERING_REDIRECT_URI']
SCOPE = 'document'

# Initialize HTTParty for API requests
class DiaSheringAPI
  include HTTParty
  base_uri DIASHERING_API_URL

  def initialize
    @auth_token = nil
  end

  # Get authorization URL for user to authenticate
  def auth_url(state = nil)
    params = {
      response_type: 'code',
      client_id: CLIENT_ID,
      redirect_uri: REDIRECT_URI,
      scope: SCOPE,
      state: state
    }
    "#{base_uri}/oauth/authorize?#{params.to_query}"
  end

  # Exchange authorization code for access token
  def get_token(auth_code)
    response = self.class.post('/oauth/token', {
      body: {
        grant_type: 'authorization_code',
        code: auth_code,
        redirect_uri: REDIRECT_URI,
        client_id: CLIENT_ID,
        client_secret: CLIENT_SECRET
      },
      headers: { 'Content-Type' => 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded' }
    })

    if response.success?
      @auth_token = JSON.parse(response.body)['access_token']
    else
      raise "Failed to get token: #{response.body}"
    end
  end

  # Get user documents
  def get_documents
    return [] unless @auth_token

    response = self.class.get('/documents', {
      headers: {
        'Authorization' => "Bearer #{@auth_token}",
        'Content-Type' => 'application/json'
      }
